name: Congressman Jim Jordan
subject: Save the date — I'll be in NC-14
body:
Peter,I don't get to North Carolina as often as I'd like -- but when Tim Moore asked me to come stand with him in Gaston County, there was no way I was saying no.Tim and I serve together in the House, and I've seen firsthand how hard he fights for hardworking families in western North Carolina. He doesn't grandstand. He doesn't chase headlines. He just shows up and gets the job done -- on fiscal responsibility, on cutting red tape, on standing firm against the kind of reckless spending that's bankrupting this country.That's why I'm asking you to join us: [](https://timmoore.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fatudk-hkhielhuy-r/) **An Evening with Congressman Jim Jordan & Congressman Tim Moore**
Friday, July 31st | 5:00 PM
Gaston Country Club
3700 County Club Drive
Gastonia, NC [CLICK HERE TO RSVP AND MAKE YOUR DONATION NOW](https://timmoore.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fatudk-hkhielhuy-y/) This is a grassroots event -- and I hope you'll stand with us to hold the line for NC-14. I want a room full of people who know what's at stake this November and are ready to help Tim keep representing our values the right way.**Reserve your spot today** by replying to this email, or contacting Tara Mingledorff at [**RSVP@CastlebarStrategies.com**](mailto:RSVP@CastlebarStrategies.com).I hope to see you there.In the fight, Rep. Jim Jordan (OH-04)_If you're unable to attend but would still like to support Congressman Moore's efforts, contributions may be mailed to:**Moore Victory Committee, PO Box 97275, Raleigh, NC 27624**_ Paid for by Moore Victory Committee, a joint fundraising committee authorized by and composed of Friends of Tim Moore, NC2DC Leadership PAC, and NRCC.
PO Box 97275 Raleigh, NC 27624. | [Unsubscribe](https://timmoore.cmail19.com/t/y-u-fatudk-hkhielhuy-t/)
---

A deep dive into Colorado's dirty voter roll
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**July 13, 2026** **MONDAY NEWS DIGEST**
| | Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,
Over the past several weeks, we've published one of the most extensive investigations Rocky Mountain Voice has ever undertaken.
Using Colorado's publicly available voter roll, state statutes, election records and other publicly available data, guest columnist Mike O'Donnell has spent months examining one fundamental question: **_**How accurate is Colorado's voter roll, and are there vulnerabilities that deserve closer scrutiny?**_**
The investigation has followed the _**entire life cycle of a ballot.**_
It began by examining how voters are added to Colorado's rolls through [automatic registration](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) before exploring whether [outdated registrations](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) are removed as efficiently as they're added. From there, the series looked at [Colorado's participation in ERIC](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), ballots mailed to []()out-of-state and international addresses, [chain-of-custody procedures](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) after ballots leave the Postal Service, and examples the author says appear to show [duplicate voter registrations](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) created through differences in identifying information.
This week's sixth installment goes a step further, examining Colorado's citizenship verification process, why the author believes outside review of voter eligibility is limited, and an [unusual pattern uncovered at a single Aurora apartment](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) where 104 voter registrants became associated with what appears to be a one-bedroom unit over a two-year period. O'Donnell notes that none of those registrants currently have active status, that only one of the 104 ever cast a ballot according to voter history records, and argues the case illustrates why stronger front-end safeguards and address verification may be needed.
Throughout the series, we've encouraged readers to do what good journalism asks of all of us: _**examine the evidence, read the source material, and think critically.**_ Whether you agree with every conclusion or not, transparency builds trust—and trust in our elections depends on a willingness to ask difficult questions and openly examine the systems that underpin them.
This week, the seventh and final installment will conclude the investigation, bringing together the author's findings and recommendations after months of reviewing Colorado's voter registration system.
_**Catch up on the entire series so far below:**_
1️⃣ [Getting on is the easy part](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) 2️⃣ [Getting off isn’t so easy](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
3️⃣ [Where the ballots go](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
4️⃣ [Following the ballot](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
5️⃣ [When one registration becomes two](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) 6️⃣ [The curious case of Apartment A503](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Whether this series reinforces your existing views or challenges them, we believe it's worth reading in full. An informed citizenry is the foundation of self-government.
Thank you for reading, asking questions, and staying engaged.
In truth & liberty,
Team RMV

**[No way out: Rural Colorado is outvoted at every turn](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Tom Harrington manages a 500-cow operation on the Crystal River Ranch, two miles from the town of Carbondale on a mesa west of town. He grew up in Ridgway. A friend sent him some papers from the North Park area of Walden showing the school news, a note from the old folks’ home and local ads.
**[Colorado’s dirty voter roll: Where the ballots go](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY MIKE O'DONNELL, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Getting on and getting off the voter rolls were the first two questions. In Part 3, Mike O’Donnell turns to where Colorado voter data and ballots go next—through ERIC, out-of-state mailing addresses and overseas voting rules he argues deserve closer scrutiny.
**[Colorado’s dirty voter roll: Following the ballot](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY MIKE O'DONNELL, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Colorado relies on the U.S. Postal Service to deliver millions of ballots, but the mail carrier isn't always the last person to handle them. In Part 4, Mike O'Donnell examines Colorado's chain of custody—from group homes and shelters to commercial mail locations, drop boxes and ballot harvesting.
|
---
**STATE**
**[Pickens Technical College signed a disability agreement. Then dismissed the student.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Some mornings, she didn’t know how she got to where she was. A Colorado Springs woman who asked to remain anonymous — referred to here as CSW — had been an EMT for more than a decade, a career she began while volunteering with a fire department. She shared dozens of emails documenting her case with RMV.
**[Children’s Hospital Colorado insurance data tells one story—its testimony another.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY KELLY NOTARFRANCESCO, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Hundreds of children were provided puberty blockers or cross-sex hormones by Children’s Hospital Colorado’s TRUE Center for Gender Diversity annually in 2024 and 2025 — in numbers that may be more than 35 times higher than those previously reported in 2024 by medical watchdog group Do No Harm.
__
**[Colorado immediately assessed Trump’s election order. USPS defended its proposal. A court blocked key parts.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Colorado election officials said they diverted staff to evaluate President Trump's executive order while 2026 preparations were already underway. USPS said the proposal formalizes election-mail practices it has recommended for years. The dispute has now moved to the appeals courts.

**LOCAL**
**[Federal lawsuit says Denver school board used race to draw voting districts](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) A conservative election-law firm filed a federal lawsuit against the Denver Public Schools Board of Education on July 2, arguing the board deliberately drew its school district voting map along racial lines. The board’s own words, the suit says, prove it.
__
**[Colorado College Awards Credit for Progressive Activism Internships](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COMPLETE COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Colorado College is putting a price tag on political activism — or rather, waiving it for its own students — by offering academic credit to undergraduates who spend the summer, among other offerings, working to “shut down immigration detention centers.”

**[Why capitalism and the Constitution still offer America’s best path](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RUSS MINARY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _“From each according to his abilities, to each according to his needs.” – Karl Marx. Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels published “The Communist Manifesto” in 1848. The popular quote above appeared in Marx’s “Critique of the Gotha Programme” written 1875. This article will examine how that idealistic worldview has – or has not – worked out in reality. Spoiler alert: it hasn’t._
____
**[Should America reserve its highest offices for natural-born citizens?](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY CHRISTINE COLEMAN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _When God brought the children of Israel into the Promised Land, He established clear laws and commandments for their governance. Among them was the explicit requirement that rulers must be chosen from among their own people — no foreigner born outside the nation was permitted to rule over God’s covenant people._
__
**[The American Dream is slipping away and socialism is filling the gap](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[AMERICAN THINKER](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Not long ago, the American Dream followed a familiar script. Graduate from school, find a job, buy a modest home, start a family, and gradually build a better life than the generation before you._

**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[THE FEDERALIST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) A week before the 250th anniversary of America declaring independence, more than 1,000 people assembled at the nation’s capital to make a declaration of their own: their vision to dismantle America’s founding institutions. “All of US Next250 National Mobilization” protested the Trump administration, debuted new “founding documents,” and re-envisioned America as seen by Marxist revolutionaries.

" President Trump on [March 31] stepped up efforts to promote his false claims of widespread voting fraud, signing an executive order of questionable constitutionality seeking to create a national list of citizens that would determine voting eligibility and restrict mail ballots. "
Let's be clear: The president has no explicit Constitutional authority over elections, and much of this latest attack on our fundamental right to vote appears difficult to enforce and legally dubious.
This order directs the Department of Homeland Security to create a “ state citizenship list ” based on data from various federal databases. It also directs federal officials to send that made-up list to state election officials, and orders the attorney general to prioritize prosecution of election officials who provide ballots to voters not on the made-up list. It also directs the U.S. Postal Service not to transmit mail-in ballots from any individual not included on Trump's “ state citizenship list ," even though elections are mandated by the constitutional the be run by the states.
This order is yet another sign that the MAGA crew will do anything they can to codify their power permanently and silence the will of the people by suppressing and eliminating the votes we cast.

name: Fran Hong
subject: Not my first rodeo
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
Let’s talk about experience
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260713-3029)
Peter,
I spend a lot of time talking about Wisconsin's future. Today, I'd like to tell you a little more about my past.
Since being elected to the Wisconsin Legislature in 2020, I've authored dozens of bills to make life better for working-class families.
I've led the fight for a moratorium on AI data centers, andI've introduced legislation to lower utility bills, provide healthy school meals for every child, and establish universal paid leave. I’ve also pushed to tax the ultra-wealthy so working families can finally catch a break, and fought to protect Wisconsin from ICE.
One of the things I'm proudest of is working across the aisle with Republicans to successfully pass bipartisan legislation that had to do with diversity, equity, inclusion AND education (can you even imagine?).
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260713.sCLbJC&refcode=em20260713-3029&t=1&akid=3029%2E105371%2EMhjAUp)
Experiences like this remind me that even in today's political climate, it's still possible to find common ground when you stay focused on solving problems instead of scoring political points.
Long before I was elected, I was serving my community in a different way.
As a chef and small business owner, I learned how to lead under pressure, stretch every dollar, and bring people together around a common table. I co-founded two nonprofits to feed neighbors facing food insecurity while supporting restaurant workers through some of the hardest moments our communities have faced.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260713.sCLbJC&refcode=em20260713-3029&t=2&akid=3029%2E105371%2EMhjAUp)
Those experiences shaped the kind of leader I am today.
I've led a kitchen as executive chef, and now I'm running to lead Wisconsin's executive branch. I can handle the heat, I'm ready on day one. As governor, I'll lead the same way I always have, with transparency and constant communication with all the invested parties. I'll uplift the voices of those closest to the problems so we can find the best solutions. I'll find common ground with my colleagues in the legislature.
**[If you believe Wisconsin deserves a governor with a proven record of fighting for working people, I hope you'll help power this campaign today.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260713.sCLbJC&refcode=em20260713-3029&t=3&akid=3029%2E105371%2EMhjAUp)**
**[Please chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can to help us win](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260713.sCLbJC&refcode=em20260713-3029&t=4&akid=3029%2E105371%2EMhjAUp). **
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260713.sCLbJC&refcode=em20260713-3029&t=5&akid=3029%2E105371%2EMhjAUp)
From the bottom of my heart, I want to thank you for being in this fight with us. We make better possible.
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260713.sCLbJC&amount=5&refcode=em20260713-3029&t=8&akid=3029%2E105371%2EMhjAUp)**
With gratitude,
Francesca Hong
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260713-3029&t=9&refcode2=3029_105371_MhjAUp&akid=3029%2E105371%2EMhjAUp)**

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is one of the most powerful tools that grassroots campaigns like ours have to reach everyday people across Wisconsin and beyond, so thank you for reading to the end.
The more people who engage with our emails, the more likely we’ll go straight to your inbox. For a free and easy way to help our campaign, please [click this link to our website](https://francescahong.com/) after you finish reading our emails.

Peter,

**My son, who was a U.S. Marine and father of two, was murdered in 2016 when he was just 28 years old.**

[**This is a longer email, but I humbly ask you to read it and consider joining my team at the end.**](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=308039bb075e42ce9839e9dbbb0bf673&_e=LM6va6pqZ7M_fcwqO8TWt4OkYLpfSYozIxx9JCUBDaj5SWfctXrt8z_F15TOwAQ_ra5RUUlfpQFUtSwB4_ehB5bI1mO4Er5h-tiFccHhQ6lLRrX7-qUY_xpO8ONif1PBxIR0jH-itA_fcuVhsThB1he9Gtp-mZ1AB12tZc3mx03c_P81or74NSwWgROkVLk1TqNLq1FlrTzqZWgGytI2X-FZD10QB7tG7sRbKtqQgXXoXAS7QJAWBU28kOJIlENh7kGQtcAgnFaTLUhN2x5xus2VfOcWSSdHFa1gHbugrnbrmECMJRsG_t3BH-L7zbPfnp9bQunQUUmPSCsKq8Pn1R9VuSn8aoCDHiDmCFqpLybvI1f_CtobjRMMjWq8AWQ7EsGUP4yRoCn7PLQKtIV8Jbc6AwyBokifX0K6luwb6NfuUqQ7nHuFQXtzsUAKS3CRUzeOb0_5L32-aZ8OvGN9TP3efIzWTYsgPSX4i9KXT03uImnCZWj9pKfoZBPUWd8fJXypuZF5VGiWinFa9t7MkJb-9aamYGYN4jMhaaXfF44%3D)

**In case you don 't know me, my name is Joe Males, and I'm a proud Mexican-American, U.S. Marine Veteran, small business owner, and a city councilman who's running for Congress in CA-25. But above all else, I'm a father who is still in mourning.**

[](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=308039bb075e42ce9839e9dbbb0bf673&_e=LM6va6pqZ7M_fcwqO8TWt4OkYLpfSYozIxx9JCUBDaj5SWfctXrt8z_F15TOwAQ_ra5RUUlfpQFUtSwB4_ehB5bI1mO4Er5h-tiFccHhQ6lLRrX7-qUY_xpO8ONif1PBxIR0jH-itA_fcuVhsThB1he9Gtp-mZ1AB12tZc3mx03c_P81or74NSwWgROkVLk1VHkN2K400buT6M4crbG4J9q2H4dXhaw3GDpZe79stGlnKbmNwZp4C1dlp2lHGRs_I_aryIzeSDdI8garsaAzI7qFlnr_MR_hUBSCEqfMNHEGvS0sloJo-3Kb2WyavRDxUQGPZ002huRbjIElSSgFHUjpVJ8xk3VPWuNgVPrDlh9xQY_5SxI_0nJt2yxpBJucYhfnBSa2oS3Moqhp11-tj96PnqjY_IdCnPy0QafnBSfmqDRxQ3WfyZaT4vnaeYu88ZL3XsEUYtsivHs_CJXm4Ur7qJr7icbXKPoGuMQeqvM4yMyWeIJEz0vC0MCjzM-qbncn3qYiZP-SZpsstzDKLhsc9N93S9nMUe4nRaNgvfg%3D)
**I ran for city council and am running for Congress because of my son, Nicholas.**

In 2016, Nicholas came home to visit for his sister's birthday and Father's Day. It was supposed to be a wonderful time to bring our family back together. Then, he was tragically stabbed to death in my hometown of Hemet, California.

[](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=308039bb075e42ce9839e9dbbb0bf673&_e=LM6va6pqZ7M_fcwqO8TWt4OkYLpfSYozIxx9JCUBDaj5SWfctXrt8z_F15TOwAQ_ra5RUUlfpQFUtSwB4_ehB5bI1mO4Er5h-tiFccHhQ6lLRrX7-qUY_xpO8ONif1PBxIR0jH-itA_fcuVhsThB1he9Gtp-mZ1AB12tZc3mx03c_P81or74NSwWgROkVLk1r28Xx8xfURIXy2xDomgvbdNo4QFWaQiR6x0N74jDKBod435zIuVeFkZF8KytADVCGThuWudUHOjD6Ay2HbSFJdJipnTiv1K-BrH39-6zzj-cqkgWpdaY-lEBFZYq8JtUDvKwKV2rxlC4okBkPY1FedrZeftoX8W_FBKzMZasplhXd9YgjL-wUORTCivVHM6ZM4M4GmaXk_VPA3FoqS_eSfpN3eD9WMLUE4fslIGX1xcn5v-HnVveE1m3aYbp8tlLR5EK-v9U8spnT_E8LUoK8DyW3zKY3Z6XhPsx1t05-w4ta_evV22eAgjJ7gw_x8X51ba_FYFgp-enrtorV7TwOdn7-QfrIQP7XNpq96xoL38%3D)
No one stepped forward with information on my son's killer, so the case went cold. After five years of not knowing anything about what happened, I decided to do something about it. I ran for City Council, and just a few months later, by the grace of God, they found the killer.

As a parent, losing your child is the most difficult thing to go through. But I'm pushing through it and am committed to making him proud as I fight for a better tomorrow for his children.

I'm grateful to Hemet's law enforcement, who was able to find the killer and arrest him.

Nicholas serves as a daily reminder to me to never take a single precious moment for granted and that I must continue to fight every single day for a better future.

[**Now, I’m running for United States Congress to FLIP California’s 25th district RED.**](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=308039bb075e42ce9839e9dbbb0bf673&_e=LM6va6pqZ7M_fcwqO8TWt4OkYLpfSYozIxx9JCUBDaj5SWfctXrt8z_F15TOwAQ_ra5RUUlfpQFUtSwB4_ehB5bI1mO4Er5h-tiFccHhQ6lLRrX7-qUY_xpO8ONif1PBxIR0jH-itA_fcuVhsThB1he9Gtp-mZ1AB12tZc3mx03c_P81or74NSwWgROkVLk1W2aK0jqFkBq7Ctldp7X4eR-4cnJ3tGB1FvQ-7Vp6usHfgKp69CotM8jLjW7HKR52jHqg0GVtBnoGirWte1_FRC4VdV_2cCRdjDVbLYupPBNohvTf5X7FRXfjFeHUoNM8CDYNcR-Ez5q5LFMf1v2wZk3pZ_-jyxJV-qBW1WnGqM-Kqh8kGR6tasVHEgcA8CIk3DXGgUV_aFwKnk-O6sXCraFOBqBwuBi4krQfxwYkPeZQKSH7mM5CXkZpujjoGngXD6dPvQhnV-L9m7A1DK2M-rT-MfQ9uc_51lbqLbkFclH8gB6Eqr1oz6c1i80hp66SGp0VgeDD9A7QrDkoFOK_aB1_wYE6hxjp4MnzzMcoTDc%3D) As a border district, my community feels the pain of Biden's failed open border policies every day. I'm grateful to President Trump for the work he's already done to secure our border, and I'm hopeful to win my election in 2026 so I can FIGHT, FIGHT, FIGHT alongside him.

[](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=308039bb075e42ce9839e9dbbb0bf673&_e=LM6va6pqZ7M_fcwqO8TWt4OkYLpfSYozIxx9JCUBDaj5SWfctXrt8z_F15TOwAQ_ra5RUUlfpQFUtSwB4_ehB5bI1mO4Er5h-tiFccHhQ6lLRrX7-qUY_xpO8ONif1PBxIR0jH-itA_fcuVhsThB1he9Gtp-mZ1AB12tZc3mx03c_P81or74NSwWgROkVLk1ZvvliqMjPc28bGWsgk9_eouJdQleFlDKUyi2gHJYqbZJhYqJtI8IlAh5j2ROpxr9mmNFNlXlrvsEZu7Z4PMu-D_kiEyliXw4lrhsi4ovqAq8eNfbnh1kQiyK4pgpAP3XaQo7g2kUbnjJe_KZsyH9Cu5DktBCXa6AGJr7pspnXit1lbm-ZHqMQMrRo-NvTI7sN7Q0P5OQ62K4pt8tCM9KDqXns2QrhGHOGygw3Z7Q3nkOJqlwGnyWMRDGPm3ozvHTHKfS9zPB4pfsEvMlF7p7_qAmz3OS49YP88ebnTMsJ3Alfz8G46OgEYOVZNq-0-z5UkZZ_I7BqAVhx3WOr8soupmtRVuRpp6KFlVduZqc1Sg%3D)
**But as you know, California is DEEPLY blue.** _Nancy Pelosi, Gavin Newsom, and Adam Schiff have deep roots in our state 's politics, and they'll do anything to prevent a Hispanic Marine Corps Veteran from going to Congress, all because I'm a proud Republican._

**They have millions and millions of dollars already built up, ready to spend to keep California blue.** But my neighbors and I know their leadership has FAILED Californians and Americans.

[**I’m humbly asking you to send my campaign a donation of whatever you can afford.**](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=308039bb075e42ce9839e9dbbb0bf673&_e=LM6va6pqZ7M_fcwqO8TWt4OkYLpfSYozIxx9JCUBDaj5SWfctXrt8z_F15TOwAQ_ra5RUUlfpQFUtSwB4_ehB5bI1mO4Er5h-tiFccHhQ6lLRrX7-qUY_xpO8ONif1PBxIR0jH-itA_fcuVhsThB1he9Gtp-mZ1AB12tZc3mx03c_P81or74NSwWgROkVLk1mYum_h62CClwZEJtJw10e2LWr8VTOCjWOGfLmIMx0yRYdTtus2c1JTWQEFrzhtMAhhOyqsNZcY3HlC3zfFsKu3yR0Cn2Le7FeomG4i-H9Nyx-JoaTiGLXg8Qo-5b4qQ7RzHJGTmZAcdPwDcn9h3ok-BA5biK-ZEQoJPsMSJXEifRo1jq1XSHGLC9hRJ9czPR9Xbve0fD0bZj6fmd1nI6GS8P6Vx3NBeuQAtYjxTyU4nyCmkZ7SZqdnFBbCzsmg0eT_M3DUIH-JfZfq_7-KZzsxjk-GDAWLztIHO14CzutrDePfI3FS0wAzDkn8ngspyMaNBGWZef3R5dr3KDpQnqI0269HuO1rlv_3fkETZACZM%3D) I vow to make your donation count and to help President Trump usher in the Golden Age of America. name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: New Mexico Just Got Ranked Dead Last.
body:
Plus: Graham gone at 71, and a two-week scramble for his seat | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/SFEAjQoNV5E?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |

A new study just ranked New Mexico the number one worst state in America to move to, and the categories they graded us on are everything we talk about on this show every week. [And we woke up to surprising news this weekend](https://us.list-manage.com/1BCTYZbgv0v?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e): Lindsey Graham passed away Saturday night at 71. Whatever you thought of him, he was a giant, and we play the one clip from his career that everybody should see.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/I6ISJ6MAJeJ?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
🔥 **NEW MEXICO RANKED THE WORST STATE TO MOVE TO. THEN A SECOND LIST MADE IT WORSE.**

The first study grades safety, healthcare, education, the stuff that actually matters. We come in last. Fine. We know we've got problems, and we talk about the fix.
The second list is where Mark lost it. CNBC put out their "worst states to live" rankings, and when he read what they based Tennessee on out loud, Krysty just started laughing. Every state on their list has one thing in common, and it's got nothing to do with jobs, safety, or schools.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/3QslnKh0HD2?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
🇺🇸 **LINDSEY GRAHAM GONE AT 71, AND THE CLIP EVERY STATION SHOULD BE PLAYING**
Lindsey Graham was booked on Meet the Press Sunday morning. He passed away Saturday night at 71. We play the Kavanaugh hearing moment we think was the best of his entire career. If you've never seen it, watch the episode just for that.
Then the politics kick in fast. Anyone who wants his Senate seat has two weeks to file. Two weeks! And there's one name that could blow the whole race open.
🦬 **A BISON LAUNCHES GRANDPA 8 FEET, AND OUR MOUNTAIN LION IS DOING LAPS**
You have to see this Yellowstone video. A bull bison sends a grandfather flying 8 feet, and the poor guy did absolutely nothing wrong. Watch what actually sets it off. Then our trail cams caught our mountain lion again. Twice in two hours. Krysty has officially retired from hiking that trail.
---
| [WATCH NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/P0nK8jqOsjP?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
🏔️ **THE MARK VS. THE MOUNTAIN SEASON FINALE IS THIS THURSDAY**
A year of fighting that mountain comes down to one episode. The reveal drops this Thursday on Amazon Prime Video, and we really love how it turned out.
Need to catch up first? Pure Flix is 99 cents this month. Just search "Mark vs. The Mountain" on Prime Video. Every view helps us grow the show and bring season two home to New Mexico.

|
---
| |

**🎟️ WE'RE EMCEEING THE**[**STATESMAN DINNER JULY 25**](https://us.list-manage.com/OrDqXVb0QPB?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)**\- RSVP NOW**

Come see us in person! We're hosting the Republican Party of New Mexico's biggest night of the year — a black-tie dinner celebrating America's 250th, Saturday, July 25 at Isleta Resort & Casino.
You'll hear from gubernatorial nominee Gregg Hull, plus a keynote from Nick Shirley, the independent journalist whose undercover investigations have been making national news all year. It's going to be a fun night, and we'd love to see you there.

Our campaign is fighting to end all US military aid to Israel and to stop all weapons and tech for genocide and imperialist wars. We are fighting to shut down ICE and the detention centers. We are fighting to stop the data centers and AI-related mass layoffs. We are fighting to stop the climate catastrophe by taking big energy corporations into democratic public ownership of workers, so we can make a lightning-fast transition to clean energy and end the use of fossil fuels.
There is massive anger among the working class at Trump's deportation machine and the horrific bloodshed in the Middle East driven by both parties. The AI boom has also left many working people concerned about their jobs, their living conditions, and the sustainability of the planet due to the extreme amounts of energy consumed by data centers and the deregulated fossil fuel industry. All of this is leading us towards a complete disaster of epic proportions.
We urgently need to fight back and Kshama's campaign is the most important spearhead in that fight right now. Kshama has a long track record of leading movements to beat the billionaires, like when she defeated Jeff Bezos to win the Amazon Tax. She also defeated the corporate landlords, including billionaire Trump-donor Martin Selig, to win unprecedented renters rights. We need a proven working class fighter like Kshama in Congress to go to war against the political establishment to fight for free healthcare for all funded by taxing the rich, national rent control, and an end to all military aid to Israel.
If you agree with these demands and you are in, or near, Seattle, join our campaign at our rally to elect Kshama on July 18th at 11am at Pratt Park. If we can get Kshama into the general election, that would be a massive leap forward for the antiwar movement, for the fight for universal public healthcare, and for working class fightback in the labor movement.
Our campaign is by far the most threatening one in decades to the Democratic and Republican parties, and the entire billionaire class which backs them. body:
We're hitting the road to speak with Texas voters about the threats data centers pose to our water and our health| | | |
---
| | | Peter, since I launched my campaign for Texas Lt. Governor last year, I've been speaking about how important it is to protect our most valuable natural resource - Water. Lately, this issue has been thrust into the headlines. We see how rampant commercial developments, such as data centers and crypto-mining operations, have been consuming vast amounts of water. Let me say it plainly: Our communities deserve real transparency and accountability from facilities that already exist or are under construction. **We must have a moratorium on new data center construction** until we can pass comprehensive legislation that puts the resource use of people and animals before the resource use of these massive facilities. On Tuesday, July 14th, I'm kicking off a tour to hear from people across the state. Starting with a press conference in Austin (which you can watch live online) and continuing with a tour of the South Plains region - currently on the front lines of data center development. Here are the details:
---
| | | **DATA CENTER ACCOUNTABILITY PRESS CONFERENCE**
---
| | | **When:** Tuesday, July 14th@ 10am
---

clean_body: We're hitting the road to speak with Texas voters about the threats data centers pose to our water and our health| | | | | | | Peter, since I launched my campaign for Texas Lt. Governor last year, I've been speaking about how important it is to protect our most valuable natural resource - Water. Lately, this issue has been thrust into the headlines. We see how rampant commercial developments, such as data centers and crypto-mining operations, have been consuming vast amounts of water. Let me say it plainly: Our communities deserve real transparency and accountability from facilities that already exist or are under construction. We must have a moratorium on new data center construction until we can pass comprehensive legislation that puts the resource use of people and animals before the resource use of these massive facilities. On Tuesday, July 14th, I'm kicking off a tour to hear from people across the state. Starting with a press conference in Austin (which you can watch live online) and continuing with a tour of the South Plains region - currently on the front lines of data center development. Here are the details: | | | DATA CENTER ACCOUNTABILITY PRESS CONFERENCE | | | When: Tuesday, July 14th@ 10am | | | | | Below is a list of the cities we'll be visiting in the next week for Town Hall-style meetings. I'll be joined on the road by several of my fellow candidates who share my concerns. name: Data Center Awareness
subject: Five Communities. One Warning.
body:
Across Pennsylvania, people are sounding the alarm about data centers. Josh Shapiro isn't listening.

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| | | | | | Hey Peter -
Over the past month, Stacy Garrity has traveled across Pennsylvania meeting with residents, township officials, county leaders, and community members concerned about massive data center developments coming to their neighborhoods.
She didn’t give a speech.
She went to listen.
And no matter where she went - From Wilkes-Barre to the Philadelphia suburbs to Cranberry Township - the concerns were strikingly similar.
Families are worried about soaring electricity demand.
Communities are worried about their water supply.
Residents are worried about industrial-scale facilities being built next to homes and farms.
Local officials are worried they’ll be left to deal with the consequences while decisions are made hundreds of miles away in Harrisburg.
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | While Pennsylvanians have been raising these concerns, Josh Shapiro has been doing what he always does: changing his position whenever it’s politically convenient.
Just months ago, Shapiro was celebrating massive data center projects and touting Pennsylvania as a leader in attracting them.
Now, after public opposition has grown across the Commonwealth, he’s trying to rewrite history.
The people Stacy has met aren’t asking for politicians to score political points.
They’re asking to be heard.
They’re asking honest questions about what these massive developments could mean for their communities, their quality of life, and their future.
That’s exactly why Stacy has spend the past month meeting directly with people who will have to live with the consequences, not hiding behind press releases or changing her position when the political winds shift.
Take a few minutes to read about the conversations that happened across Pennsylvania:

The fight to keep Virginia's 5th District Republican and America First is on right now. Unfortunately, most people do not know we have a primary vote going on right now so please spread the word. Early voting is underway, and the Republican primary deadline of August 4 is fast approaching, I'm reaching out personally to ask for your vote today.
We must defend our conservative principles and send a proven fighter back to Washington, not someone who talks the talk, but a battle-tested conservative who delivers real results.
As a Navy SEAL veteran, husband, father of five, and your Congressman with prior service in the Virginia General Assembly, I've stood firm for conservative values while getting things done for our district. I was the first incumbent in the nation endorsed by President Trump for re-election this cycle.
Here's what we've accomplished together:

* Delivered real results for constituents: In just 18 months, my incredible team and I returned nearly $10 million back into the pockets of 5th District families and businesses, money the federal government owed them.
* Secured community funding: Congress approved 18 out of 18 of my community project requests this appropriations cycle, including a new fire truck for Louisa County and renovations for the Nottoway County Sheriff's Office.
* Passed long-stalled legislation: Recently passed two bills out of the House in just three weeks, including the Wintergreen emergency egress bill, a 25-year fight that six previous Members of Congress couldn't finish.
* Working to help Liberty University get a Navy ROTC Program
* Helped 57 constituents from The Point Church get home during ballistic missile attacks in Israel
* Helped President Trump with language for his counter drone executive order
* Connected with thousands of constituents through 5 tele-town halls
* Earned top conservative credentials:
* Club for Growth's top conservatism award
* Champion of Limited Government top conservatism award from the Institute for Legislative Analysis
* CPAC's top conservatism award, Award for Conservative Excellence
* 100% score from the Family Research Council (FRC)
* 100% score from the Heritage Foundation
* Endorsed by the NRA and Tyler Yzaguirre, President of the Second Amendment Institute

In the General Assembly, my team and I passed bills every year with every Republican and every Democrat voted yes. Two of these, McGuire bills in my last year, all Republicans said we could not pass, but by the Grace of God we passed both with unanimous support, earning yes votes from every Republican and every Democrat in the State Senate, while still earning the highest awards for conservatism.
Why should you vote to remove re-elect John McGuire by August 4?

* Proven Fighter: A Navy SEAL who understands sacrifice and brings that same relentless drive to Congress every day.
* Pro-Life, Pro-Gun, Christian Conservative: I will always defend the unborn, protect our Second Amendment rights, and stand unapologetically for our Judeo-Christian heritage.
* America First Record: Strong on border security, tax relief, deregulation, election integrity, and fighting back against projects like Valley Link that hurt our rural communities. I proudly support the Save America Act.
* Results Over Rhetoric: While others talk, I've secured major funding, passed historic bills, and returned millions to our district.
* Trump-Endorsed Conservative: The first incumbent Trump backed because he knows I'll fight alongside him for the America First agenda.
* One of Us: A rural Virginian, husband, and father of five who shares your values and works every day to defend our families, our freedoms, and our future.

Liberty University, a university that trains champions for Jesus Christ, has already produced generations of outstanding soldiers and airmen. I've been working with stakeholders to make Navy ROTC at LU happen and it is my hope soon Liberty University will also develop the next generation of naval leaders. Go Navy! Faith, Family, and Freedom | == The fight to keep Virginia's 5th District Republican and America First is on right now. Unfortunately, most people do not know we have a primary vote going on right now so please spread the word. Early voting is underway, and the Republican primary deadline of August 4 is fast approaching, I'm reaching out personally to ask for your vote today. We must defend our conservative principles and send a proven fighter back to Washington, not someone who talks the talk, but a battle-tested conservative who delivers real results. As a Navy SEAL veteran, husband, father of five, and your Congressman with prior service in the Virginia General Assembly, I've stood firm for conservative values while getting things done for our district. I was the first incumbent in the nation endorsed by President Trump for re-election this cycle. Secured community funding: Congress approved 18 out of 18 of my community project requests this appropriations cycle, including a new fire truck for Louisa County and renovations for the Nottoway County Sheriff's Office. Passed long-stalled legislation: Recently passed two bills out of the House in just three weeks, including the Wintergreen emergency egress bill, a 25-year fight that six previous Members of Congress couldn't finish. Working to help Liberty University get a Navy ROTC Program Helped 57 constituents from The Point Church get home during ballistic missile attacks in Israel Helped President Trump with language for his counter drone executive order Connected with thousands of constituents through 5 tele-town halls Earned top conservative credentials: Club for Growth's top conservatism award Champion of Limited Government top conservatism award from the Institute for Legislative Analysis CPAC's top conservatism award, Award for Conservative Excellence 100% score from the Family Research Council (FRC) 100% score from the Heritage Foundation Endorsed by the NRA and Tyler Yzaguirre, President of the Second Amendment Institute In the General Assembly, my team and I passed bills every year with every Republican and every Democrat voted yes. Two of these, McGuire bills in my last year, all Republicans said we could not pass, but by the Grace of God we passed both with unanimous support, earning yes votes from every Republican and every Democrat in the State Senate, while still earning the highest awards for conservatism. Why should you vote to remove re-elect John McGuire by August 4? Proven Fighter: A Navy SEAL who understands sacrifice and brings that same relentless drive to Congress every day. America First Record: Strong on border security, tax relief, deregulation, election integrity, and fighting back against projects like Valley Link that hurt our rural communities. I proudly support the Save America Act. Results Over Rhetoric: While others talk, I've secured major funding, passed historic bills, and returned millions to our district. Trump-Endorsed Conservative: The first incumbent Trump backed because he knows I'll fight alongside him for the America First agenda. One of Us: A rural Virginian, husband, and father of five who shares your values and works every day to defend our families, our freedoms, and our future. == Let's keep Virginia's 5th District represented by a strong, effective conservative who gets the job done. Thank you for standing with me. Your vote, your generosity, and your patriotism mean everything. Please vote for John McGuire by August 4 and help keep the momentum going. Outside, cold and blustery weather returned to Adams County after several days of spring like temperatures. Inside, fragrant blossoms and shiny green leaves on our greenhouse window plants and dwarf citrus trees provide an antidote to the whipping winds. Nothing makes a room smell more like spring than the soft lemony scent of the blossoms of a Meyer lemon tree. Citrus from Seed? Dwarf Citrus Tree, Improved Meyer Lemon (Plant and Planter) Citrus lemon 'Improved Meyer' Children often wonder if they can grow a tree from the seeds found inside oranges, tangerines, oranges, lemons, and grapefruit. Yes, as long as the seed is not damaged, the odds are good that it will produce a plant. But, you need to know that seedlings experience a very long period before they flower and bear fruit- perhaps seven years or more! Most citrus grown for indoor home use are dwarf varieties that are either cuttings grown or grafted on a dwarfing rootstock. By using cuttings or grafts from mature trees, a plant is produced that is ready to begin fruiting right away. According to GFEKXGKWCOUEX8KYDHDWTL0200G6YH, garden writer for the E34OJ204425EQSG, if you are serious about citrus, consider trees that are sold for pot culture like the Meyer lemon and other dwarf varieties. The "improved" Meyer Lemon tree is the most popular of all citrus trees, easy to grow, prolific in its blooming and fruiting, and a favorite of chefs for gourmet recipes. If you are looking for an unusual plant to give as a gift, consider a dwarf kumquat, lemon, tangerine, or a handsome calamondin orange with small white blooms that perfume the house. Citrus Varieties That Thrive Indoors Calamondin- The plants have wide, lush leaves and bright orange fruit that resemble small tangerines. Kaffir lime- A lime tree that also boasts delicious leaves used in cooking Southeast Asian dishes. Meiwa kumquat- These kumquats are sweet, round, and perfect for fresh eating. Meyer lemon- The lemons are deep yellow and the trees will bear fruit heavily. Caring for Indoor Citrus Here is a brief guide for keeping your indoor citrus plants happy and healthy: Location: Make sure your plants receive five to six hours of sunlight. Set your tree in a southern exposure, if possible, or supplement the light by using 40 watt fluorescent shop lights above the plants. Fertilizer: Use an acidic fertilizer during the plant's active growing season in late winter, June and August. Use a high-nitrogen-low phosphorus food (20-10-10) or one specifically for citrus every time you water. Water: Your pot must have good drainage as you water every few days. Mist the leaves and give your tree a shower occasionally. Humidity: Homes in winter have drier air, so try a tray of pebbles under the pot. With the right care and a little luck, your own personal citrus grove will bring you great enjoyment and last for years. Just imagine strolling into your living room or kitchen to pluck a lemon for use in your favorite lemon bar recipe or limes for Tex-Mex dressing. ## FCC Approves Giant Space Mirror in the Sky
Federal regulators have [approved a California startup's plan](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu2zAMRb_G3hjIshqng4cu2V7XjgZtUTFfadGQmOfm7wunn9CN4ME9wL2_PqYPZOH8-IkbjZZ0ynRUITMqExfMs-jyGyMJ51jx9Si44jZ556_gBujCFJHlNYU2jonIU9_S2A234Hw_dNd2Hb8F7G-YFuz6GIc54YCIdP3e94FuGF3L42lzQxc65259uKR59l3AkHBOOA--CY4im5bLp3K2lZK89IvKZdGtlXE122vT_2j8vfH34zgudceFTtr4-_sG-rOLFjTWfP7QSISNauPvhZLQYqBlZkOBz2c1eKjBTmXjWlkzmILgMy8rsFXoqsE_7calaDnxOw1GuYImsFWfFXOssGkhWPQpEZKK6NGWMe4Hi3C9Dk1wjw1Z3k3sv-b_Gv3fAAAA___naqDE) to launch a giant space mirror that will catch sunlight and beam it back down to targeted spots on Earth long after the sun has set. ## _Jurassic Park's_ Sam Neill Dies at 78

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

name: Dan Cox
subject: 16 Saturdays left
body:
We need your help now. | | |
# Only 16 Saturdays to Save Maryland.
---
| | Dear , We want to thank you for all you have and are doing to save Maryland with us. What we cannot do alone, you are helping happen together. **IMPORTANT - please read our PS below as well as this e-mail update.**

We as Republicans in Maryland are united like never before; Wes Moore has awakened us to the need of this hour. **Our children and seniors are questioning a future here in Maryland, businesses and family finances are facing certain overwhelming taxes and fee increases, and our streets are more and more dangerous, only to get worse without change**.

**We literally only have 16 Saturdays until the election on November 3** where we will determine the future of our State. This is why I am personally asking for your help now to do three things:

1\. Sponsor our TV ads now running state-wide on streaming services to over 550 channels such as ESPN, NBC/CBS/ABC, CNN, FoxNews, movie shows, and more. We also need to get our ads on cable. We need at least [10 donors at $400/week](https://us.list-manage.com/108xXCu659q?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) for the remaining 16 weeks until the election to cover this push. Will you help us?

2\. Sign up to volunteer to door knock with me and our teams across the five bluest counties plus Baltimore City. People are hurting and they realize it's not about Party politics, it is about right policies. When we reach them door to door, they vote for our policies. Sign up today [here](https://us.list-manage.com/Wet275HLmas?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b).

3\. [Display a sign](https://us.list-manage.com/ze_4wSBkQ0z?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) and [buy our merch](https://us.list-manage.com/16uY4Nh9kPW?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b). We are adding new merchandise weekly - help us out by getting it delivered to your house and displaying them.
Thank you for joining us to fight for our State, Our Beautiful Maryland.

[](https://us.list-manage.com/ErSh3Ftq2GX?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)
Dan Cox
Republican Nominee for Governor of Maryland
P.S. If you are wondering why I am asking you every day now for help to win, it is because this is the most time sensitive task we have: to raise the funds necessary to save our State and get our excellent TV ads all over streaming, cable and social media platforms reaching millions. Keep in mind it can take 5-7 days to get a TV ad airing once we have shot the commercial, just because of cyclical programming. So this request if acted on today by you will actually matriculate into TV ads likely a week from now at the earliest. So this is why time is of the essence today. Thank you for helping!

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. # Conforti Grassroots Newsletter
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

Welcome to our interactive grassroots newsletter. As we approach the Midterm Election 2026, this newsletter is dedicated to keeping the hardworking constituents of Illinois' 6th Congressional District informed and engaged.

Our campaign is built on a "district-first" mentality. We are committed to prioritizing your needs, focusing on fundamental ideals of sensible solutions and open dialogue. Through this newsletter, we will provide you with regular updates on policy, campaign events, and current community events happening right here in our district.
Click the button below to make a donation today. Your donations are what makes this possible.
---
| | [DONATE](https://us.list-manage.com/wiE14a1kNA2?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)
---
| |
---
| |
## Kitchen Table Tuesday.
The Conforti Brief.
District-First Events.
---
| |
### Educate. Inform. Invite.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
# Kitchen Table Tuesday
---
| | **Educating and connecting** with voters on important issues.
---
| | |
---
| | I know how deeply our community values safety, and right now, many of us are concerned about the direction things are heading. **Policies like the Safe-T Act have proven to be detrimental** to the safety of our communities, directly contributing to a rise in violent crime. It is unacceptable that everyday citizens are feeling less safe in their own neighborhoods. Furthermore, the radical agenda attacking our police has deterred people from joining the force, driving recruitment to all-time lows and exacerbating our safety challenges. We cannot continue to support a system that favors criminals over victims.
.To reverse this dangerous trend, my goal is to **strongly oppose defunding our local police departments while advocating for sensible criminal justice reforms.** We must provide our law enforcement officers with improved training and procedural improvements so they can do their jobs effectively. The impact of this approach will be clear: by ending the reckless practice of releasing violent felons on their own recognizance, we will immediately make our communities safer. It is time to restore order and ensure that our neighborhoods remain secure places to live, work, and raise a family.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
## The Conforti Brief
---
| | **Informing voters** on current events and how Niki plans to help them once in office.
---
| | Restoring Safety and Accountability to Our Communities
.Recently, the DuPage Policy Journal reported that Glen Ellyn residents are experiencing a **spike in encounters with a volatile homeless population, coupled with a lack of adequate enforcement policies.** Residents have witnessed homeless individuals threatening pedestrians and screaming at children, yet the response is often nonexistent or subpar. Furthermore, despite hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars being spent statewide, homelessness continues to worsen. Organizations heavily dependent on public funding, like DuPage Pads, are seeing their waitlists explode while their executives receive massive salaries and demand even more state funding.
.This escalating crisis is a **direct result of the failed, radical agenda championed by politicians like Democrat incumbent Sean Casten.** Instead of demanding accountability and fiscal responsibility, Casten handpicked the CEO of DuPage Pads as a VIP guest for the 2023 State of the Union Address to praise federal support for organizations like hers. Casten is one of the most liberal members of the House Democratic caucus. Instead of protecting our communities, Sean Casten favors criminals over victims and turns a blind eye to the systemic inefficiencies making our district less safe.
.When elected to represent the 6th District in the U.S. House of Representatives, Niki Conforti will **prioritize public safety and ensure taxpayer dollars are not wasted** by systematic inefficiencies. She will take direct federal action by:

1. 1\. **Stopping Wasteful Spending:** To maximize the impact of your tax dollars, Niki will push for spending caps that rein in the Left's radical debt crisis. Furthermore, she will hold Washington accountable by ensuring the oversight committee aggressively investigates financial fraud and abuse.
.
2. 2.**Backing Law Enforcement:** Niki opposes defunding our local police departments. She will support sensible criminal justice reforms, improved police training, and procedural improvements.
.

We cannot allow a lack of policing and reckless government spending to hold our local communities hostage.

Stay informed on this issue—[**read the full breakdown here.**](https://us.list-manage.com/232k7AvTPnQ?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)

# Events
---
| | **Inviting voters** to community events and how they can get involved!**
**Join the Conforti Campaign at the** Meet the Candidates Night!**
---
| |
---
| | **Meet the Candidates Night!**
.We warmly invite you to join Niki Conforti and our campaign team for an exciting evening of open dialogue. This event is a fantastic opportunity to discuss our campaign's focus on grassroots engagement, economic affordability, and community safety with local leaders and neighbors. Come out to meet your candidates and share your vision for the district!

* **Date:** Wednesday, July 22, 2026
* **Time:** 5:30 PM – 7:30 PM
* **Featured Candidates:** Niki Conforti (Candidate for U.S. Congressional District 6) and Brian Skala (Candidate for IL Senate District 14)
* **Location:** Elks Lodge in Crestwood, IL

.

**Coffee with Niki Conforti
.**Looking for a casual setting to talk about the issues that matter most to your family? Grab a cup of coffee and join Niki for a one-on-one conversation about reining in reckless government spending, cutting red tape for small businesses, and protecting local communities.

* **Date:** Thursday, August 6, 2026
* **Time:** 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM
* **Location:** Krema Coffee in Tinley Park, IL

Get Involved: Bring your family, friends, and neighbors to these events to learn more about our District-First vision. For more information, please contact our team at [**info@conforti4congress.com.**](mailto:info@conforti4congress.com?subject=Event%3A%20Meet%20the%20Candidates%20%2F%20Coffee%20with%20Niki&body=)

We look forward to seeing you there!

# Our Next Fight
| |
---
|
---
Many Texans assume vaccine mandates are a thing of the past. Unfortunately, that's not true. Today, **vaccine requirements still threaten** the livelihoods of healthcare workers, block students from pursuing careers in human and animal healthcare, and allow patients to face discrimination simply because they decline a vaccine. That's why Texans for Vaccine Choice is making **Ending Medical Mandates** our top legislative priority for the 90th Legislative Session. _Our legislative agenda focuses on three critical reforms:_ **End Vaccine Mandates for Healthcare Workers**
No doctor, nurse, technician, veterinarian, or other healthcare professional should ever have to choose between earning a living and making a personal medical decision. **End Vaccine Mandates for Healthcare Students**
Future healthcare professionals should not be denied the education they've worked for because clinical training sites impose vaccine requirements. **Protect Patients from Vaccine Discrimination**
No Texan should lose access to medical care because they decline a vaccine. The doctor-patient relationship should be guided by trust and informed consent alone. These discriminatory policies are still in full force today, and they have **no place in Texas**. It's time to ensure that every Texan can work, learn, and receive medical care without being judged or penalized based on vaccination status. Although the 90th Legislative Session doesn't begin until January, Team TFVC is **already laying the groundwork** by preparing our November Voter Guide, drafting legislation, meeting with elected officials, and securing bill authors. When the Session begins, we'll need **YOUR** voice to help turn these priorities into law. **Together, we can make Texas the national leader in protecting medical freedom.**

That's why Texans for Vaccine Choice is making Ending Medical Mandates our top legislative priority for the 90th Legislative Session. Our legislative agenda focuses on three critical reforms: End Vaccine Mandates for Healthcare Workers No doctor, nurse, technician, veterinarian, or other healthcare professional should ever have to choose between earning a living and making a personal medical decision. End Vaccine Mandates for Healthcare Students Future healthcare professionals should not be denied the education they've worked for because clinical training sites impose vaccine requirements. Protect Patients from Vaccine Discrimination No Texan should lose access to medical care because they decline a vaccine. subject: Fajr prayer at 6:00 AM

body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=2611%2E251025%2E0YeLvF ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=2611%2E251025%2E0YeLvF ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter,

As folks turn their attention to Michigan and the critical primary
election taking place on August 4th, I want to share a bit more about who
I am.

One of the aspects of my candidacy that has become a key focus, like it or
not, is my faith. Whether or not people want to say it, when they raise
questions about my “electability,” they are usually pointing to the most
obvious thing about me that makes me “different,” that's my name and my
Muslim faith.

And it’s true. My faith does make me a bit different.

See, faith, to me, isn’t just about an identity. It’s about the choices
that I make every single day about how I live my life. I wake up, usually
between 5:30 and 6:00. I wash up in preparation for my morning fajr
prayer. At 6:00 AM, every single day. That’s the first of five times every
day I pray. It’s a spiritual practice that reminds me that I am
accountable. I am accountable to my belief, to the people I love, to the
people I serve, and to a future I hope to be a part of building.

My faith has also shaped the paths I've walked. In college, you'd sooner
find me in the stacks in the library at midnight than at a party. I met
Sarah, my wife of 20 years, through the Muslim Students' Association. We
got married soon after — we were 21 and 19. Even then, it was so unusual
that the school paper wrote a headline article about it!

[ The ]The Michigan Daily headline: Married ... with classes. The article
features a photo of Abdul and his wife, Sarah, as college students.

We’re raising our two little girls, Emmalee and Serene, as strong, capable
women. I want them to be just like my grandmother, my mom, and Sarah — a
doctor (the kind that sees patients!). Just like the strong women who’ve
built me.

My faith has also taught me how to be comfortable with my differences. I
know what it’s like to be discriminated against. Before I ever ran for
office, I knew what it was like to have my intentions questioned, my
choices scrutinized, and my every word picked apart. Because that scrutiny
didn’t start when I ran for office. I’ve been under scrutiny since I can
remember, in every room where I am “the only.” And I’ve always known that
I won’t be held to the same standard as everyone else, but that my bar
will be higher because of my faith. And yet the same faith that’s exposed
me to scrutiny has offered me the discipline and accountability to
withstand it.

Being different has also taught me not to judge others for how they might
be different. It teaches you a particular kind of empathy. We all deserve
the dignity, security, and goodwill to chart our life's path without being
told we are less than, or not worthy. We deserve that regardless of who we
are, how or if we pray, how we love, how we identify, or where we grew up.

That is the politics I am fighting to build. A politics of empathy, where
dignity is not reserved for some of us but guaranteed to all of us, in our
health care, our paychecks, and our communities.

clean_body: [ ]Abdul for US Senate [ ]Abdul for US Senate Peter, As folks turn their attention to Michigan and the critical primary election taking place on August 4th, I want to share a bit more about who I am. One of the aspects of my candidacy that has become a key focus, like it or not, is my faith. Whether or not people want to say it, when they raise questions about my “electability,” they are usually pointing to the most obvious thing about me that makes me “different,” that's my name and my Muslim faith. And it’s true. My faith does make me a bit different. See, faith, to me, isn’t just about an identity. It’s about the choices that I make every single day about how I live my life. I wake up, usually between 5:30 and 6:00. I wash up in preparation for my morning fajr prayer. At 6:00 AM, every single day. That’s the first of five times every day I pray. It’s a spiritual practice that reminds me that I am accountable. I am accountable to my belief, to the people I love, to the people I serve, and to a future I hope to be a part of building. My faith has also shaped the paths I've walked. In college, you'd sooner find me in the stacks in the library at midnight than at a party. I met Sarah, my wife of 20 years, through the Muslim Students' Association. We got married soon after — we were 21 and 19. Even then, it was so unusual that the school paper wrote a headline article about it! [ The ]The Michigan Daily headline: Married ... with classes. The article features a photo of Abdul and his wife, Sarah, as college students. We’re raising our two little girls, Emmalee and Serene, as strong, capable women. I want them to be just like my grandmother, my mom, and Sarah — a doctor (the kind that sees patients!). Just like the strong women who’ve built me. My faith has also taught me how to be comfortable with my differences. I know what it’s like to be discriminated against. Before I ever ran for office, I knew what it was like to have my intentions questioned, my choices scrutinized, and my every word picked apart. Because that scrutiny didn’t start when I ran for office. I’ve been under scrutiny since I can remember, in every room where I am “the only.” And I’ve always known that I won’t be held to the same standard as everyone else, but that my bar will be higher because of my faith. And yet the same faith that’s exposed me to scrutiny has offered me the discipline and accountability to withstand it. Being different has also taught me not to judge others for how they might be different. It teaches you a particular kind of empathy. We all deserve the dignity, security, and goodwill to chart our life's path without being told we are less than, or not worthy. We deserve that regardless of who we are, how or if we pray, how we love, how we identify, or where we grew up. That is the politics I am fighting to build. A politics of empathy, where dignity is not reserved for some of us but guaranteed to all of us, in our health care, our paychecks, and our communities. But that kind of politics does not come from super PACs or corporate interests. It never has. It is built by people. By many giving what they can. ### Most Americans don't have a college degree. It's time to let veterans pursue the skilled trades with the same GI Bill benefits as those attending college.
| | [Patrick J. Murphy](https://substack.com/@patrickmurphypa) and [Jason Altmire](https://substack.com/@jasonaltmire)
