body:
We can’t keep living — and dying — this way.
#

Friends,
Yesterday, ICE was involved in another shooting — killing Joan Sebastian Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine. Sebastian was shot in front of his partner and their 3-year-old daughter, who are now grieving a loss no family should ever have to bear.
This marks the second fatal ICE-involved shooting in less than one week.
Last Tuesday, ICE agents shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo during a traffic stop in Houston, Texas. He was a father, husband, and business owner who had been in the country for 35 years.
While these stories are still unfolding, there is one thing we know: These tragedies deserve a full, transparent, and independent investigation.
ICE surges do not increase public safety — they escalate violence, stoke fear in communities, and greatly increase the risk of wrongful shootings. It was just earlier this year when ICE agents shot and killed Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti in Minnesota.
We can’t keep living — and dying — this way. Our country deserves better.
GIFFORDS will continue working to make our communities safer, holding the Trump administration accountable whenever they overstep, and ending the gun violence epidemic in our country.
— GIFFORDS

**Please, take a second to read this...**
Gabby Giffords has led the fight against the gun lobby for more than a decade, but she can't do it alone.
If everyone reading this donated just $17, we'd have the resources to take on the gun lobby in Congress and states across the country. But not everyone gives — making it even more important for people who care and understand the stakes of our struggle to pitch in what they can.
If $17 seems worth it to you to change our gun laws in order to make our communities safer from gun violence, we're asking you to contribute to GIFFORDS PAC today.

name: Raja Krishnamoorth
subject: Trump just dismantled a bipartisan election agency. 🚨
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
I need to tell you something I don't talk about enough.
Outside of my office, a group of extremists gathered and screamed what translates to "Death to Krishnamoorthi" at the top of their lungs.
A crowd of people, in America, calling for my death.
I'm an immigrant. The son of people who came to this country with nothing because they believed it was a place where you could live freely, speak freely, and serve your community without fearing for your life. A place where disagreement didn't end in threats of violence.
Sadly, this is nothing new. I have faced this before.
A sitting Republican elected official also publicly tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media to report me as a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name" and called for the mass deportation of Indians. I have been mocked, threatened, and told in a hundred different ways that someone like me doesn't belong in American public life.
And every single time, I have made the same choice.
Keep going.
Because the moment I stop — the moment I let the hatred win — is the moment I break faith with every family that came to this country believing it was worth fighting for. Including my own.
This is the America we are living in right now. Extremists feel emboldened to threaten, intimidate, and silence the people who are trying to do the work. Hatred has been given permission to operate in the open. The machinery of government is being used to make certain communities feel like they don't belong.
Equal Opportunity Now exists because we need leaders who have faced this kind of hatred and didn't flinch . Who know what it costs to keep going and choose to keep going anyway. Who will stand up — not just for themselves, but for every family that is being targeted, threatened, and told they don't belong.
Those leaders are out there. And they need our support right now.
Will you chip in $10, $20, or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now today to help us elect leaders who won't be intimidated — no matter what they face? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE TODAY! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
They can scream all they want.
We are not slowing down.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi
Founder | Equal Opportunity Now

Today is the final day of our fundraising deadline and what we raise by midnight determines how many Maine voters we can reach with my real solutions before the summer is over. * Digital ads that put my housing plan in front of families who need to hear it
* Voter contact that turns supporters into volunteers and volunteers into votes
* Travel so we can continue to show up in every corner of Maine, not just the easy ones
* Printed materials for doors, town halls, and community events across the state

On Sunday, I had the honor of marching in the **Puerto Rican Parade of Fairfield County in Bridgeport** --an extraordinary celebration of Puerto Rican pride, heritage, resilience and culture.
To my knowledge, I was the only Republican candidate who officially marched in the parade. I was proud to be joined by my son Jonathan.
There were many elected officials marching including Governor Lamont, and Senator Blumenthal.
Together, we carried my banner as families filled the streets, waved Puerto Rican and American flags and celebrated traditions passed from one generation to the next. I cannot think of another parade in Fairfield County that inspires this same level of enthusiasm, participation and community spirit.
## More Than a Campaign Banner
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/86cee14c-aaff-4c6a-96fa-10c8b3be72c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The banner we carried represented much more than a political campaign. It celebrated my longstanding relationship with the Puerto Rican community--a community I have had the privilege of serving as an eye physician for more than 40 years in New York.
The banner also featured boxing gloves, recognizing my experience as an examining physician for the New York State Athletic Commission. In that role, I examined and medically cleared boxers before they competed in New York, including fighters appearing at Madison Square Garden.
I have examined generations of Puerto Rican patients, listened to their stories and witnessed their commitment to family, faith, hard work and cultural pride.
Marching in this parade was not the beginning of that relationship. It was a public celebration of a connection that has developed over decades.
One of my favorite parts of Puerto Rican celebrations is the beloved refrain:
**" Que bonita bandera, la bandera puertorriqueña."**
How beautiful is the Puerto Rican flag.
Its beauty comes from more than its design. It comes from everything it represents--the struggles Puerto Ricans have endured, the sacrifices families have made, the traditions they have preserved and the pride that has carried the community forward.
**Puerto Rican pride lifts all of us.**
It reminds us that hardship can make us stronger, that heritage should be celebrated and that pride in where we come from can inspire us to build a better future together.
## An Essential Part of Connecticut
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a8da436-2953-4da5-a1f8-8612f9bda284?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
According to 2021 estimates from UConn's Puerto Rican Studies Initiative, Connecticut was home to approximately **283,528 Puerto Rican residents**.
Approximately **44,544 Puerto Ricans lived in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District**, representing about 6 percent of the district's population and approximately 29 percent of its Hispanic and Latino population.
Bridgeport is at the heart of this community. Approximately **29,012 Puerto Ricans lived in Bridgeport** , accounting for roughly 20 percent of the city's population, according to the same estimates.
These are not merely statistics. They represent families, workers, veterans, business owners, healthcare professionals, educators, students, artists, tradespeople and community leaders who contribute to Connecticut every day.
## Pride in the Face of Adversity
Puerto Rico has faced poverty, political corruption, destructive hurricanes and persistent infrastructure and electrical problems. Yet those challenges have not diminished the Puerto Rican people's love for their island or their determination to preserve their culture.
In many ways, adversity has made the Puerto Rican spirit stronger.
That strength could be seen throughout the parade. Young dancers performed in traditional clothing. Floats honored Puerto Rican history and Bridgeport's Puerto Rican culture. Music filled the streets, and families spanning several generations cheered as the Puerto Rican flag passed before them.
I was also impressed by the many Bridgeport residents who were not Puerto Rican but came out to celebrate and support their neighbors.
That is what community means--respecting one another, celebrating together and standing beside our neighbors.
## Discipline, Boxing and the Next Generation
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e775bc73-9013-4379-8f52-2717644b15cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It is fitting that Puerto Rico has produced so many great boxers. Boxing requires courage, preparation, sacrifice, discipline and the willingness to keep fighting when circumstances become difficult.
As an eye doctor, I have examined many boxers before their competitions--from fighters beginning their careers to world champions preparing for the biggest contests of their lives. Many of those boxers were Puerto Rican.
Before the parade, I spoke with Coach Carlos Ortiz about Ortiz Boxing Gym and its work to keep young people active, focused and off the streets.
Athletics teach discipline, responsibility, respect and perseverance. A boxer cannot simply enter the ring and expect to succeed. Success comes through training, sacrifice and learning how to recover after being knocked down.
That lesson applies to life.
Learn more about **[Coach Carlos Ortiz and Ortiz Boxing Gym](https://substack.com/redirect/b0d6147b-1d08-4900-b1ea-ce290a765981?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
Our next generation must receive the education, skills and discipline needed to compete and succeed. A four-year college should not be presented as the only path available to students.
We need stronger vocational education, apprenticeships, technical programs, healthcare training and partnerships between schools and employers. Just as disciplined training prepares a boxer to enter the ring, education and workforce training must prepare young people to enter the economy with confidence.
## Listening to the People I Am Running to Serve
The most important part of the day was not simply walking in the parade. It was listening to the people I am running to represent.
Before and after the parade, I spoke with residents and families about healthcare, affordability, job opportunities, education and workforce training.
They discussed the rising costs of groceries, housing, electricity, insurance and healthcare. They questioned whether Connecticut's economy will provide meaningful opportunities for their children and whether our schools are preparing students for real careers.
These are not merely Republican or Democratic problems. They are Connecticut problems.
A family's electric bill does not care how that family voted. The cost of healthcare does not decrease because someone belongs to a particular political party. A young person looking for work does not benefit from partisan speeches that fail to produce a genuine opportunity.
This campaign is about **people over parties** and results over political rhetoric.
## Supporting the Campaign - Taking the Fight to November - The Primary - August 11th
Despite the nearly 90-degree weather and the relentless summer sun, I never felt tired.
I felt energized.
Every cheer, handshake, high-five, flag, song and conversation reinforced the same message:
**Heritage matters. Family matters. Community matters. Opportunity matters.**
I am in a Republican primary because the people of Connecticut's Fourth Congressional District deserve a representative who will show up, listen and fight for every community.
**I am a fighter.**
I have spent my professional life fighting for my patients, my family and people who needed someone willing to stand beside them. I am ready to bring that determination to Congress.
I would be honored to earn the support of voters across the Fourth Congressional District.
_**If you are a registered Republican, I ask for your vote in the Republican primary. on August 11th with Early Voting August 3-9.**_
Unaffiliated voters who choose to enroll as Republicans may also participate and help us take this fight to November.
I am running to represent everyone in Connecticut's Fourth Congressional District--not only Republicans and not only those who vote for me.
> _**A member of Congress is elected by a district, but the responsibility reaches beyond district lines. Members of Congress make decisions affecting their state, their country and American citizens throughout our nation --including our fellow Americans in Puerto Rico.**_
> _**We must fight for accessible healthcare, greater affordability, better-paying jobs, stronger schools and workforce training that prepares the next generation to succeed.**_
## Thank You To the Puerto Rican Parade of Fairfield County
My sincere thanks to **Milta Feliciano, President of the Puerto Rican Parade of Fairfield County, Inc.** , the entire board and every volunteer whose time, energy and hard work made this remarkable celebration possible.
A parade of this size and importance cannot happen without volunteers. Thank you to every person who helped organize the event, prepare the route, coordinate the participants, support the performers, assist families, clean up afterward and contribute countless hours behind the scenes.
Thank you as well to the performers, sponsors, participating organizations and families who brought the streets of Bridgeport to life.
I also thank the Bridgeport Police officers, the Norwalk Police officers who participated and all the public-safety professionals who helped keep the parade safe and welcoming.
Learn more about the organization and support its work at **[PRPFCCT.org](https://substack.com/redirect/21fcac5f-90d0-44a4-a607-987bf3b55be1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
The Puerto Rican Parade of Fairfield County was more than a parade. It was a celebration of heritage, resilience, family, discipline, patriotism and community.
It was an honor to march with you, listen to you and celebrate with you.
**Qu e bonita bandera, la bandera puertorriqueña.**
**¡ Que viva Puerto Rico!**
**God bless Bridgeport, God bless Puerto Rico and God bless the United States of America.**

The banner also featured boxing gloves, recognizing my experience as an examining physician for the New York State Athletic Commission. In that role, I examined and medically cleared boxers before they competed in New York, including fighters appearing at Madison Square Garden. I have examined generations of Puerto Rican patients, listened to their stories and witnessed their commitment to family, faith, hard work and cultural pride. Marching in this parade was not the beginning of that relationship. It was a public celebration of a connection that has developed over decades. One of my favorite parts of Puerto Rican celebrations is the beloved refrain: " Que bonita bandera, la bandera puertorriqueña." How beautiful is the Puerto Rican flag. Its beauty comes from more than its design. It comes from everything it represents--the struggles Puerto Ricans have endured, the sacrifices families have made, the traditions they have preserved and the pride that has carried the community forward. Puerto Rican pride lifts all of us. It reminds us that hardship can make us stronger, that heritage should be celebrated and that pride in where we come from can inspire us to build a better future together. An Essential Part of Connecticut | | ---|---|--- According to 2021 estimates from UConn's Puerto Rican Studies Initiative, Connecticut was home to approximately 283,528 Puerto Rican residents. Approximately 44,544 Puerto Ricans lived in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District, representing about 6 percent of the district's population and approximately 29 percent of its Hispanic and Latino population. Bridgeport is at the heart of this community. Approximately 29,012 Puerto Ricans lived in Bridgeport , accounting for roughly 20 percent of the city's population, according to the same estimates. These are not merely statistics. They represent families, workers, veterans, business owners, healthcare professionals, educators, students, artists, tradespeople and community leaders who contribute to Connecticut every day. Pride in the Face of Adversity Puerto Rico has faced poverty, political corruption, destructive hurricanes and persistent infrastructure and electrical problems. Yet those challenges have not diminished the Puerto Rican people's love for their island or their determination to preserve their culture. In many ways, adversity has made the Puerto Rican spirit stronger. That strength could be seen throughout the parade. Young dancers performed in traditional clothing. Floats honored Puerto Rican history and Bridgeport's Puerto Rican culture. Music filled the streets, and families spanning several generations cheered as the Puerto Rican flag passed before them. I was also impressed by the many Bridgeport residents who were not Puerto Rican but came out to celebrate and support their neighbors. That is what community means--respecting one another, celebrating together and standing beside our neighbors. Discipline, Boxing and the Next Generation | | ---|---|--- It is fitting that Puerto Rico has produced so many great boxers. Boxing requires courage, preparation, sacrifice, discipline and the willingness to keep fighting when circumstances become difficult. As an eye doctor, I have examined many boxers before their competitions--from fighters beginning their careers to world champions preparing for the biggest contests of their lives. Many of those boxers were Puerto Rican. Before the parade, I spoke with Coach Carlos Ortiz about Ortiz Boxing Gym and its work to keep young people active, focused and off the streets. Athletics teach discipline, responsibility, respect and perseverance. A boxer cannot simply enter the ring and expect to succeed. Success comes through training, sacrifice and learning how to recover after being knocked down. That lesson applies to life. Learn more about . Our next generation must receive the education, skills and discipline needed to compete and succeed. A four-year college should not be presented as the only path available to students. We need stronger vocational education, apprenticeships, technical programs, healthcare training and partnerships between schools and employers. Just as disciplined training prepares a boxer to enter the ring, education and workforce training must prepare young people to enter the economy with confidence. Listening to the People I Am Running to Serve The most important part of the day was not simply walking in the parade. It was listening to the people I am running to represent. Before and after the parade, I spoke with residents and families about healthcare, affordability, job opportunities, education and workforce training. They discussed the rising costs of groceries, housing, electricity, insurance and healthcare. They questioned whether Connecticut's economy will provide meaningful opportunities for their children and whether our schools are preparing students for real careers. These are not merely Republican or Democratic problems. They are Connecticut problems. A family's electric bill does not care how that family voted. The cost of healthcare does not decrease because someone belongs to a particular political party. A young person looking for work does not benefit from partisan speeches that fail to produce a genuine opportunity. This campaign is about people over parties and results over political rhetoric. Supporting the Campaign - Taking the Fight to November - The Primary - August 11th Despite the nearly 90-degree weather and the relentless summer sun, I never felt tired. I felt energized. Every cheer, handshake, high-five, flag, song and conversation reinforced the same message: Heritage matters. Family matters. Community matters. Opportunity matters. I am in a Republican primary because the people of Connecticut's Fourth Congressional District deserve a representative who will show up, listen and fight for every community. I am a fighter. I have spent my professional life fighting for my patients, my family and people who needed someone willing to stand beside them. I am ready to bring that determination to Congress. I would be honored to earn the support of voters across the Fourth Congressional District. If you are a registered Republican, I ask for your vote in the Republican primary. on August 11th with Early Voting August 3-9. Unaffiliated voters who choose to enroll as Republicans may also participate and help us take this fight to November. I am running to represent everyone in Connecticut's Fourth Congressional District--not only Republicans and not only those who vote for me. A member of Congress is elected by a district, but the responsibility reaches beyond district lines. Members of Congress make decisions affecting their state, their country and American citizens throughout our nation --including our fellow Americans in Puerto Rico. We must fight for accessible healthcare, greater affordability, better-paying jobs, stronger schools and workforce training that prepares the next generation to succeed. Thank You To the Puerto Rican Parade of Fairfield County My sincere thanks to Milta Feliciano, President of the Puerto Rican Parade of Fairfield County, Inc. , the entire board and every volunteer whose time, energy and hard work made this remarkable celebration possible. A parade of this size and importance cannot happen without volunteers. Thank you to every person who helped organize the event, prepare the route, coordinate the participants, support the performers, assist families, clean up afterward and contribute countless hours behind the scenes. Thank you as well to the performers, sponsors, participating organizations and families who brought the streets of Bridgeport to life. I also thank the Bridgeport Police officers, the Norwalk Police officers who participated and all the public-safety professionals who helped keep the parade safe and welcoming. Learn more about the organization and support its work at . The Puerto Rican Parade of Fairfield County was more than a parade. It was a celebration of heritage, resilience, family, discipline, patriotism and community. It was an honor to march with you, listen to you and celebrate with you. Qu e bonita bandera, la bandera puertorriqueña. ¡ Que viva Puerto Rico! God bless Bridgeport, God bless Puerto Rico and God bless the United States of America.** The Goldstein Substack is free today. But if you enjoyed this post, you can tell The Goldstein Substack that their writing is valuable by pledging a future subscription. You won't be charged unless they enable payments. | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Michael Goldstein ? ?

For the first time, we're releasing a limited number of guest tickets at $1,000 each, giving you a front-row seat to the energy, the speeches, and the people shaping the party's direction. You don't have to be an elected delegate to be in the room.
Here's what's included:

subject: Join Us for Our Cocktails for a Cause Fundraiser
body:
** Join Our Cocktails for A Cause Fundraiser
------------------------------------------------------------

We are excited to invite you to our upcoming Cocktails for A Cause fundraiser benefiting Autism Health on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM at The Park Club in Costa Mesa, CA. Registration starts at 5:30 PM.

Sponsored by Cellular Performance Institute, this special evening will bring together supporters, families, professionals, and community leaders for a night of connection, purpose, and giving back. Guests will enjoy cocktails, networking, an inspiring presentation from Dr. Dayan Goodenowe, and both a live auction and silent auction filled with exciting items and experiences.

Tickets are $85 per person, and proceeds from the evening will help support Autism Health’s ongoing mission to provide education, resources, support programs, and outreach for families impacted by autism and neurological conditions.

We hope you will join us for this meaningful evening as we come together to make a difference in the lives of so many families.
BUY TICKETS HERE (https://givebutter.com/cocktails-4-a-cause?gbtid=364872ca-6248-4fff-badb-efb5ca682c2c&mc_cid=73c0326123&mc_eid=UNIQID)

** Our Monthly Autism Support Group Is Today!
------------------------------------------------------------

We invite you to join us for our upcoming Autism Support Group Today, July 14th at 5 PM PST / 8 PM EST via Zoom. Whether you are a parent, caregiver, family member, self advocate, or professional, this monthly gathering offers a welcoming space to connect with others who understand the autism journey.

Our support group provides an opportunity to share experiences, ask questions, exchange resources, and receive encouragement from a compassionate community. Together, we discuss the challenges and victories that come with raising and supporting individuals with autism and related neurological conditions, while learning from one another in a respectful and supportive environment.

This is more than a meeting. It is a community where families can build meaningful connections, gain practical insights, and know they are not alone on this journey.

Advance registration is required to attend. Please register using the link below to receive your Zoom access information.

We look forward to seeing you there!
REGISTER HERE (https://us06web.zoom.us/meeting/register/xQxg3Z3QSCybI3_aGxmUkA?mc_cid=73c0326123&mc_eid=UNIQID#/registration)

** Don't Miss Out on this Spectacular Savings!
------------------------------------------------------------

Save 50% on the 2027 Autism Health Summit This July!

There has never been a better time to reserve your seat for the 2027 Autism Health Summit! Throughout the month of July only, receive 50% OFF your in person admission with promo code AHS50.

Join us April 29 - May 1, 2027 at the beautiful Legacy Center Resort & Spa in San Diego, California, for three inspiring days of education, collaboration, and community. The Autism Health Summit brings together leading physicians, researchers, practitioners, advocates, and families from around the world to explore the latest advances in autism research, integrative medicine, and whole person health. This exclusive offer ends July 31st and will not be available again, so reserve your seat today.

As part of our mission to make education accessible to everyone, Autism Health proudly offers scholarships for low and middle income families who may not otherwise be able to attend. We believe every family deserves access to trusted education, resources, and a supportive community, regardless of financial circumstances. You can access the application on our website.

Register today and learn more using the links below.
REGISTER HERE (https://ahsconference.com/pricing-table/?mc_cid=73c0326123&mc_eid=UNIQID)
Are you interested in partnering with Autism Health? During the month of July, organizations can receive 10% OFF all 2027 sponsorship packages by using promo code Sponsor10. This is the perfect opportunity to showcase your organization while supporting one of the nation's premier autism education conferences.
REGISTER HERE (https://ahsconference.com/sponsors/?mc_cid=73c0326123&mc_eid=UNIQID)

Join Our July Monthly Webinar

We invite you to join us on Saturday, July 25th at 9:00 AM PST / 12:00 PM EST for an engaging and educational webinar featuring Dr. Basima Williams on Understanding the Impact of the Gut Microbiome on the Immune System.

The gut microbiome plays a vital role in overall health, influencing immune function, inflammation, digestion, and neurological well being. During this presentation, Dr. Williams will explore the powerful relationship between the gut and the immune system, discuss emerging research, and explain why optimizing gut health is an important consideration for individuals with autism and other complex health conditions.

Attendees will learn about:
- The connection between the gut microbiome and immune function
- How gut health can influence inflammation and overall wellness
- The role of the microbiome in supporting neurological health
- Practical strategies for promoting a healthy gut ecosystem
- Current research and clinical insights into microbiome based care

Whether you are a parent, caregiver, healthcare professional, or advocate, this webinar offers valuable information that can help you better understand one of the most important systems affecting overall health.

Advance registration is required. Please register using the Zoom link below to reserve your spot.

We look forward to seeing you online!

REGISTER HERE (https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_CcSG3osHTduoYUHC-bG0lQ?mc_cid=73c0326123&mc_eid=UNIQID#/registration)

** Summer Movie Fundraiser!
------------------------------------------------------------

Looking for a fun way to support Autism Health this summer? We are excited to partner with GroupRaise and Regal Cinemas for a special fundraising campaign that allows you to enjoy a night at the movies while supporting a great cause.

For just $30 per order, you'll receive a Regal Movie Ticket Bundle that includes two Standard 2D Movie Tickets, redeemable at any Regal theater location nationwide. Best of all, 20% of every purchase will be donated to Autism Health Inc. to help support our educational programs, support groups, webinars, scholarships, and research initiatives.

Did you know that many Regal Cinemas locations also offer Sensory Friendly Screenings? These special screenings are designed to create a more comfortable movie-going experience for individuals with autism and sensory sensitivities, making this fundraiser even more meaningful for our community.

Whether you're planning a family outing, date night, or looking for a unique gift, your purchase helps advance our mission of serving individuals and families impacted by autism and related neurological conditions.

Campaign Ends: Monday, August 17, 2026

Thank you for supporting Autism Health Inc. Every ticket bundle purchased helps us continue making a difference in the lives of families around the world.
BUY TICKETS HERE (https://www.groupraise.com/offer-campaigns/78957-autism-health-inc-regal-fundraising-campaigns?mc_cid=73c0326123&mc_eid=UNIQID)

About Autism Health Inc.
Autism Health is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to educating individuals, families, and communities about autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Autism Health provides educational programs, workshops, events, research, and resources tailored to meet the diverse needs of those impacted by autism and other neurological disorders.
DONATE HERE (https://autismhealth.com/donations/?mc_cid=73c0326123&mc_eid=UNIQID)

clean_body: Join Our Cocktails for A Cause Fundraiser We are excited to invite you to our upcoming Cocktails for A Cause fundraiser benefiting Autism Health on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM at The Park Club in Costa Mesa, CA. Registration starts at 5:30 PM. Sponsored by Cellular Performance Institute, this special evening will bring together supporters, families, professionals, and community leaders for a night of connection, purpose, and giving back. Guests will enjoy cocktails, networking, an inspiring presentation from Dr. Dayan Goodenowe, and both a live auction and silent auction filled with exciting items and experiences. Tickets are $85 per person, and proceeds from the evening will help support Autism Health’s ongoing mission to provide education, resources, support programs, and outreach for families impacted by autism and neurological conditions. We hope you will join us for this meaningful evening as we come together to make a difference in the lives of so many families. BUY TICKETS HERE () Our Monthly Autism Support Group Is Today! We invite you to join us for our upcoming Autism Support Group Today, July 14th at 5 PM PST / 8 PM EST via Zoom. Whether you are a parent, caregiver, family member, self advocate, or professional, this monthly gathering offers a welcoming space to connect with others who understand the autism journey. Our support group provides an opportunity to share experiences, ask questions, exchange resources, and receive encouragement from a compassionate community. Together, we discuss the challenges and victories that come with raising and supporting individuals with autism and related neurological conditions, while learning from one another in a respectful and supportive environment. This is more than a meeting. It is a community where families can build meaningful connections, gain practical insights, and know they are not alone on this journey. Advance registration is required to attend. Please register using the link below to receive your Zoom access information. We look forward to seeing you there! REGISTER HERE () Don't Miss Out on this Spectacular Savings! Save 50% on the 2027 Autism Health Summit This July! There has never been a better time to reserve your seat for the 2027 Autism Health Summit! Throughout the month of July only, receive 50% OFF your in person admission with promo code AHS50. Join us April 29 - May 1, 2027 at the beautiful Legacy Center Resort & Spa in San Diego, California, for three inspiring days of education, collaboration, and community. The Autism Health Summit brings together leading physicians, researchers, practitioners, advocates, and families from around the world to explore the latest advances in autism research, integrative medicine, and whole person health. This exclusive offer ends July 31st and will not be available again, so reserve your seat today. As part of our mission to make education accessible to everyone, Autism Health proudly offers scholarships for low and middle income families who may not otherwise be able to attend. We believe every family deserves access to trusted education, resources, and a supportive community, regardless of financial circumstances. You can access the application on our website. Register today and learn more using the links below. REGISTER HERE () Are you interested in partnering with Autism Health? During the month of July, organizations can receive 10% OFF all 2027 sponsorship packages by using promo code Sponsor10. This is the perfect opportunity to showcase your organization while supporting one of the nation's premier autism education conferences. REGISTER HERE () Join Our July Monthly Webinar We invite you to join us on Saturday, July 25th at 9:00 AM PST / 12:00 PM EST for an engaging and educational webinar featuring Dr. Basima Williams on Understanding the Impact of the Gut Microbiome on the Immune System. The gut microbiome plays a vital role in overall health, influencing immune function, inflammation, digestion, and neurological well being. During this presentation, Dr. Williams will explore the powerful relationship between the gut and the immune system, discuss emerging research, and explain why optimizing gut health is an important consideration for individuals with autism and other complex health conditions. Attendees will learn about: - The connection between the gut microbiome and immune function - How gut health can influence inflammation and overall wellness - The role of the microbiome in supporting neurological health - Practical strategies for promoting a healthy gut ecosystem - Current research and clinical insights into microbiome based care Whether you are a parent, caregiver, healthcare professional, or advocate, this webinar offers valuable information that can help you better understand one of the most important systems affecting overall health. Advance registration is required. Please register using the Zoom link below to reserve your spot. We look forward to seeing you online! REGISTER HERE () Summer Movie Fundraiser! Looking for a fun way to support Autism Health this summer? We are excited to partner with GroupRaise and Regal Cinemas for a special fundraising campaign that allows you to enjoy a night at the movies while supporting a great cause. For just $30 per order, you'll receive a Regal Movie Ticket Bundle that includes two Standard 2D Movie Tickets, redeemable at any Regal theater location nationwide. Best of all, 20% of every purchase will be donated to Autism Health Inc. to help support our educational programs, support groups, webinars, scholarships, and research initiatives. Did you know that many Regal Cinemas locations also offer Sensory Friendly Screenings? These special screenings are designed to create a more comfortable movie-going experience for individuals with autism and sensory sensitivities, making this fundraiser even more meaningful for our community. Whether you're planning a family outing, date night, or looking for a unique gift, your purchase helps advance our mission of serving individuals and families impacted by autism and related neurological conditions. Campaign Ends: Monday, August 17, 2026 Thank you for supporting Autism Health Inc. Every ticket bundle purchased helps us continue making a difference in the lives of families around the world. ## Protecting our kids online...
Thirteen.
That's the legal age kids can sign up for social media platforms under current law.
Thanks to a 1998 law passed when the internet was still in its infancy -- the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act -- kids essentially get unfettered access to everything the internet has to offer at just 13 years old.
Porn, adult content, toxic algorithms, and endless scrolling.
And that's to say nothing of the potential predators that they could run into on these platforms.
It's crazy when you think about it.
Thankfully, lawmakers are working to fix the problem.
I recently had IN Representative Erin Houchin on the show to talk about her efforts to pass the RESET Act.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3482fbcc-d117-4c84-ae46-64105a2a1e79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It would be a giant step in protecting our children, both physically and mentally.

# [ Millionaires flee New York, wiping out $11 billion in tax revenue
(and thats before Mamdani) ](https://substack.com/redirect/dddc8744-6086-4320-a358-4ccb1b9d6822?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
New York's **[share of the nation's millionaires fell from 12.7% to 8.7% between 2010 and 2022,](https://substack.com/redirect/a1e7e716-0874-4b45-a656-dda45b43731e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the largest decline of any state, causing roughly $10.7 billion less in personal income tax collections in 2022, a Citizen Budget Commission study found.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dddc8744-6086-4320-a358-4ccb1b9d6822?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Millionaire share declines:** New York's portion of US millionaires dropped sharply even as the state added 34,000 millionaires, but other states far outpaced growth with California tripling, Texas tripling and Florida quadrupling counts.
* **Tax revenue impact:** Had New York maintained its 2010 share of millionaires, personal income tax collections would have been substantially higher by roughly $10.7 billion in tax year 2022.
* **High earner reliance:** The top 1% of earners pay about 45% of all state income taxes, making New York revenue very reliant on wealthy taxpayers staying in the state.
* **Policy concerns rise:** Experts warn proposed tax hikes on the wealthy and the pied-a-terre tax could accelerate the exodus of high earners and businesses to states like Florida and Texas.

# [Warsh declares war on elevated inflation with zero tolerance vow](https://substack.com/redirect/fa91eaee-6f27-4189-a6be-8107c14e816f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh told House lawmakers **[the central bank has no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation](https://substack.com/redirect/f82d631f-b55c-47ee-82a0-d0f50cb07c14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and held the benchmark federal funds rate steady at 3.5% to 3.75% in June to restore price stability.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dd9acea1-29ab-4e55-be49-64786fdbd974?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Inflation policy priority:** Warsh emphasized the Fed's number one objective is to get monetary policy right so the inflation surge of the last five years becomes a thing of the past.
* **Rate decision context:** Inflation concerns influenced the decision to maintain the benchmark federal funds rate range at the June meeting.
* **Independence affirmed:** Warsh stressed the Federal Reserve is an independent central bank as affirmed by the Supreme Court with a goal for no politics in policy.
* **Price stability commitment:** Policymakers share a resolute commitment to restoring price stability as high inflation burdens American households and businesses.

# [IBM shares plunge 23% after brutal Q2 earnings miss](https://substack.com/redirect/fa91eaee-6f27-4189-a6be-8107c14e816f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
IBM stock **[cratered 23% Tuesday after the company warned preliminary second-quarter adjusted earnings](https://substack.com/redirect/eb31d897-47b7-43aa-8379-64a5bc1a5080?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of $2.93 per share on $17.2 billion revenue fell short of analyst expectations of $3.01 and $17.86 billion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fa91eaee-6f27-4189-a6be-8107c14e816f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Client spending shift:** Clients shifted quarterly capex toward servers storage and memory purchases to secure supply-constrained infrastructure ahead of expected price increases.
* **Software weakness cited:** CEO Arvind Krishna blamed weakness in software and infrastructure business with numerous large deals failing to close on expected timelines.
* **Execution shortfall:** Teams did not adapt and move quickly enough driving the majority of the shortfall despite some anticipated supply chain impact.
* **AI disruption fears:** The miss comes amid concerns that growth in artificial intelligence tools will disrupt businesses of major software companies.

# [Tim Scott grills Fed Chair Warsh on massive AI data center power demands](https://substack.com/redirect/fa91eaee-6f27-4189-a6be-8107c14e816f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Senate Banking Committee Chair Tim Scott said he wants Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh to address data centers and artificial intelligence including **[how such facilities pay for electricity and water use during Wednesday testimony.](https://substack.com/redirect/90db979a-fd1e-499d-907e-47854d73e1a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fa91eaee-6f27-4189-a6be-8107c14e816f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **AI conversation focus:** Scott wants to drill into the artificial intelligence discussion in South Carolina beyond the Fed dual mandate of price stability and employment.
* **Data centers pay way:** The real question is ensuring data centers pay their own way as it relates to electricity and water use amid growing moratoriums.
* **Global competition question:** Artificial intelligence will determine who wins the future between China or America requiring America to solve problems at home.
* **Utility bill recoil:** Some parties in South Carolina want to ban data centers driving AI due to increased utility bills for voters.

# [SpaceX alumni construction tech startup scores massive $115 million raise](https://substack.com/redirect/fa91eaee-6f27-4189-a6be-8107c14e816f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
TerraFirma a construction technology company[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/9213782c-3070-44aa-99db-e21f6adf631c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[founded by two former SpaceX engineers raised $115 million](https://substack.com/redirect/9213782c-3070-44aa-99db-e21f6adf631c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in funding to develop remote-controlled equipment using interfaces like Xbox controllers with long-term Mars ambitions.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fa91eaee-6f27-4189-a6be-8107c14e816f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Remote operation tech:** The Austin-based startup uses Xbox controllers and other interfaces to remotely operate construction equipment cutting costs and improving safety.
* **Funding investors:** Investments came from Kleiner Perkins Bain Capital Ventures SpaceX Anduril and Hadrian.
* **Expansion plans:** The money will hire 300 employees over the next year and build a Texas factory plus a mission control center.
* **SpaceX roots:** Founders Noah Schochet and Noah McGuinness worked at SpaceX on Starlink Starship and Starshield along with about half the engineering team from SpaceX Tesla and Boring Company.

# Frontier Airlines passengers get Starlink in 2027
Frontier Airlines **[will debut in-flight Wi-Fi early in 2027 using SpaceX Starlink satellite internet](https://substack.com/redirect/5cd618f0-9b42-4484-8f11-d16b92aeb4a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on its first equipped Airbus plane as the latest budget carrier to offer the service.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fa91eaee-6f27-4189-a6be-8107c14e816f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **No current Wi-Fi:** Frontier currently does not offer in-flight Wi-Fi and was one of the last major U.S. holdouts after hesitation over added plane weight.
* **Budget carrier group:** The deal covers Frontier Volaris Wizz Jetsmart and Cebu Pacific all sharing private equity firm Indigo Partners as investor with over 1,000 planes combined.
* **Global Starlink deals:** Starlink has signed with more than 40 carriers worldwide including United Airlines and American Airlines.
* **Upmarket shift:** Frontier plans to debut first-class seats next year amid pressure on budget carriers to enhance amenities.

# [World Cup semifinals spark massive last-minute travel rush to US cities](https://substack.com/redirect/fa91eaee-6f27-4189-a6be-8107c14e816f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Travel demand and spending in U.S. World Cup host cities **[is rising as semifinals approach](https://substack.com/redirect/23448ec9-5a8c-4ccd-9c05-c3439d0cf46d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with France versus Spain in Dallas and Argentina versus England in Atlanta driving late bookings and revenue gains.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fa91eaee-6f27-4189-a6be-8107c14e816f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Spending increases:** In-person spending in host cities rose 5% over last year from June 10 to July 5 with Kansas City leading gains according to Bank of America data.
* **Hotel performance:** Kansas City saw nearly 50% RevPAR increase while Philadelphia had weekend RevPAR up more than 74% during knockout matches.
* **Argentina fan surge:** Flight bookings from Argentina jumped nearly 46% year over year with Atlanta bookings more than doubling as fans respond in real time.
* **Knockout stage impact:** Demand increased 2.4% and RevPAR rose 23% in early knockout stages despite fewer matches as fans waited for matchups.

* * *
Donald Trump lost the 2020 election to Joe Biden and Kamala Harris because he was a shitty president. He wrecked the economy. He got people killed. He unleashed a pandemic across this country. He was corrupt as hell, and we were all sick of his shit. That's it. That's the whole story.
And yes -- he came back into power four years later because people were mad at the Democratic Party. Mad about the economy, mad about inflation, mad about how Joe Biden's aging was handled. I accept that. I've never pretended otherwise.
But you have to be a special kind of stupid to believe that Democrats were capable of rigging the election in 2020 and somehow incapable of rigging it in 2024. You have to be a special kind of stupid to think we could pull off stealing an election across fifty states -- leaving basically no evidence, because there is no evidence -- but we can't manage to get a damn thing we actually want done in Washington.
It's the perfect distillation of what Trump's second term has become, of what the Republican Party and the MAGA movement have become: a party fueled purely by grievance.
Donald Trump is not serving as president on behalf of the American people. If he were, he'd be spending his time helping you afford your grocery bill. Helping you buy a house. Helping you take a vacation -- the things that make up the core of the American dream. Not waging stupid wars so he can manipulate markets and profiteer off them. Not stealing billions from the American people. And certainly not lingering on an election from 2020 that he lost fairly and that has been litigated to death. He lost every single court case he brought. Every one.
The truth is that Donald Trump should be in prison right now for attempting to incite an insurrection and overthrow our elections. But we don't live in a country where somebody as rich and powerful as Donald Trump ever gets held accountable for his crimes. If he'd been held accountable at any point in his life, he never would have made it to the presidency in 2016.
No -- this is a revenge tour. The only thing Trump cares about in his second term is getting even with every single person he believes ever wronged him. That's why he's going after Jimmy Kimmel and trying to get him pulled off the air. That's why he's trying to lock up Don Lemon for reporting something he didn't like. That's why he's stealing so much -- because he never had the wealth he actually wanted, the lifestyle he wanted. He was always jealous of the New York social elite who wouldn't let him into their clubs, wouldn't invest with him, wouldn't party with him -- because they knew he was a creep. That's why he spent all his time with Jeffrey Epstein instead.

* * *
Here's the thing that makes it genuinely disturbing: he can't even enjoy winning. He's won two presidential elections -- fairly, I believe. Democrats gave him plenty of legs up along the way, but that's not cheating. That's just us being bad at our jobs. And still, the 2020 loss eats him alive. It drives him crazy.
And it's electorally idiotic. Nobody outside the MAGA cult believes anything he says about 2020. The polling is clear. The American people want to hear their president talk about the economy, or the war he started, or literally any problem that actually touches their lives. Instead, he has large parts of the federal government working overtime to prove a lie -- stealing ballots in Georgia, trying to pry open state voter rolls. Maybe if Donald Trump spent less time on stupid shit like proving an election was stolen when it wasn't, and more time doing things that would improve your life, we'd be in a fundamentally stronger position as a nation. He had a chance at the start of this term to reset American politics. He doubled down on the stupid shit instead, because he simply cannot get out of his own way.
He is a bad human being. He is bad for our democracy. And everybody of good conscience -- everybody who lives in reality -- needs to speak out about whatever he says on Thursday, because we already know it's going to be bullshit. How do I know? His lips will be moving. Everything Donald Trump says is more or less a lie, and when he stumbles onto a truth, it's usually one that's uncomfortable for him and his movement.
He knows he lost. He just can't let it go. So he's trying to rewrite history -- and more importantly, trying to create the conditions where people doubt the outcome of the midterms in November. Because the same reason he lost in 2020 is the same reason he's going to lose in November: he's a bad president, he got people killed, and people are furious about the economy. Politics is not complicated.
He'll try to steal it anyway. That's why he's pushing the SAVE Act to make it harder to register to vote. That's why they're stealing ballots. That's why they're gerrymandering in the middle of the decade, which is more or less unheard of. They will bend and twist every rule, and they will lie and cheat and steal to win the midterms.
So we have to build a wave too big for them to rig.
Period. End of story.

_**By Eric J. Lullove, DPM, CWSP, MAPWCA, FFPM RCPS(Glasg)
** Contributing Medical Editor, Blue Amp Media_
To every Michigan resident heading into the August 4 Democratic Senate primary: Read this one carefully, because it lives in my professional lane. And before anyone files it under "partisan attack," understand what this piece is and isn't. It is not an endorsement of anyone. It is not a case for a party. It is a case for a _process_ --the same credentialing process every licensed clinician in this country is held to, applied without regard to whose name is on the ballot.
This week, Mehdi Hasan--no conservative, and by his own record a broadly sympathetic interviewer of this candidate--asked a question most reporters wouldn't touch. Abdul El-Sayed has repeatedly called himself a _physician_. Yet he holds no valid state medical license in New York or Michigan. Hasan pressed the obvious follow-up: Did you tell the truth? El-Sayed didn't answer it. He pivoted--to your child's education, to his tenure as Detroit's health director, to the claim that he's eliminated more medical debt than "most doctors." He then pointed to his diploma, noting he graduated from a school literally called Columbia College of Physicians and Surgeons, and suggested anyone with a problem could take it up with the university.
That the questioner was an ally is the whole point. When the person most inclined to give a candidate the benefit of the doubt still must stop and ask whether the biography is accurate, the issue has left the realm of partisanship and entered the realm of fact. And in my field, it's a serious fact.
#### **Why I Get to Say This to Michigan**
Let me be clear about my standing to write these words to this state, because it matters. I grew up in Michigan. I graduated from high school there and earned my college degree there. My roots are still in that ground--family, friends, and a set of values I carry into every exam room and every hearing to this day. I am not a stranger parachuting in with an opinion about a place I've never lived. When I address Michigan voters, I address them as one of their own, with the standing that comes from having been shaped by that community.
That is precisely why I can make these statements with the phrasing I'm using. I know what Michigan expects of the people who serve it, because Michigan is where I learned it. The state raised me on the idea that your word and your credentials should match. This isn't a lecture from the outside. It's a message from someone who came up in the same places these voters did, asking them to hold to the same standard the rest of us were taught there.
#### **A Diploma Is Not a License**
Let me draw the line cleanly, because I've spent a career on the credentialing side of medicine--in audit rooms and appeals hearings where the difference between a degree and a license is the whole case. This line does not move for Democrats or Republicans. It does not move for candidates I might vote for or against. It is fixed.
Abdul El-Sayed earned a Doctor of Medicine degree. That is real, and it is not nothing. But an MD is an academic credential--proof you completed medical school. A **license** is something entirely different. It is a state's active grant of authority to practice medicine, issued only after residency training, board examination, and ongoing accountability to a licensing board that can suspend or revoke it. The public record shows El-Sayed has never held a medical license in Michigan or New York. He has the diploma. He does not have the license.
The word _physician_ is the license word. It signals to a patient, a voter, a hospital, or a court that the state stands behind you and that a board can hold you to account. It is not a synonym for "went to medical school." It is not a vibe. It is a legally regulated title, and both states in question say so in statute--statutes written by legislatures of both parties, enforced against members of both parties, and neutral on their face.

Friend, This year is shaping up to be one of the most important election cycles in recent memory. Voters across the country are facing an unprecedented wave of bills designed to make it harder to cast a ballot. State legislatures in over 20 states have introduced measures to restrict early voting, limit mail-in ballots, and add barriers that disproportionately affect everyday Americans. Things aren’t any better in Washington, friend. Anti-voting lawmakers in Congress have tried to ram through legislation designed to make it harder to vote — including the SAVE Act, which would require Americans registering to vote to provide documents that millions don’t readily have. And conservative justices on the Supreme Court can’t be trusted, either. Peter, Let's be honest about what Donald Trump has done to this country. He has weaponized the government against its own people, hollowed out our institutions, enabled ICE to brutalize our communities, and stripped our country for parts to be sold to the highest bidder in order to enrich himself. Perhaps worst of all, he has made cruelty his policy. The costs of all of this are real — we see them in rising prices, in the loss of our civil liberties, and in the fear that too many Americans are living with on a daily basis. name: Kathryn Harvey
subject: 🗳️What's next for Dr. Annie Andrews Senate Campaign?
body:
📣Meet Annie at Miles with the Mayor this Saturday at 8am.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/b6f17ebb66db/kathryn-harvey-for-congresscampaign-kickoff-6426663?e=edbde6c9b1)
---
|
---
|
---
| | [**Support our ten Spartanburg State House Candidates with one contribution.**](https://us.list-manage.com/lxl_qlTVgsL?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)[**Read our July Newsletter**](https://us.list-manage.com/1CVVxfn5veG?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
---
| |
# Life is so much bigger than politics.
---
| |
After the sudden passing of longtime Senator Lindsey Graham a rapid fire Republican Primary contest for his seat has begun. Yesterday, Governor McMaster announced the appointment of Darlene Graham, Lindsey’s sister, as the interim Senator to fill his seat through January 3, 2027. This turn of events has catapulted Dr. Andrews, our Democratic Nominee for Senate, into the spotlight. Listen to her message and read how her race in transforming.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/nyrPeNp2WRs?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
| [Listen to Annie’s message](https://us.list-manage.com/m90Alv5zlF1?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/gfvZ4TQ9YHj?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
| |
# What this means for Dr. Andrews campaign
---
| |
**You can’t gerrymander an entire state.** South Carolina isn’t a red or blue state - it’s a non-voting state. We already know the majority of independents in South Carolina are looking for something else to vote for other than Republicans who are hitching themselves to Trump and his agenda. And boy, do we have a ballot full of options. Dr. Andrews and our other statewide candidates also have the energy of 124 house candidates pulling votes from every district in SC to the top of the ticket.
**And nevermind that she is the most disciplined candidate I’ve ever worked with.**
Her core message doesn’t change. She’s been focusing on key issues that impact the majority of South Carolinians (like healthcare) since day one, and that’s what she’ll continue to do.
---
| |
-She will no longer be challenging a 20+ year incumbent.-She handily won the Democratic Primary with 61% of the vote.-She has considerable name recognition and money in the bank.-None of the potential Republican Challengers will come close to Lindsey’s name ID.-Republicans will have to spend a considerable amount of funds in the knock down drag out special election, and whomever comes limping out will have only two months to run.-She will continue to run a disciplined race that focuses on the needs of our state.\- This could be a perfect storm.
---
| |
# Come meet Annie this Saturday in Spartanburg at Miles with the Mayor 8am - 180 Magnolia St.
---
|
---
| |
# Here’s what comes next.
---
| |
-Filing period for US Senate Republican Primary**July 21 to July 28** -Early Voting **August 5-7** -Special statewide Republican primary election Tuesday, **August 11** -Republican Primary runoff Tuesday, **August 25** -General election voter registration deadline **October 4** -Early voting **October 19 - 30** -Election Day Tuesday, **November 3**
[**You can find information on all the candidates in August on the South Carolina Voter Guide.**](https://us.list-manage.com/IjlVFEVyDmn?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/T2YGNRvUtzf?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
| |
# Check out our latest pod on the SC Senate Race
---
| |
Lindsey Graham's sudden death has reshaped South Carolina politics overnight. We discuss what happens next, who could replace him in the U.S. Senate, how the special election process works, and why this moment could change the future of South Carolina politics. We also look at the Republican primary field, the implications for Annie Andrews' campaign, and what voters should expect in the months ahead. The race for Lindsey Graham's Senate seat is already underway, and the decisions made over the next few weeks could shape South Carolina politics for years to come.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/pxDeJCDTeUZ?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
| |
# The election breakdown with Bakari Sellers
---
| |

Bakari Sellers joined me to break down the 2026 South Carolina elections, what the primary results revealed, and why building a competitive Democratic Party is a long term strategy rather than a single election cycle. We discuss the senate campaign, legislative races, fundraising, voter turnout, candidate recruitment, and what it will take to compete statewide over the next decade.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/kYzs8paYpbb?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
|
---
| |
# Meet the Democratic women running in 2026 on Aug 20!
---
| | If you live in Spartanburg County you’ll have women to vote for on your ballot from County Council to the US Senate. Join us on Thursday, August 20th at Party Headquarters to meet these trailblazers, learn about their campaigns, and how you can best support them. Tickets will go on sale next week. This event is hosted by the Spartanburg County Democratic Party and proceeds will benefit our Get Out The Vote efforts in 2026.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/wG6A37XYCsE?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
|
---
|
---
| |
**The SC Legislature failed to pass a budget. That’s it. That’s the whole post.**
Fourteen days without a state budget. That's unacceptable. Republicans control South Carolina's government, and they have no excuses. After decades of one-party rule, they still failed to do one of their most basic jobs. South Carolinians deserve leaders who will put our state first.
---
| [Support our candidates today!](https://us.list-manage.com/wAXeoFemctq?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)

|

| |
* **July 16**[**Virtual Phone Bank Training at 6pm**](https://us.list-manage.com/k42_dwUD7M2?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
* **July 23** [**Poll Watcher Training at 6pm**](https://us.list-manage.com/Kuda66P3SwT?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
* **July 30** Car Canvassing with Saville Williams HD 34 & Virginia McClean HD 36 at 10:00am
* **Aug 3** SPCDP Meeting 6pm TK Gregg Center: Youth Voices Panel
* **Aug 3** Spartanburg County Delegation Meeting 5:30pm
* **Aug 20** Meet the Dem Women Running for Office in Spartanburg 6pm Party HQ
* **Aug 27** Pacolet Town Hall with Lekesa Whitner and Courtney McClain
* **Sept 14** SPCDP Meeting: Dr. Jermaine Johnson for Governor

The earthquakes in Venezuela dominated the news for a matter of days. The collapsed buildings, the death toll, the rescue teams pulling survivors from the rubble, **the world watched, then largely moved on.** But for the children left behind, the danger didn't end when the ground stopped shaking. **In some ways, it was only the beginning.** Displacement does something traffickers understand better than almost anyone. It breaks the systems that normally protect a child -- records, schools, familiar faces, parents who never let go of their hand. In that broken space, a stranger offering "help," a ride, a promise of safety somewhere else, can be all it takes for a child to disappear.

I've sat with survivors. I've heard what it costs a family to lose a child this way, and what it takes to bring one home. And I've learned that disasters like the one in Venezuela don't create new evil, they simply hand existing evil an opening it has used again and again. If this is the first time you're hearing from me, my name is Eduardo Verastegui, and I produced the film Sound of Freedom. The film Sound of Freedom was truly a movie that launched a movement. That movement is now. Our mission at the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** is to **stop the sale of God's children.** We do that through five pillars:
---
* **Prevention**
* **Intervention**
* **Education**
* **Information**
* **Influence**

---
We are working urgently, with trusted partners on the ground, to:
---
* Find children who have already fallen into trafficking, including exploitation happening online in the chaos of the disaster.
* Support rescue operations that bring a child out of danger and into safety.
* Provide a safe bed the moment a child is free.
* Fund reunification when a family can be found and verified.
* Walk alongside a child through long-term care when there is nowhere safe to send them yet.

clean_body: After the earthquakes in Venezuela, traffickers are already moving. Here's how we're responding. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Friend, The earthquakes in Venezuela dominated the news for a matter of days. The collapsed buildings, the death toll, the rescue teams pulling survivors from the rubble, the world watched, then largely moved on. But for the children left behind, the danger didn't end when the ground stopped shaking. In some ways, it was only the beginning. Displacement does something traffickers understand better than almost anyone. It breaks the systems that normally protect a child -- records, schools, familiar faces, parents who never let go of their hand. In that broken space, a stranger offering "help," a ride, a promise of safety somewhere else, can be all it takes for a child to disappear. We've set an urgent goal to raise $50,000 in the next 30 days to help rescue children, provide safe shelter, and reunite families before more children disappear into trafficking. Every gift brings us one step closer.Will you help us reach this lifesaving goal today? I've sat with survivors. I've heard what it costs a family to lose a child this way, and what it takes to bring one home. And I've learned that disasters like the one in Venezuela don't create new evil, they simply hand existing evil an opening it has used again and again. If this is the first time you're hearing from me, my name is Eduardo Verastegui, and I produced the film Sound of Freedom. The film Sound of Freedom was truly a movie that launched a movement. That movement is now. Our mission at the Sound of Freedom Foundation is to stop the sale of God's children. We do that through five pillars: Prevention Intervention Education Information Influence We are working urgently, with trusted partners on the ground, to: Find children who have already fallen into trafficking, including exploitation happening online in the chaos of the disaster. Support rescue operations that bring a child out of danger and into safety. Provide a safe bed the moment a child is free. Fund reunification when a family can be found and verified. Walk alongside a child through long-term care when there is nowhere safe to send them yet. "Defend the weak and the fatherless; uphold the cause of the poor and the oppressed. Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked." (Psalm 82:3-4) That command is what guides every decision this Foundation makes. It is not a suggestion. It is not poetry. It is an instruction, and I take it as one. We're trusting God to help us raise $50,000 in the next 30 days, but He often answers prayers through people willing to act. I hope you'll be one of them today. Friend, I am asking you urgently, humbly, and personally to make your first gift today. Please do not wait. For God's children, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. Right now, a displaced child in Venezuela is being watched by someone who does not have their best interest at heart. Your gift today helps make sure someone who does gets there first. 6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074

body:
Don't Let Trump Eliminate Media Freedom
| | | | |
---
| | | **[Sign: Disbar and Prosecute the Officials Behind Trump’s Reporter Subpoenas](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tff5bf1da-010e-4361-a8ea-ed41afb36767/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** Donald Trump's Justice Department has [subpoenaed](https://default.salsalabs.org/T87fde90a-aa5d-4ec0-90d5-044e85f45330/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) four _New York Times_ reporters after they exposed security concerns involving his Qatari-provided Air Force One. [**Federal agents even delivered some of the subpoenas to the reporters' homes, in what appears to be an attempt to intimidate them.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tdae226f0-8474-4e99-a0be-bb6d8cce1bd5/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) **This is not normal law enforcement. It looks like an effort to frighten journalists, expose their sources and punish reporting that embarrasses the president. These subpoenas threaten freedom of the press, the public's right to know and the First Amendment itself.** Officials who abuse federal power must know that consequences can follow them long after their boss leaves office. If they broke the law, they should be prosecuted and, if convicted, sent to prison. State bar authorities should act even sooner, investigating the lawyers involved and disbarring any who violated their professional duties. [**Add your name: Disbar and prosecute the officials behind Trump's reporter subpoenas.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T5093020f-1af1-4054-b7a8-2c4356785223/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

name: Noelle Dorward
subject: See what’s possible for damaged forests →
body:
You know that feeling of a job well done? When you’ve used a skill to the best of your ability, and you feel like you’ve just tapped into your superpower?

As the Redwoods Rising Partnership Manager, I have the unique honor of seeing Save the Redwoods, California State Parks, and the National Park Service combine their superpowers to reach our common goal: to heal the scars left by decades of industrial logging and revive 70,000 acres of second-growth redwood forest.

Each year, scientists, conservationists, equipment operators, local businesses, budget wranglers, and restoration experts collaborate to restore hundreds of acres of dense forest and remove miles of failing logging roads to ensure a brighter future for the forest, for local communities, and for you.

That collaboration also involves local communities along the North Coast, bringing sustainable, high-paying jobs to areas with high unemployment. Redwoods Rising has created growth opportunities within the North Coast natural resource job market, with staff and former apprentices advancing to new roles within Redwoods Rising and other local restoration projects.

This depth of knowledge and passion is why we can be ambitious and give a second life to forest ecosystems that would once have been considered a lost cause.

Your support is an important piece of this puzzle and helps us ramp up restoration work, hire Redwood Rising Apprentices, and make the most of the summer restoration season. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM12&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

Save the Redwoods League National Parks Service

California State Parks + YOU!

DONATE NOW [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM12&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

You don’t need to be an expert to help restore these forests. You just have to care. Donor support is a crucial piece of this puzzle, allowing us to navigate uncertainties and maintain momentum on science-driven restoration work. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM12&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

The redwood forests of the future need us, now. Together, I know we won’t let them down.

Yours in partnership,
Noelle Dorward
Redwoods Rising Partnership Manager

P.S. We have an important funding deadline coming up on July 31. If you want to be part of bringing these damaged forests back to life, please make your gift now! subject: We Cannot Accept ICE’s Violence As Normal
body:
Recent Shootings Are A Reminder That It’s Time For Change

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/elizabethforvirginia/we-cannot-accept-ices-violence-as-normal?e=2f83c585b2)

|
---
|

| | | | | |
# _We Cannot Accept ICE’s Violence As Normal. It’s Time For Change._
---
| |
**The last week has been heartbreaking.**
**In Texas, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo \- a father, husband, and small business owner - was fatally shot by an ICE agent during an enforcement operation. ****Just days later, in Maine, 26-year-old Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, a Colombian national who was authorized to work in the United States, was shot and killed by an ICE agent during another operation. **
**These are not isolated incidents.**
**It has been less than two years under the Trump administration, and we've already seen a disturbing pattern of escalating immigration enforcement and violence. With renewed intensity over the past year, we've watched families separated, communities terrorized, and lives forever changed. We've mourned people like Renee Good and Alex Pretti, whose stories have become symbols of a system that has failed to protect human dignity and public trust. **
**These recent shootings are not disconnected tragedies; they are the latest reminders of what happens when an agency is allowed to operate without accountability. **
**Every person - regardless of where they were born - deserves dignity, due process, and humane treatment under the law. When government agents use deadly force, the public deserves accountability, transparency, and answers.**
**That's why I am proud to call for the abolition of ICE.**
**I know "abolish" is a strong word. But so is the violence we're seeing today. So is the fear that spreads through immigrant communities every time masked officers arrive in unmarked vehicles. So is the trauma inflicted on children who watch their parents disappear. So is the loss of life that has become far too common.**
**Calling to abolish ICE does not mean just opening our borders. It does not mean abandoning immigration enforcement. But the agency we have today has become too plagued by abuse, excessive force, and a lack of accountability to simply tweak around the edges. At some point, reform is no longer enough.****We need to dismantle the current agency and rebuild our immigration enforcement from the ground up.**
**That means reallocating resources into a system rooted in justice, professionalism, transparency, and respect for human rights. It means investing in trained personnel, meaningful oversight, and due process.**
**America is strongest when our laws reflect both justice and humanity.****We can have secure borders without cruelty. We can enforce immigration laws without fear becoming the policy. And we can build an immigration system worthy of the country we aspire to be.**
**That's the future I'm fighting for. I hope you'll join me.****— Elizabeth**

# 6 stops, 5 days, 1 very large district

Peter,When I got into this thing, I told you I was going to stay rooted right here.
This district covers close to 19,000 square miles, which makes it bigger than the whole country of Denmark, and the only honest way to run in a place like that is to actually drive it.
That was true when I was one guy standing on a corner in New Richmond with a sign, and it is true now with a debate on television.
You put the miles in.
You show up where people already are, and you listen to what they tell you.The next five days are about as good an example of that as I can give you.
Here is where I will be:
**TONIGHT: Tuesday, July 14, WJFW Candidate Debate, Rhinelander.** Five to 6:30 pm, live on WJFW and streaming on their website.
**Wednesday, July 15, WJMT Radio, Merrill.** Laura Bergh has me on the Bluejay 96.3 Morning Show at 7:45 am to talk about this campaign. Grab your coffee and tune in.
**Wednesday, July 15, Wisconsin Farm Tech Days, Stratford.** From 9 am to 4 pm, you'll find me at Redetzke's No Joke Dairy, in Booth 328 with the WisDems Rural Caucus.
Come talk farming with me. I want to hear it straight from the people living it.
**Thursday, July 16, BADD Candidate Forum, Brule.** Six to 8 pm at the Brule Town Hall with the Brule Area Defenders of Democracy.
**Friday, July 17, St. Croix County Fair, Glenwood City.** Three to 9 pm in the Commercial Building with the St. Croix County Dems.
**Saturday, July 18, Honor the Earth Powwow, Hayward.** Ten to 6 pm at the Lac Courte Oreilles powwow grounds, at the Sawyer and LCO Dems tent.
