## 3 More Weeks to Go:
## A Moment of Reflection & A Call to Action
---
Speaking with voters at the Pulaski Candidate Forum who were very interested to learn about all the candidates.
As we enter the final weeks before the August 4 Democratic primary, I am thinking about how far this campaign has come and what remains to be done. Early voting is already underway, and every conversation, every door knocked, and every hour volunteered now matters even more.
This campaign has always been about the people of Virginia’s Ninth Congressional District. It is about families who work hard but still struggle to keep up with rising costs. It is about communities that deserve accessible healthcare, reliable infrastructure, affordable energy, good schools, and jobs that help young people establish a future close to home.
It means ensuring that no one in Southwest Virginia falls through the gaps that have become chasms through decades of neglect. We need another New Deal. Hollers, coal camps, towns, farms, and cities: there is no part of SWVA that does not deserve world-class resources and the tools to build communities up and keep our kids here, our families close.
I am _deeply_ grateful to the volunteers who have made this campaign possible. Over two hundred people actively drive our grassroots effort, helping us canvass neighborhoods, make phone calls, organize events, and reach voters across the district. Together, we have visited every county in the Ninth District SWVA many times and reached hundreds of doors, gas stations, grocery stores, and community centers. That work represents more than campaign activity. It represents a belief that democracy is strongest when ordinary people step up, listen to one another, and take responsibility for their communities.As of today, we are over 15k direct voters contacted, and hundreds of thousands more via billboards and other passive ads, all thanks to your direct support.
I am also thankful for the opportunity to campaign alongside two other Democratic candidates. We are competitors in this primary, and we have real differences in our backgrounds, approaches, and policies. Yet both have brought important perspectives to this race. Our forums have given voters an opportunity to hear those perspectives directly and compare how each of us would serve the district.
---
Those forums have covered difficult and consequential issues, including economic-related development, affordable housing, student debt, healthcare, energy costs, and the rapid expansion of data centers. I have argued that Southwest Virginia needs stronger federal standards for data centers’ water use, power consumption, and noise. I have also emphasized that our region must create high-paying jobs that provide dignified lives and give young people a reason to stay, while the federal government works with regional organizations to expand housing for working families, young people who want to stay local, and seniors who want to stay in their communities.
Not every moment of this primary has been easy. It has been a wild ride, full of many ups and some downs as we navigated the political arena. Some of those moments have received more attention than the issues affecting voters every day. Still, we are proud to say we have stayed positive and managed distractions in line with the rules & ethical standards.
Democracy is not always comfortable. It brings together people with different experiences, personalities, and ideas, and it asks us to compete without losing sight of our common responsibility. We can disagree firmly while still recognizing one another and our desire to represent the Ninth District. We can hold ourselves and one another accountable while remembering that our ultimate obligation is to the people we seek to serve.
When this primary is over, Democrats, independents, and Republicans of conscience must be prepared to come together. The larger challenge is defeating Morgan Griffith and the Trump-aligned politics he represents. Griffith has held this seat for 16 years, yet too many people across the district still feel overlooked, unheard, and left behind. We will not change that by allowing a hard-fought primary to permanently divide us. The winds of change will push us all the same way if we but let them.
---
Celebrating Juneteenth with Rev. Jackie Nophlin and organizers in Bristol.
The people of the Ninth District deserve representation that belongs to them, not to corporate interests, billionaire donors, special interests, or party insiders relying on NOVA supporters. They deserve a representative who will listen in every county, show up in every community, and fight for healthcare as a human right, lower costs, better jobs, stronger public services, and a twenty-first-century economy that fuels Southwest Virginia.
_I believe that I am the best person to provide that representation._
I bring the perspective of someone who understands what it means for a family to struggle through great loss due to medical debt and financial industry disasters. I know what it means to see people fall through the gaps in systems that were supposed to protect them. I also bring the technical and professional experience to understand the economic changes already changing our communities. Most importantly, I am pledged to putting people first and solving problems together with the people of SWVA.
But no candidate can do this **alone**. Campaigns succeed because people decide that the future is worth their time, their effort, and their courage. _**If you believe the Ninth District deserves a representative who will fight for everyone, I ask you to step forward during these final three weeks and help us finish strong.**_
---
Join us by signing up here: www.murphy4va.com/volunteer.
Volunteer to canvass. Make phone calls. Talk with your neighbors. Share our message in person or reshare it on social media. Help voters make a plan to cast their vote.
**If you have been waiting for the right moment to get involved, this is that moment.**
Thank you to every volunteer, supporter, voter, and community member who has welcomed us, challenged us, communicated a story, or offered encouragement. And for those who can donate in these tough times, your money has been spent on materials and expenses, not consultants and gala events. I feel hopeful because I have seen the strength, generosity, and determination of the people of Southwest Virginia.
Democracy requires participation. Let us finish this primary with purpose, come together afterward, and push forward with everything we have. Because the Ninth District belongs to its people, together we can guarantee that its representation does too.
**Here’s to a Future We All Deserve!**

We can hold ourselves and one another accountable while remembering that our ultimate obligation is to the people we seek to serve. When this primary is over, Democrats, independents, and Republicans of conscience must be prepared to come together. The larger challenge is defeating Morgan Griffith and the Trump-aligned politics he represents. Griffith has held this seat for 16 years, yet too many people across the district still feel overlooked, unheard, and left behind. We will not change that by allowing a hard-fought primary to permanently divide us. The winds of change will push us all the same way if we but let them. Celebrating Juneteenth with Rev. Jackie Nophlin and organizers in Bristol. The people of the Ninth District deserve representation that belongs to them, not to corporate interests, billionaire donors, special interests, or party insiders relying on NOVA supporters. They deserve a representative who will listen in every county, show up in every community, and fight for healthcare as a human right, lower costs, better jobs, stronger public services, and a twenty-first-century economy that fuels Southwest Virginia. I believe that I am the best person to provide that representation. I bring the perspective of someone who understands what it means for a family to struggle through great loss due to medical debt and financial industry disasters. I know what it means to see people fall through the gaps in systems that were supposed to protect them. I also bring the technical and professional experience to understand the economic changes already changing our communities. Most importantly, I am pledged to putting people first and solving problems together with the people of SWVA. But no candidate can do this alone. Campaigns succeed because people decide that the future is worth their time, their effort, and their courage. If you believe the Ninth District deserves a representative who will fight for everyone, I ask you to step forward during these final three weeks and help us finish strong. Join us by signing up here: www.murphy4va.com/volunteer. Volunteer to canvass. Make phone calls. Talk with your neighbors. Share our message in person or reshare it on social media. Help voters make a plan to cast their vote. If you have been waiting for the right moment to get involved, this is that moment. Thank you to every volunteer, supporter, voter, and community member who has welcomed us, challenged us, communicated a story, or offered encouragement. And for those who can donate in these tough times, your money has been spent on materials and expenses, not consultants and gala events. I feel hopeful because I have seen the strength, generosity, and determination of the people of Southwest Virginia. Democracy requires participation. Let us finish this primary with purpose, come together afterward, and push forward with everything we have. Because the Ninth District belongs to its people, together we can guarantee that its representation does too. body:
https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,
I just returned from Palestine, where I spent several days meeting with families about the daily realities of life under occupation.
https://x.com/RoKhanna/status/2076675686916354109 [https://x.com/RoKhanna/status/2076675686916354109]
While visiting a Palestinian school that had been burned down by settlers, my staff and I were surrounded by armed settlers carrying American-made M4 rifles. They blocked our vehicle, called in reinforcements, mocked us, and held us against our will for more than an hour.
When Israeli soldiers arrived, I expected them to stop the settlers. Instead, they protected them.
I was eventually allowed to leave because I'm an American member of Congress. Millions of Palestinians don't have that privilege.
If violent settlers and the Israeli military could do this to an American congressman, imagine what Palestinian families endure every day—with no cameras, no headlines, and no one to speak up for them.
Throughout this trip, I met people who had lost loved ones, been driven from their land, and were struggling for the most basic human rights: safety, freedom of movement, and the dignity to live in peace.
For too long, their voices have been ignored.
There must be consequences for violent extremism and continued settlement expansion.
* Designate the Hilltop Youth as a terrorist group,
* Prosecute violent settlers like Yinon Levy, and
* Halt all settlement construction in the occupied West Bank
Will you join me and demand that the United States take action to urge Israel to act? [https://act.rokhanna.com/a/idf-hilltop-youth-petition?contactdata=34Ke23PGbmexJd9NHUuj/DpOsb89PCkhixYJvabTdZ9T79waWssNjEFWFvlk6vpPOsxWeGoaNfPi+TcIhPKhch4WNTENPih1ONp17wv7bAPHdBULH0vRcUrvPwMTM4bG3gABFmPM7ZUTezeBgEMw740DTDIociA9gjDgpzw5xOAiap46VK6lsz9Csx6w5Lcr]

I won't be silenced about what I witnessed in Palestine. I'll continue sharing the stories I heard over the coming weeks because Americans deserve to know what is happening. But today, I'm asking you to stand with people who are simply demanding equal rights, accountability, and the chance to live with dignity.
Thank you for your support, your activism, and all that you do.
Onward,
Ro

name: Wes Moore
subject: Conversations
body:
What I saw in that room.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1619%2E1086043%2EwqmxVi)
A few weeks ago, I sat down for Jubilee’s _Surrounded_ and debated with 20 people who had not voted in the last election.
**The cynics out there in the world tell us a conversation like the one I had isn’t worth having.** That we’ve become too divided. That everyone has already chosen a side, and the only thing left to do is shout louder than our political opponents.
But that isn’t what I saw in that room. And I do not think it is true in this country. We haven’t crossed a threshold where we can no longer listen to one another or to work together.
Shortly after we’ve celebrated America’s 250th anniversary, I’m struck by the fact that our nation’s story has never been one of perfection. It’s one of progress. Generation after generation, Americans have chosen to do their part in expanding the promise of this country.
That work has never been automatic. It has always required participation from people who believe that tomorrow can be better than today.
**[If you share that belief with me, I would appreciate a donation to our re-election campaign today so we can continue our work.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260714-1.z8E4Dy&refcode=em-20260714-1&t=2&akid=1619%2E1086043%2EwqmxVi)**
I did not go into _Surrounded_ – or write this – to shame people who have opted out of the system.
Quite the contrary. I understand that choice.
I don’t come from a political background. When I ran for office the first time a few years ago, I had to convince many of my family members to vote for me. It’s not like we aren’t cool. They just don’t rush to the ballot box every year.
It struck me that people I love – people who cared deeply about their communities and their country – had been absent from a democratic act that generations of Americans fought for.
Somewhere along the way, they stopped believing that politics had much to do with them – or that anyone in politics had much interest in them. That realization has stayed with me. And it is exactly why I did _Surrounded._
Democracy is a relationship. Those who have the privilege of serving in government share a responsibility to give people a reason to believe their participation counts. To earn their trust. To show the public that government is not something that happens to us, but something we have the power to shape. As an elected official, I take that responsibility seriously. It’s sacred, and essential.
If those of us in public office do our jobs right, then voting becomes about more than casting a ballot. It is an act of hope.
If we’re serious about strengthening democracy over the next 250 years, we cannot only invest in elections. _We have to invest in one another._ The work of patriotism is not passive, and it is not performative. It is service.
Real patriotism asks us to see our humanity in each other before we see our differences. It asks us to remember that the future of this country has always depended on ordinary people doing extraordinary things together – not because they agreed on everything, but because they believed this nation was worth building together, despite our disagreements.

clean_body: What I saw in that room. A few weeks ago, I sat down for Jubilee’s Surrounded and debated with 20 people who had not voted in the last election. The cynics out there in the world tell us a conversation like the one I had isn’t worth having. That we’ve become too divided. That everyone has already chosen a side, and the only thing left to do is shout louder than our political opponents. But that isn’t what I saw in that room. And I do not think it is true in this country. We haven’t crossed a threshold where we can no longer listen to one another or to work together. Shortly after we’ve celebrated America’s 250th anniversary, I’m struck by the fact that our nation’s story has never been one of perfection. It’s one of progress. Generation after generation, Americans have chosen to do their part in expanding the promise of this country. That work has never been automatic. It has always required participation from people who believe that tomorrow can be better than today. I did not go into Surrounded – or write this – to shame people who have opted out of the system. Quite the contrary. I understand that choice. I don’t come from a political background. When I ran for office the first time a few years ago, I had to convince many of my family members to vote for me. It’s not like we aren’t cool. They just don’t rush to the ballot box every year. It struck me that people I love – people who cared deeply about their communities and their country – had been absent from a democratic act that generations of Americans fought for. Somewhere along the way, they stopped believing that politics had much to do with them – or that anyone in politics had much interest in them. That realization has stayed with me. And it is exactly why I did Surrounded. Democracy is a relationship. Those who have the privilege of serving in government share a responsibility to give people a reason to believe their participation counts. To earn their trust. To show the public that government is not something that happens to us, but something we have the power to shape. As an elected official, I take that responsibility seriously. It’s sacred, and essential. If those of us in public office do our jobs right, then voting becomes about more than casting a ballot. It is an act of hope. If we’re serious about strengthening democracy over the next 250 years, we cannot only invest in elections. We have to invest in one another. The work of patriotism is not passive, and it is not performative. It is service. Real patriotism asks us to see our humanity in each other before we see our differences. It asks us to remember that the future of this country has always depended on ordinary people doing extraordinary things together – not because they agreed on everything, but because they believed this nation was worth building together, despite our disagreements. My final challenge is a simple one: Sit down with people in your life and in your community who disagree with you. Have honest conversations. Listen. You may be surprised by what you find. And you may even end up working together to make a big difference in our world. Elevate, Wes

body:

Hi friend — I was at an event in Warwick recently, and I got into a conversation with a woman who asked me something I’ve been sitting with ever since. She said: _“I’m so glad you’re here. But most of my neighbors would never come to something like this. How are you going to reach them?”_ It was a fair question; it’s the central challenge of any campaign. And despite our best efforts, reaching 110,000+ Rhode Islanders is really, really difficult. The block parties and the coffee shop conversations and the front porch visits are the part of campaigning I love most, and they’re genuinely the most effective (and fun) way to earn a vote.
---
|
---
But digital advertising, mailers, and ads on TV are how I get to the neighbors who weren’t at the block party. [**That’s what this fundraising push is for →**](https://sue4ri.com/l/pEOkLcNq7FaQ)**to get this campaign in front of the Rhode Islanders I can’t reach on foot, in enough places and enough times (research says the number is**** _at least_****4) that my name and my actual positions start to feel familiar before they walk into a voting booth.** [**I’m trying to activate 200 grassroots donors this month to make this extended outreach possible. Will you be one of them, friend?**](https://sue4ri.com/l/apQfvejmCdEc)
---
If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | [DONATE $25](https://sue4ri.com/l/vSWDheoaY86c)

It’s how I’ve always done this, from my first City Council race to now. But it’s only possible if enough people chip in.

How are you going to reach them?” It was a fair question; it’s the central challenge of any campaign. And despite our best efforts, reaching 110,000+ Rhode Islanders is really, really difficult. The block parties and the coffee shop conversations and the front porch visits are the part of campaigning I love most, and they’re genuinely the most effective (and fun) way to earn a vote. | But digital advertising, mailers, and ads on TV are how I get to the neighbors who weren’t at the block party. get this campaign in front of the Rhode Islanders I can’t reach on foot, in enough places and enough times (research says the number is at least4) that my name and my actual positions start to feel familiar before they walk into a voting booth. If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | This campaign runs on contributions from actual people who care about Rhode Island and care what happens here — not on political machine money or donors who expect a seat at the table in return. It’s how I’ve always done this, from my first City Council race to now. But it’s only possible if enough people chip in. | | Here’s what your contribution could help power: A targeted digital ad reaching voters in a community I haven’t visited yet A week of social media presence that keeps the campaign visible between in-person events Mailer production that puts my actual positions — not spin — in someone’s mailbox TV or streaming ads in a part of Rhode Island where name recognition is still being built Thank you for being here. I am so grateful for you. name: Dan Osborn
subject: Why I was fired:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY RESIST RECLAIM REBUILD PAC (WWW
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
In October 2021, I had been an employee of Kellogg’s for almost 18 years.
I had dropped out of college and started working for the company after my wife got pregnant. Life’s easy when all you gotta do is take care of yourself – but we needed diapers and health insurance for our growing family.
Working at Kellogg’s used to be a lifelong career. A good-paying job that lets you become a homeowner, live decently, and hopefully retire someday.
But over the years, that changed. Workers were paid less. Cost-of-living adjustments weren’t keeping up anywhere near inflation. Retirement and health insurance plans were gutted. It just wasn’t right. They were making record profits – and doing it off the backs of workers.
So in October 2021, we walked out. And as president of our local union, I led the strike. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/120031/images/Screen%20Shot%202026-04-24%20at%2011.20.44%20AM.png]
Most of us had never walked a picket line. It was cold, but we were determined to hold our lines through the dead of winter if we had to. We were a part of something bigger than ourselves. We were in a fight for the future of the American middle class.
After 11 weeks in the cold, we reached an agreement. More importantly, we saved 500 good-paying union jobs.
It was one of the proudest moments of my life.
Following the strike, I was fired. Someone had to pay – and as union president, my head was on the chopping block.
It’s easy to let yourself get beaten down by life. To let big corporations and the politicians they own in Washington make all the decisions – and just accept that that’s how things will always be. But that’s not me.
Instead, I decided last year to run against one of the most corporate politicians – U.S. Senator Republican Deb Fischer – and we nearly won. I got 47% of the vote in one of the closest Senate races in the country.
Now, I’m running again for the U.S. Senate – this time against billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts – and the first poll shows us virtually TIED: 46% to 45%.
I am taking on a literal billionaire senator. We can finish what we started last year and flip Nebraska’s Senate seat for working-class people, but I need grassroots donors like you to give now if we’re going to win.
Please, will you contribute to my campaign for U.S. Senate to help me defeat billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts here and flip Nebraska’s Senate seat? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
DONATE TODAY TO DEFEAT THE MAGA BILLIONAIRES! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
I believe we can win this race and keep up the fight for the American middle class. But I’m counting on your support now to win.
Thank you,
Dan Osborn

Private sector companies and nonprofit charities often donate money and provide grants to communities across the country to help administer voting.

Peter, Six days. **That is how long it took for ICE agents to kill again.** Six days after ICE agents in Houston shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo on his way to work, agents in Biddeford, Maine shot and killed **Joan Sebastian Guerrero.** He was a 26 years old father here legally with a Social Security number in his wallet. His three-year-old daughter was nearby wearing Bluey pajamas as she watched her daddy die in the street. I have read a lot of hard things in my life but, as a father, this tragedy has been sitting on my chest all day. Every single beat of this is the Houston playbook run again. It's the second time in a week that agents killed a man with NO body cameras for accountability - after Congress handed them $20 million for bodycams earlier this year. And Joan, like Lorenzo, was not even their intended target for removal. Initial statements from local officials attempted to roll out the same tired lie they always use, that _he threatened the officer 's safety with his vehicle_. But a bystander video came out and made such a mess of their story that the official DHS statement twelve hours later did not even bother to try lying again. Now whistleblowers within the agency are reporting that there's been an immediate stand-down order on most ICE vehicle stops. That's a sign that something went very wrong here, and the American people deserve to know the truth. I'm running for Congress because I believe that public servants have a duty of care to the people and communities they serve, and that when they fail to meet that standard there must be accountability. What we've seen from this agency is a systemic pattern of abuse and an apparent intent to cause as much harm as possible. That cannot be allowed to continue. [**When I get to Washington I will fight for public hearings and accountability. body:

# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Hi Peter, it’s Gina. I know your time is valuable, so I’ll keep this short.
[**If you’re in the position to do so, will you give a $5 donation to my campaign today?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260714_2_fec.0Y87uU&refcode=em20260714-1567&amount=5&t=1&akid=1567%2E299639%2EbfhGW0) Let me explain why your donation is important to my campaign — _especially_ right now.
Tomorrow, our public fundraising numbers will be officially released. This is the very first report since I became the official Democratic nominee for Governor back in March, and I’m going to be completely candid with you — I’m a little nervous.
The total we report tomorrow matters a lot. It’ll prove how much momentum we’ve built since March, show the exact resources we have at our disposal, and show how much we have in the bank to fight back when the attacks come.
But tomorrow also means we’ll see Greg Abbott’s updated campaign numbers. We already know he’s sitting on a massive $106 million war chest, and there’s a chance he’s gotten more money from his billionaire buddies since earlier this year. Meaning Abbott might have even more money to drown out this campaign.
But I don’t need to match Abbott’s numbers. I’m deeply grateful for everything you and this grassroots team has done for me. **But before these numbers go live and Abbott's team gets a look at our fundraising,_I want to see one final surge to show that we aren't backing down once his attacks start._**

Gina

But she needs EVERY LAST DEMOCRAT behind her for support! This faces an UPHILL BATTLE in Congress!!

**_[Please sign our petition ASAP – it will take less than 3 minutes>>](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75126?t=5&akid=24514%2E4449941%2EL-Htna)_** | [SIGN THE PETITION →](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75126?t=6&akid=24514%2E4449941%2EL-Htna)

If you were thinking of ignoring our urgent petition, here’s why you SHOULDN’T:

→ Donald Trump only became President in 2016 because of the outdated Electoral College.

→→ Hillary Clinton won the popular vote by nearly 2.9 million.

→→→ But the Electoral College overruled her victory!!

**[We can’t let something like that happen again! That’s why Sen. Elizabeth Warren is SOUNDING THE ALARM:](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75126?t=7&akid=24514%2E4449941%2EL-Htna)**
[](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75126?t=8&akid=24514%2E4449941%2EL-Htna)
And that’s exactly why we need you to sign today, team.

If every Democrat reading this signs our petition, we will reach our 125,OOO signature goal within minutes and gain traction for this urgent legislation in Congress. [**_Please add your name immediately:_**](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75126?t=9&akid=24514%2E4449941%2EL-Htna)
[Sign to demand Congress abolish the Electoral College →](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75126?t=10&akid=24514%2E4449941%2EL-Htna)
---

Fight For Reform

Letters delivered, families defended, a movement growing. Chip in to power what comes next. | | | Peter, For the past year, this administration has poured billions into the detention, deportation, and surveillance of our communities. **But they didn't count on us.****[Will you chip in $10 today to power the movement for citizenship?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIGjw8YzSH_UAUmMq7WLV0krCNSeQgLJ3AAolc0INa2cCMpccy2Ab9RLEr4KrEWPLCxKSzGr-UiAyUB02STKGtDXiihtSaA5q4ZCLEvQ_-rNxb8SnzSRSU_40tex_Y77TUXqjfXlTj6_lYT9edtFY6Si3bzLsnG7KNLxT_8eZ97KRQMqoiYPlz3CQdR3JLUhBYdkrVl5v9vsh0lx8qOXn2ogugci0s2PzJhDdEinFsdqy-fPxxHkEvp-TsPpyVCEXi1JXiNdIvmtchnViSWbp2jIRUms1LXDLYymF4aH69dVKBDPf1sK9fh2CKGrv3CDc4H7HaAlh8fkz--e-4HNya2vNsCxO21_NGlI1NYAr5kfilD6NuCrZXSnbrpDZ02XI8JO8narPAhpFBtnh1GFhVGkf7NH2hSD9D2di6CwzDXTgDzr6DclzMfYqHxR6H55mRMZLs1gJh57q-5HUyas5x4VArgAFtjYszSWcOgBd4vMV136a3k6v8-fYBl4yd1tjwMIkD-mvfUhrMlipjKQ6kA/4sb/gIYOiCZdQ8mLthrBXodYXw/h0/h001.0wXj4hmJjtSy-9qhL6H9Bg69NiwOUI0gq_eWy4kJrlA)** Here's what we've built together these past few months: [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIGjw8YzSH_UAUmMq7WLV0krCNSeQgLJ3AAolc0INa2cCMpccy2Ab9RLEr4KrEWPLCxKSzGr-UiAyUB02STKGtH2e_wl3nQxcvny8PgKrbBfh5x9SIi3Kf6lO1g8VosurzBNnPZwtCZvwciTaW88328qbTzPZu0FL7i9ZfZYepit9NiXIjA_f3NitBNNXT8mCSY345ZnudWHL32FyGzLyVnqiP7zr1-KDWAETK3FUb0Zn4QMZuyinRW0p3Df_k-96igp-xxtdT7ClyxaHpDfuGhBWUTDwp7PVXrIqkN3X1vz2oSLwK07YNA8Vvf9biB1fRi_tPPQyyBbX9i7X_cElaCcRtu8qwJPoxgwv5MUrgW3s3jtFYVsC-6XxdyHAsaQTw2TGMoHwXCJ2T00GEJIXnxYX4NWW7o4-75WiSqFmuVyz_cAQLAOcCtXylznIi1p0l7_Vri4wZs0DR4_X2KcCxtVun7bWahipMBaZW5_VFPqJjid9gQTDiBPInOuEXL1_/4sb/gIYOiCZdQ8mLthrBXodYXw/h1/h001.QXUTVwZJvjbEkM7ZSbruZpkUp4cScg2DpoT3hCPeZCQ)
* **Mobilizing for citizenship:** On the 14th anniversary of DACA, we delivered 62,000 letters to Congress and rallied at the Capitol to demand a pathway to citizenship through the Dream Act and the Dream and Promise Act.
* **A victory for the Constitution:** The Supreme Court upheld birthright citizenship — a fundamental guarantee, and a win for every community member who refused to stay silent.
* **Bruce Springsteen put a spotlight on our movement.** The legendary musician chose to uplift United We Dream at his "Land of Hope & Dreams" tour stop in Elmont, NY — speaking directly to thousands about what immigrant communities are facing, while our team connected with concertgoers who were fired up and ready to take action with us.

**[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIGjw8YzSH_UAUmMq7WLV0krCNSeQgLJ3AAolc0INa2cCMpccy2Ab9RLEr4KrEWPLCxKSzGr-UiAyUB02STKGtN_7jFSbWHABsKBalJ1X5zH9R3eDBa-WZwazpUApaD_CN434VdzisSBCSVLcnVsXuC4BzkzFcD5I7Ptn-JsaUhUJePtTmykaY9B7m2tBENEGcWeQUoXl50JIheYtRxYPOXW1cAapoFiEhE6tUmYDVC-WfJP9xWAm2_Qm_ZqY-CsgldSoVOyB09TNFv-jqLCQNWYy4wXQlrCf3SSnk6e6BzWKSN_qBWwPT00NYUrEyXLinegTFhMKhDDx4VQkWVWKomgeqEh-2C7aqTNMo3GhWBoh2q_aJUgrfzBUeZs1Kd68Ii0pFGzPXwd2F05W3YHwtaceW2ovG8XwejF7jOQ-Gf7-6dx0K4aqbB9ipDAiu_thuuizMRUp81rC6Y6bLQbNmjy1Uvxzf_xYJkR3Txj8gQk_QF10qTz3UdkOfB0yJ5yx/4sb/gIYOiCZdQ8mLthrBXodYXw/h2/h001.OKPNP-UCjInnBYGjgSZ5WrGJL__VJ9mw3dHaHQVAu0g)**
* **Joy and Cultura built power in Los Angeles.** Over one incredible weekend of door-knocking, music, and cultura — from USC to a packed Coffee & Cultura party in South LA — we welcomed Homies Unidos into our movement family and sparked two brand-new chapters in Orange County and at LA City College. When organizing feels like belonging, people don't just show up — they stay, they organize, and they lead.

**Congress leaves for August recess soon** —**** and when members go home to their districts, that's exactly when they need to hear from us the most. clean_body: Letters delivered, families defended, a movement growing. Chip in to power what comes next. | | | Peter, For the past year, this administration has poured billions into the detention, deportation, and surveillance of our communities. But they didn't count on us. Here's what we've built together these past few months: Mobilizing for citizenship: On the 14th anniversary of DACA, we delivered 62,000 letters to Congress and rallied at the Capitol to demand a pathway to citizenship through the Dream Act and the Dream and Promise Act. A victory for the Constitution: The Supreme Court upheld birthright citizenship — a fundamental guarantee, and a win for every community member who refused to stay silent. Bruce Springsteen put a spotlight on our movement. The legendary musician chose to uplift United We Dream at his "Land of Hope & Dreams" tour stop in Elmont, NY — speaking directly to thousands about what immigrant communities are facing, while our team connected with concertgoers who were fired up and ready to take action with us. Joy and Cultura built power in Los Angeles. Over one incredible weekend of door-knocking, music, and cultura — from USC to a packed Coffee & Cultura party in South LA — we welcomed Homies Unidos into our movement family and sparked two brand-new chapters in Orange County and at LA City College. When organizing feels like belonging, people don't just show up — they stay, they organize, and they lead. Congress leaves for August recess soon —** and when members go home to their districts, that's exactly when they need to hear from us the most. Your support keeps organizers on the ground, letters flowing, and ensures DACA recipients, TPS holders, and immigrant youth have someone fighting for them all recess long. ** If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | In solidarity, Aria, United We Dream Follow us on: | | | | |

Frankly, Derek, our campaign needs a strong showing as we enter the final stretch before general election voting begins in Virginia.

National Republicans and their super PACs have their sights set on Virginia. **Help Shape the Next Session: Your Ideas, Your Feedback** Over the coming newsletters, I'll be sharing a series of policy ideas we're developing ahead of the next legislative session — not finished bills, but concepts in progress. The best legislation I've worked on started with conversations back home, and I'd rather hear from you now, while these ideas can still be shaped, than after a bill is already written. Each issue will spotlight one topic. Read it, react to it, and tell me what you think — what would work, what wouldn't, and what we're missing. **First Up: Child Care** Ask any young family or employer on the coast, and you'll hear the same thing: child care is too scarce and too expensive. Providers are closing their doors, parents are leaving the workforce, and employers can't fill jobs. **What we've already tried.** In previous sessions, I worked on what seemed like a common-sense idea: put child care facilities inside affordable housing developments — child care where the kids actually are. The catch? Adding a child care center triggers prevailing wage requirements for the whole project, driving up construction costs enough to kill the deal. So we proposed removing that trigger. Simple fix, right? Apparently not. The public employee unions objected, the Democrat majority obliged, and the idea died — because in Salem, protecting a wage mandate matters more than whether working parents can find child care down the hall. I still think kids and housing belong together, but I've stopped waiting for the majority party to agree. So we've shifted to proposals they'll have a harder time saying no to. Here's what we're working on: **Solving the liability insurance crisis.** One of the quiet forces driving providers out of business is the cost — and sometimes the sheer unavailability — of liability insurance. I serve on the Task Force on Liability Insurance for Child Care Providers, and our goal is legislation creating industry-wide liability coverage based on the task force's findings, so a provider's insurance bill no longer decides whether they can keep their doors open. **Making child care affordable.** Two ideas here. First, increasing Oregon's child care tax credit to put money directly back in parents' pockets. Second, a "Tri-Share" model based on Michigan's successful program: child care costs split three ways — one-third employer, one-third employee, one-third state and county. In Michigan, average family out-of-pocket costs dropped from $716 a month to $252 — a 65% reduction — and 82% of participating employees said they were more likely to stay in their current jobs. Under our concept, the employer's share would be a 100% tax deduction, up to $3,600 per child per year. Families save, employers keep workers, and communities keep young families. **Partnering with counties.** Allowing public-private partnerships between counties and child care providers would open new ways to deliver care in rural communities where the private market alone hasn't been able to make it work. **What do you think?** Are these the right approaches? Would a Tri-Share program work for your family or your business? Email my office — every response gets read, and your input will shape what we bring to Salem. sen.dickanderson@oregonlegislature.gov **Senator Dick Anderson**
Oregon State Senate, District 5 |
* * *

* * *
---
To every graduate in Oregon Senate District 5, whether you are heading to college, trade school, the workforce, or military service- I am proud of each and every one of you, Congratulation, Class of 2026!
Whether you're combing the sands of Lincoln City in search of one of the elusive hand-blown glass floats, settling in for an evening of live music at the Newport Performing Arts Center, watching giant kites paint the sky above Chinook Winds, or browsing the freshest local produce and handcrafted goods at the Coos Bay Farmers Market, I hope you are taking advantage of all the wonderful things Senate District 5 has to offer. From the fishing docks of Charleston to the forested lanes of the central coast, there's nowhere I'd rather be than right here, talking with all the hardworking fishermen, small business owners, farmers, and families who make Senate District 5 a community worth fighting for every single day in Salem. I hope to see you out and about this summer!
* * *
****
**Working for You in Salem**
Serving the Oregon Coast means showing up wherever coastal voices need to be heard. Beyond my committee assignments in the Legislature, I serve on a wide range of commissions, boards, task forces, and work groups tackling the issues that matter most to our district — from fisheries and ocean science to rural housing, child care, state parks, and support for our tribal communities. Each of these seats is a chance to make sure coastal Oregon has a voice at the table when decisions are made. Below is the full list of where I'm putting in the work on your behalf.
**Coast & Ocean**
* Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission
* Oregon Ocean Science Trust
* Oregon Coastal Caucus Member
* Blue Economy Task Force

**Children & Families**
* Vice-Chair on Behavioral Health and Early Learning
* Task Force on Liability Insurance for Child Care Providers
* Oregon Child Integrated Dataset Governance Committee

**Tribal Relations**
* Statewide Legislative Commission on Indian Services
* Task Force on Tribal Consultation

**Housing & Economy**
* Vice-Chair Housing and Development Committee
* Senate Committee on Finance and Revenue
* Work Group for Eastern Oregon Rural Housing Needs
* Oregon Life Sciences Competitiveness Task Force
* Oregon Retirement Savings Board (OregonSaves)
* Denmark Industrial Symbiosis Study Tour

**Parks & Culture**
* Oregon State Parks Revenue Workgroup
* Oregon Cultural Trust Board

**Legislative Operations**
* Joint Committee on Legislative Administration
* Joint Emergency Board Subcommittee on Higher Education
* Joint Emergency Board Member and Committee on Ways and Means
* Asset Forfeiture Oversight Advisory Committee

The connection between **people** and their **governmen** t is bolstered when the public has **substantial opportunity** to let their concerns be heard by their elected officials. Below are a few ways that **YOU** can join in on the**legislative process.**
[OLIS- Oregon Legislative Information System](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Folis.oregonlegislature.gov%2Fliz%2F2025R1/1/0101019f623c5bd5-e99bfee7-188b-4c69-81c9-404134bfdcc3-000000/CXbmwTK7rz_K9ZntluBoGQ2lPPnvqgjMv4fLUGA-LHY=452)\- This is where you can find extensive details about every bill as well as follow them through the legislative process. This is also where you can view committee hearings online.
[Legislative Session Participation Guide](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.oregonlegislature.gov%2Fmarsh%2FDocuments%2FLegislative_Session_Participation_Guide.pdf/1/0101019f623c5bd5-e99bfee7-188b-4c69-81c9-404134bfdcc3-000000/lQFjfcPb0xGlWqNfQy2XWBLInLsMc_Il7LZbkeih4AY=452)\- This is a wonderful resource with everything you will need to know about how to participate in the Legislative Session. Links to find your legislatures, how to follow bills and watch meetings, how to testify and visiting the Capitol.

Friend, I’m proud to support two candidates who are deeply rooted in their communities and fighting for their neighbors: Will Lawrence, who’s running to flip the Republican-held U.S. Congressional seat in Michigan’s 7th district, and Rima Mohammad, who’s running for re-election to the Ann Arbor Public Schools Board. As a Palestinian and Muslim American, a University of Michigan professor, a healthcare worker, a school board trustee, and community advocate, Rima has consistently worked to center equity and defend vulnerable communities. Will helped found Sunrise Movement, a national youth-led environmental justice organization that shaped the Green New Deal and the Build Back Better Agenda, winning billions of dollars for good green jobs. He also founded groups in Michigan to fight for tenants’ rights and protect families from homelessness. Will is running against a Republican member of Congress and a Democratic primary election opponent who are both backed by Big Oil. These movement leaders and community organizers are unbought, focusing on people power and relying on grassroots donations. They need our support now. As a Palestinian and Muslim American, a University of Michigan professor, a healthcare worker, a school board trustee, and community advocate, Rima has consistently worked to center equity and defend vulnerable communities. Will helped found Sunrise Movement, a national youth-led environmental justice organization that shaped the Green New Deal and the Build Back Better Agenda, winning billions of dollars for good green jobs. He also founded groups in Michigan to fight for tenants’ rights and protect families from homelessness. Will is running against a Republican member of Congress and a Democratic primary election opponent who are both backed by Big Oil. These movement leaders and community organizers are unbought, focusing on people power and relying on grassroots donations. They need our support now. Last year he organized a 36-hour vigil outside of the incumbent’s office to protest cuts in federal food assistance, where he also gathered food for local food banks. He will take on AI data centers, the Epstein class, the fossil fuel industry, weapons corporations, and the for-profit healthcare system. If he’s elected to Congress, he’ll join me in the fight for Medicare for All, building affordable housing and ending homelessness, ending weapons sales to Israel and other human rights violators, and banning members of Congress and the White House from trading stocks. Meanwhile, as a school board trustee, Rima Mohammad has advocated for immigrant families and LGBTQ+ students, protected free speech on campus, advanced environmental justice, and ensured that students and their families have meaningful voices in district decision making. Rima’s parents and grandparents were refugees pushed out of Palestine during the 1948 Nakba, living in refugee camps in Lebanon. Her experience with U.S. public schools transformed her life. She’s committed to accountable leadership, meaningful engagement with the community, building power from the ground up, expanding access to justice and opportunity, and ensuring that marginalized voices are not only included but centered in decision making. Thank you for fighting alongside me for a better future for all of us. Together we’ll keep growing our progressive movement and winning the changes that our communities urgently need. Now she’s running for re-election to continue supporting marginalized students. Rima and Will are both unbought and people-powered, running grassroots campaigns that are deeply rooted in their communities. As an immigrant growing up in poverty, Rima found stability and opportunity in public schools. Her family came here when she was 5 years old, and their experience with displacement and rebuilding their lives in multiple countries shaped how she approaches immigration policy — with urgency, compassion, and a focus on dignity. While serving as a school board trustee, Rima has pushed to protect the privacy and safety of immigrant students and families , including safeguarding immigration status information and ensuring training for teachers and staff. She has supported school policies that protect LGBTQ+ students and ensure inclusivity and safety. She also supported transitioning from diesel to electric school buses and installing solar panels on school rooftops — prioritizing underserved communities, where environmental and health burdens are often greatest and infrastructure investment has historically lagged. In college, Will built a national student network of students working for fossil fuel divestment. For decades, Oregon has led the nation in making voting more accessible.
We've pioneered vote-by-mail. We created Automatic Voter Registration. We've shown that making it easier to vote strengthens our democracy.
But there's still more work to do.
Right now, Oregon's Voters' Rights Act provides important protections against vote dilution in school board elections and special districts
That's a good start. But it shouldn't be the finish line.
As Donald Trump and reckless Republicans wage a war on our voting rights in Washington, I believe that every Oregon voter deserves the same protections — whether they're voting for a school board member, a city councilor, a county commissioner, or any other elected office.
That's why it's time to expand the Oregon Voters' Rights Act so its protections apply statewide, to every candidate, every voter, and every campaign. If you agree that every Oregon voter deserves equal protection under the law, add your name today. >> [https://secure.ngpvan.com/bcf7Ra7JfEKkSrH5ZGgwxw2]

Our democracy works best when every community has a fair opportunity to elect representatives of their choice.

And in the face of the Supreme Court’s relentless attacks on the national Voting Rights Act — and Donald Trump’s commitment to suppressing your right to vote — this fight has never mattered more.
That’s why I’m asking you to take a stand today. If enough of us speak up together, we can build the momentum to strengthen Oregon's democracy for generations to come. Will you sign your name? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/bcf7Ra7JfEKkSrH5ZGgwxw2]

_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2651%2E259176%2E-c8hDH) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2651%2E259176%2E-c8hDH)_

Peter, Last month, I named Gwen Graham as my running mate, and I filed to officially get on the ballot for Governor. I am asking you to **[_split a donation with my campaign and Blue Amp Action to be one of our Filing Donors today_](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13934?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.14_Jolly-Had-To_B3_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=4&akid=2651%2E259176%2E-c8hDH)** , because moments like this only matter if we build on them together. | [DONATE →](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13934?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.14_Jolly-Had-To_B3_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=5&akid=2651%2E259176%2E-c8hDH)

I'll be honest with you about why I'm writing. Filing my name to run for Governor of Florida is one of the proudest things I have ever done, and it reminded me exactly who this is for. It's for the family watching their rent climb faster than their paycheck. It's for the parent rationing a prescription. It's for every Floridian who has been told to accept less while the people in Tallahassee look out for themselves.
I refuse to accept that. So does Gwen. And I don't believe you accept it, either.
Here's the truth about a month like this one. The headlines fade fast, and our opponents are counting on the energy fading with them. The only thing that proves them wrong is people like you stepping up in the hours right after, when it counts most.
**[_So I'm asking you directly, Peter. Split a donation between my campaign and Blue Amp Action and let's turn this moment into momentum:_](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13934?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.14_Jolly-Had-To_B3_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=6&akid=2651%2E259176%2E-c8hDH)**

---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Jeffco Schools weighs a [$135M tax hike](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for November ($3.58/mo per $100K home value) amid enrollment declines. [Primary spending hit $67M](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), mostly in Dem-vs-Dem races with $25M+ from super PACs — yet four top-funded candidates still lost. [DSA is pushing to grow in Colorado Springs,](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) trailing Denver's infrastructure. And [Rep. Lorena García's nonprofit took $6.64M in state payments since she took office](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) (up from $13K prior), with its lobbyist backing her bills and her parents on the payroll — no law bars it.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC), a top GOP voice on national security and Trump ally, [died Saturday at 71 of an aortic dissection](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). He'd served since 2003 and just won his primary for a fifth term.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** O'Donnell's voter-roll series [examines an Aurora apartment linked to 104 registrants](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) from 2021-23 (only one ever voted), amid the SOS fighting a DOJ records request. Montalbano says Colorado's "53% renewable" milestone owes [more to a coal drop than real growth](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Commissioner Pond argues [America's divide is "affective polarization," not real disagreement](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Dr. Joondeph cites a poll showing 45% think COVID's release was possibly deliberate, blaming [eroded trust from shifting pandemic narratives](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, July 14, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Lorena García’s nonprofit took $6.6 million in state money while its lobbyist backed bills she sponsored](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Before Lorena García was a Colorado state representative, the organization she runs had collected about $13,000 from the state of Colorado in the five years before she filled the vacancy, according to state payment records.
That changed when she joined the legislature.
The Colorado Statewide Parent Coalition (CSPC) was founded in 1980 by Richard Garcia, Lorena García’s father, who ran it as executive director through 2017, according to the organization’s IRS filings. Lorena García took over as executive director in 2018.
Since García was appointed to the Colorado House in January 2023, the nonprofit she leads has received $6.64 million in state payments. That is 99.8 percent of every dollar state payment records show the organization collecting from Colorado taxpayers since 2018.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado’s dirty voter roll: The curious case of Apartment A503](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY MIKE O'DONNELL, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A citizen audit of Colorado's public voter roll uncovered what appears to be a mass registration scheme at a single Aurora address — while the Secretary of State fights the DOJ's attempt to check for noncitizen voters._
* Colorado's voter roll shows 104 registrants were added to a single one-bedroom Aurora apartment between 2021 and 2023, arriving in groups of four to six on the same day with shared commercial mailing addresses; only the original occupant ever voted, most ballots came back undeliverable, and the author suggests the names may have been used in a Medicare/Medicaid fraud scheme.
* Colorado's registration system has no flag for an impossible number of new registrants at one address — and 101 of the phantom registrants will remain on the voter roll through the 2026 federal election with no mechanism to remove them sooner.
* Secretary of State Jena Griswold willingly shared confidential voter data with ERIC — a partisan nonprofit — but is actively fighting a DOJ lawsuit seeking that same data to check for noncitizen registrants, in a state home to an estimated 230,000 unauthorized immigrants where citizenship verification relies entirely on a self-declaration honor system.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[America isn’t divided because we disagree](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SEAN POND, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_Montrose County Commissioner Sean Pond argues that outrage has become a business model, constitutional principles don't require treating fellow Americans as threats, and the country has always disagreed — that's never been our greatest danger._
* Pond argues America isn't falling apart because we disagree — the Founders disagreed, and elections have always been personal — but because politics has shifted from "I think you're wrong" to "people like you don't love this country," turning policy debates into identity battles.
* Outrage is a deliberate business model: cable news, campaigns, activist groups, and social media all profit from keeping Americans angry, feeding the loudest extreme voices until we mistake them for the mainstream — when most Americans are simply working, raising families, and building good lives.
* Pond holds firm that the Constitution isn't negotiable, government must be questioned, and dishonest officials must be called out — but warns that excusing from your own side what you'd condemn in the other is loyalty, not principle, and no political victory will be enough to put the country back together if we lose the ability to see fellow Americans as neighbors.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

| | | | | | Hello Peter ,
---
| |
I want to show you something most campaigns never show you: exactly what your money does.Here's the thing about running for state treasurer without a national TV budget, you have to be smarter about [where every dollar goes](https://us.list-manage.com/REx8IwRp6SA?e=2a3e897a17&c2id=f692bbcc41c775a14e84f1daafe001aa). So instead of asking you to trust us, I'm just going to show you the math.We're running this campaign digital-first. Not because it's trendy, but because it works better than the old model. A TV ad gets bought, it airs a set number of times to whoever happens to be watching, and then it's gone. What we're building is different: people see me every day, on a platform where they can actually comment back, share it with a neighbor, or ask me a question directly. That's how our accounts have grown to 14.5K followers off 196 posts and 6.4M total views so far.And because it's digital, we can track it down to the dollar. Here's what your contribution turns into, in views of content telling Ohio voters who I am and what's actually at stake in this race:
* **$10** → about 858 views
* **$52** → about 4,460 views
* **$100** → about 8,500 views
* **$250** → about 21,500 views
* **$500** → about 43,000 views
* **$1,000** → about 86,000 views
* **$2,500** → about 215,000 views

---
| [DONATE](https://us.list-manage.com/BqCbpqtR3qb?e=2a3e897a17&c2id=f692bbcc41c775a14e84f1daafe001aa)
---

That's not a guess, it's based on what we're actually spending and actually getting back, dollar for dollar, in front of Ohio voters.If you want to go all the way, the max an individual can give a statewide candidate in Ohio this election is $16,615.67... and at our current rate, that's roughly 1.4 million views. That's a lot of Ohioans learning what happens to their pension money, their kids' teachers' retirement, and the $280 billion Ohio treasurer's office when someone who's spent his career voting for FirstEnergy's interests instead of yours is in charge of it.You don't have to max out to make a difference. Even $10 puts us in front of hundreds more people who've never heard of this race, and most Ohioans have no idea how much power this office actually has.Whatever you can do, thank you for being part of this.

Team, ICE agents shot and killed 26-year-old Joan Sebastian Guerrero in the streets of Biddeford, Maine. Less than a week after a previous killing in Houston. | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Friend,
---
The earthquakes in Venezuela dominated the news for a matter of days. The collapsed buildings, the death toll, the rescue teams pulling survivors from the rubble, **the world watched, then largely moved on.** But for the children left behind, the danger didn't end when the ground stopped shaking. **In some ways, it was only the beginning.** Displacement does something traffickers understand better than almost anyone. It breaks the systems that normally protect a child -- records, schools, familiar faces, parents who never let go of their hand. If this is the first time you're hearing from me, my name is Eduardo Verastegui, and I produced the film Sound of Freedom. The film Sound of Freedom was truly a movie that launched a movement. That movement is now. Our mission at the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** is to **stop the sale of God's children.** We do that through five pillars:
---
* **Prevention**
* **Intervention**
* **Education**
* **Information**
* **Influence**

---
We are working urgently, with trusted partners on the ground, to:
---
* Find children who have already fallen into trafficking, including exploitation happening online in the chaos of the disaster.
* Support rescue operations that bring a child out of danger and into safety.
* Provide a safe bed the moment a child is free.
* Fund reunification when a family can be found and verified.

clean_body: She survived the earthquake. Now she needs to survive what comes after. After the earthquakes in Venezuela, traffickers are already moving. Here's how we're responding. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Friend, The earthquakes in Venezuela dominated the news for a matter of days. The collapsed buildings, the death toll, the rescue teams pulling survivors from the rubble, the world watched, then largely moved on. But for the children left behind, the danger didn't end when the ground stopped shaking. In some ways, it was only the beginning. Displacement does something traffickers understand better than almost anyone. It breaks the systems that normally protect a child -- records, schools, familiar faces, parents who never let go of their hand. In that broken space, a stranger offering "help," a ride, a promise of safety somewhere else, can be all it takes for a child to disappear. We've set an urgent goal to raise $50,000 in the next 30 days to help rescue children, provide safe shelter, and reunite families before more children disappear into trafficking. Every gift brings us one step closer.Will you help us reach this lifesaving goal today? I've sat with survivors. I've heard what it costs a family to lose a child this way, and what it takes to bring one home. And I've learned that disasters like the one in Venezuela don't create new evil, they simply hand existing evil an opening it has used again and again. If this is the first time you're hearing from me, my name is Eduardo Verastegui, and I produced the film Sound of Freedom. The film Sound of Freedom was truly a movie that launched a movement. That movement is now. Our mission at the Sound of Freedom Foundation is to stop the sale of God's children. We do that through five pillars: Prevention Intervention Education Information Influence We are working urgently, with trusted partners on the ground, to: Find children who have already fallen into trafficking, including exploitation happening online in the chaos of the disaster. Support rescue operations that bring a child out of danger and into safety. Provide a safe bed the moment a child is free. Fund reunification when a family can be found and verified. Walk alongside a child through long-term care when there is nowhere safe to send them yet. "Defend the weak and the fatherless; uphold the cause of the poor and the oppressed. Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked." (Psalm 82:3-4) That command is what guides every decision this Foundation makes. It is not a suggestion. It is not poetry. It is an instruction, and I take it as one. We're trusting God to help us raise $50,000 in the next 30 days, but He often answers prayers through people willing to act. I hope you'll be one of them today. Friend, I am asking you urgently, humbly, and personally to make your first gift today. Please do not wait. For God's children, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. Right now, a displaced child in Venezuela is being watched by someone who does not have their best interest at heart. Your gift today helps make sure someone who does gets there first. 6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074

#### This post is brought to you free with our partnership with Defiance.org. Please read, watch, and then claim your three free months at [defiance.org/blueamp](https://substack.com/redirect/f2d2e552-e0b8-43e5-bbac-01b0cd79315b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Folks, I don't get to make announcements like this very often, so let me hop right to it! _**[Blue Amp Media is partnering with Defiance.org](https://substack.com/redirect/dabb9f4e-7eea-4378-857f-88fc6fb77844?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_.
If you don't know Defiance, it's the nonprofit founded by my pal Miles Taylor--the guy who blew the whistle on Trump from inside his own administration as "Anonymous," with a _New York Times_ op-ed, and whose reward when Trump got back in was an executive order investigating him for treason. _Treason_. For criticizing the president.
Most people would have taken the hint and gone quiet. Miles and his wife did the opposite: they built a club to fight back. And because you're part of the Blue Amp community, _you can now join that club for free_ --**three full months of Defiance.org membership, for $0, when you sign up at[defiance.org/blueamp](https://substack.com/redirect/f2d2e552-e0b8-43e5-bbac-01b0cd79315b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
Here's what makes Defiance different, and why I wanted this partnership: they don't just talk. Every single Wednesday since they launched last October, Defiance has taken a concrete action against Trump's corruption. And they're always the actions you ask yourself why nobody's discussing. The things that wake you up in the middle of the night to wonder: "who's protecting us from this?"
[Defiance always seems to swoop in at that moment](https://substack.com/redirect/dabb9f4e-7eea-4378-857f-88fc6fb77844?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--like they were thinking the exact same thing--to jump into the breach to protect our freedoms.
They've backed some of the biggest lawsuits against Trump--i _ncluding fights they are winning at the Supreme Cour_ t. They seeded the coalition of local prosecutors now holding federal agents accountable when they break the law--Mary Moriarty in Minneapolis has already charged ICE agents with crimes. Defiance helped fund the Campaign Legal Center's suit against Trump's blatantly unconstitutional mail-in-ballot executive order. And this week they put $15,000 behind the effort to shine a light on the Dilley detention center in Texas and get kids out of there. More than a hundred actions and counting. That's not content. That's some serious freakin action.
[Claim Your 3 FREE Months!](https://substack.com/redirect/f2d2e552-e0b8-43e5-bbac-01b0cd79315b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

When the executive order targeting him was issued, everyone in his life said the same thing: please don't poke the bear. His wife said the opposite. [Defy it, she said, because if Trump can sign one order that blows up a family's life, he'll sign a hundred more](https://substack.com/redirect/dabb9f4e-7eea-4378-857f-88fc6fb77844?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). She was right--a Reuters investigation counted 430 acts of revenge in his first nine months back in office. We also got into the election protection work Defiance is doing right now: making sure prosecutors and state attorneys general are ready before federal agents show up at the polls, not after. And yes, we talked about the Trump-Epstein Bookmobile--a mobile reading room of all 3.5 million Epstein files, built with survivors and the Trumpsonian, that rolls out of Washington at the end of this month and travels coast to coast through the midterms.
[Claim Your 3 FREE Months!](https://substack.com/redirect/f2d2e552-e0b8-43e5-bbac-01b0cd79315b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[When you become a member, you're not buying content. You're funding the fight](https://substack.com/redirect/dabb9f4e-7eea-4378-857f-88fc6fb77844?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), **and you 're getting the thing so many of us have been missing: the feeling of actually doing something**. So here's the ask, and it's an easy one.
**Go to[defiance.org/blueamp](https://substack.com/redirect/f2d2e552-e0b8-43e5-bbac-01b0cd79315b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and claim your three free months**. No gimmicks, no fine print.

For free! Just because you 're a Blue Amp reader**. Show up to their weekly action briefings. Help pick the next fight. Then come back and tell me how it feels.
Strength comes in numbers, folks. Courage is contagious. Seeing someone else stand up and be counted will always add to the number of those willing to fight. So we now add our number to theirs.
_**-- Cliff**_

Friends [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50] , can you imagine if House Republicans used their majority to pass legislation that actually made a positive impact on our lives? Like making health care more affordable, lowering grocery costs, or holding Donald Trump accountable — you know, the things Americans actually care about.
I wish I were writing to tell you that was the case, but instead, here’s what GOP leadership just called a vote on: daylight saving time.
At a moment when millions of families are being crushed by high costs, when our freedoms are under attack, when Donald Trump is openly destroying our democracy — this is what House Republicans are spending their time on.
It would be laughable if it weren’t such a clear example of just how fundamentally incapable this Republican majority is of governing. They either don’t care about the problems facing people across this country, or they simply lack the backbone to stand up and do something about it all.
It’s hard to say which is worse.
We can’t afford two more years of this. We have to flip the House in November so we can get back to working for the American people.

body:
| Derek, I want to tell you about something I've never seen in all my years in public life. **Axios reported that Republicans are preparing an $8 million ad blitz in Maine — against a Democratic nominee who does not exist yet.** Let me explain how we got here. Democrats called on our own Senate nominee in Maine to withdraw over serious, credible allegations of sexual assault. Because our commitment to standing with women and survivors doesn't bend based on party. It can't. On Friday, he withdrew. That was the right thing to do. I believe that without reservation. But it means that right now, there is no Democratic nominee in Maine — one of the seats that will decide whether we take back the Senate majority. And Republicans see an opening. Susan Collins has been stockpiling money for six years. Her allies are sitting on $8 million, ready to define our next nominee before Mainers even learn their name. **I’ve been through a lot of tough campaigns. And I have learned that when the other side has a head start, you don't complain about it. You take action.** That's what the Day One Fund does. Every dollar raised now stays ready for whoever steps forward — so our nominee starts with organizers hired, voter contact underway, and an answer on the air from day one. Not day thirty. Day one. **[Will you make a split contribution between the Maine Dems and my campaign right now? It’s Democrat Cait Conley. I’m running for Congress because Trump is a threat to our community, our country, and everything we know is right. Cowards like my opponent, Mike Lawler, have enabled this administration. We need to hold him accountable at the ballot box. Independent polling shows that I have a clear path to beat Lawler. But I’m counting on grassroots supporters to help us compete with his massive fundraising advantage. | Mike Lawler has beaten politicians before. He’s never beaten someone like me. I am under no illusions that this race will be easy. Mike Lawler has a massive fundraising head start on us, and last cycle, Elon Musk invested more money in this race than anywhere else nationwide. But in the special operations community, we have a saying: “Run to the sound of the guns.” It means we take the tough fights head-on. That’s what I’ve done for my entire career. And that’s what we’re doing in this race. Right now, my team is all-in on meeting our fundraising goals ahead of tomorrow night’s midmonth fundraising deadline. This is the most competitive battleground district in the country, so we cannot afford to come up short for a single one of our goals. Please. Peter,
_Politico_ just covered our strategy memo — and it's turning heads.
It lays out exactly how Voto Latino is moving Latino voters in the states and districts that will decide this election. But reading about it isn't enough. **We need you to fund it.**
[**Will you chip in $3 right now to help us persuade, mobilize, and turn out Latino voters — the margin of victory this fall?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260714-1.sSveNL&amount=3&refcode=em20260714-374&t=1&akid=374%2E1366028%2EmmlP9B)

But when we hold **House and Senate Republicans** accountable for the economic pain hitting Latino families? That's when things shift.
Our latest ad testing proved it. Our top-performing ad:

Voto Latino

Jon Fetherston said protesters disrupted his scheduled appearance on Laura Ingraham's show by crowding around him, shouting insults and attempting to broadcast his home address on national television. Additionally, Fetherston's tires were slashed after he covered an anti-ICE protest. He said the protest itself was more controlled than the Biddeford demonstration, but argued the vandalism showed that hostility toward the Maine Wire continued even at a more organized event.

name: Mary Peltola
subject: Six Months, Six Polls
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
We need to respond.
There have been six polls in the six months since I launched this campaign for Alaska’s U.S. Senate seat. We were leading in the first five.
Then, after my opponent and the billionaires and super PACs that back him started spending millions on attack ads against me, **the New York Times/Siena University poll released this month shows us down two points.**
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260714_2.CfqN0E&refcode=em20260714-2&t=1&akid=7734%2E582294%2EhoCzYU)
We need your help to respond.
Election forecasters like Cook Political Report, Sabato’s Crystal Ball, Split Ticket, and VoteHub have all called Alaska’s U.S. Senate race a toss-up.
They shifted the race in our favor because they know we can win, and that all eyes are on Alaska this year in what’s shaping up to be the most competitive and consequential race on the Senate map.
They know we can win because Alaskans are fed up with the rigged system that’s pricing us out and threatening our way of life while DC politicians and their donors make themselves richer.
They know we can win because my opponent, Dan Sullivan, is the least popular senator up for reelection, and Alaskans want someone who will fight for their healthcare, jobs, disaster relief, and public media – not gut them.
They know we can win because I’ve won Alaska statewide – _twice_ – against our former governor Sarah Palin, and now we’re building a movement that’s ready to take on the rigged DC system so we can lower costs, save our fisheries, and bring abundance back to our state.
**They know we can win this toss-up Senate race if we can raise the resources needed to overcome the attack ads and get our message out.**
Our fight for fish, family, and freedom resonates in every region of our big, beautiful state – _and in a state as big as Texas, Montana, and California combined, that’s a pretty broad coalition!_
We’re criss-crossing as much of Alaska’s 586,000 square miles as we can to bring every village and every voter into our campaign, and we’re doing all we can to fight back with ads online and on the airwaves.
But this is without a doubt the most expensive state on the map to run a Senate campaign. To win in Alaska means building a strong ground game and winning the screen war – reaching communities on and off the road system, from the Aleutians to Anchorage to the Arctic.
No one ever said flipping Alaska’s Senate seat was going to be easy. But we do know that this is our best chance to do it.
**I know we can pull this off, and here’s why:** If everyone getting this email split a donation between Chris Pappas and my campaign, we’d have enough to match the tens of millions in outside spending from the billionaire-backed super PACs propping up my unpopular opponent.
**[Split a donation today »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260714_2.CfqN0E&refcode=em20260714-2&t=2&akid=7734%2E582294%2EhoCzYU)**
That’s the power of a grassroots movement. We can win this when we all chip in together.
But not everyone will read this or give today, and that’s okay. But that’s why it’s all the more important that you do. You’ve already made it this far, and I really appreciate it.
Your support makes a huge difference. I’m humbled to have you with me in this campaign for Alaska’s toss-up Senate seat, and even more so in this fight for fish, family, and freedom. 🐟❤️🇺🇸
Let’s go win.
\- Mary

In the opening months of the second Trump administration, Elon Musk was unleashed on the federal government. Under the banner of "government efficiency," he methodically eliminated and undercut investigators who were in the process of probing his various companies and took a chainsaw to government regulators he deemed to be slowing down business. After eliminating surveillance of New World screwworm, the small fly, whose larvae burrow like a screw into the open wounds of animals, came surging back after decades of eradication. After Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy backed off of monitoring _Cyclospora cayetanensis_ , the putrid parasite burst across the country, contaminating produce that produces explosive diarrhea with dire health implications. Along with parasites and larvae, the Trump administration has also encouraged the explosive growth of data centers across the country.
All of it has combined to make the public just mad enough that a populist Democrat running for agriculture commissioner in Texas has a surprisingly serious chance of winning. The article below, on the campaign of Clayton Tucker, is part of Drop Site's ongoing collaboration with Barn Raiser Media t[o put a focus on rural politics](https://substack.com/redirect/7156f2ac-3510-48a0-8f7c-d23fddde1c61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with a newsletter running through November.
