Clayton Tucker campaigns against data centers in Bay City, Texas on June 11, 2026. Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle via Getty Images.
_Story by David Griscom_
Texas agriculture commissioner candidate Clayton Tucker is well-versed in populist language. The former Our Revolution organizer has no problem [railing](https://substack.com/redirect/edfbf9f6-8617-458b-a489-809afe1ae575?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against corporate monopolies like Tyson, Cargill, and John Deere that are rigging the system against the little people. That shouldn't be surprising; the 28-year-old is a longtime admirer and protege of Jim Hightower, the Texas agriculture commissioner from 1983-1991 and the last Democrat to be elected to the position.
Tucker is from Lampasas, Texas, the [birthplace](https://substack.com/redirect/3aa3a233-d2a8-46b4-9ff4-38f63248499d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the Farmers' Alliance and American populism. But is that connection enough to get Tucker, a Democrat, elected Texas's Agricultural Commissioner?
## **Betting big against data centers**
Tucker has bet big on the backlash to data centers that has engulfed the country. Whether on the trail or on social media, he is quick to raise the concerns of farmers, rural communities, and common Texans who are paying the price for the rollout of these massive warehouses--such as the planned [1,100-acre](https://substack.com/redirect/f81e029d-aae7-4d48-8aed-5a7f99cd1c67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Stargate data center in Abilene, Texas--which serve as the physical infrastructure of the artificial intelligence boom.
Many progressives hope this issue will do something that hasn't been done in a generation: attract rural voters to the Democratic ticket. Data centers are wildly unpopular. A recent [poll](https://substack.com/redirect/e4b14d90-dd61-4ef8-94d7-0556c8d9b57c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that 56% of Texans oppose data centers being built in their community.
To Tucker, the data center issue is one of local control. Major corporations like Oracle, Amazon and Meta have been sucking up Texas's scarce water and energy resources at the public expense, receiving [more](https://substack.com/redirect/e9773cf5-7826-4d30-bc1e-8c73eef33ea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than $1 billion in tax breaks each year. When local communities try to slow their development, they are often met with fierce industry resistance and even lawsuits.
In early May, Hill County, north of Waco, became the first county in the state to pass a moratorium on data center construction. A month later, the county [rescinded](https://substack.com/redirect/68d49a25-2380-4332-b0ee-53e28e0ba526?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its moratorium after a data center developer filed a federal lawsuit, claiming the county "exceeded its lawful powers" in passing the one-year moratorium, which threatened the company's existing contracts to buy more than 800 acres of land for a data center project.
Tucker was early in calling out data centers, but Republicans are now reacting to the data center unpopularity. Republican Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick has made AI regulation a priority for the upcoming legislative cycle. And, after earlier hailing Texas "the epicenter of AI development," Gov. Greg Abbott has reversed course. He recently ordered the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC) and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) to enforce a set of restrictions on data centers, including [requiring](https://substack.com/redirect/7d86ff27-cf09-4a44-a614-3c84ab089684?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) them to "fully fund the costs of electric infrastructure."
"We must prohibit them [data center companies] from building AI data centers in rural Texas neighborhoods," Abbott [said](https://substack.com/redirect/1abfaff7-0b5b-4da2-8f1b-a6e20f1ca1c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at a recent campaign stop in East Texas.
Nate Sheets, the Republican nominee for agriculture commissioner, has echoed the recent concerns made by Texas Republicans.
"We have a responsibility to make sure that growth works for Texans, not against them," he told Barn Raiser. "Texans shouldn't be forced to subsidize private infrastructure projects, and companies need real plans to address electricity demand, water use, and impacts on local communities."
Noting that the office does not regulate zoning, he argued that the best way to help Texas farmers was by improving the rural economy.
"Texas is losing roughly 68 farms every week because the economics of agriculture no longer work for too many families," Sheets said. "When farmers and ranchers can't make a living on the land, they're increasingly forced to sell it for other uses, including data centers."
Come November, the issue will remain contested ground for both parties. There are currently 248 proposed data center projects in Texas and much confusion about their oversight. Recently, when the Public Utility Commission of Texas [requested](https://substack.com/redirect/ede1abdc-4093-4e0d-a2bf-0ff41a9c26fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that data centers report on their water usage to the state, only one-third responded. Texas counties rank among the nation's [most expensive ](https://substack.com/redirect/6c5ddb76-7f23-4c3a-923b-0814f1313c3d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)for electric bills, and the state is poised to overtake Virginia as the nation's [top data center hub](https://substack.com/redirect/51b5c019-3c19-4898-91a1-6a4c82a5a192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by 2030.
"If the Internet were TNT," Tucker wrote in a recent [Houston Chronicle op-ed](https://substack.com/redirect/8922c9c4-582a-41e1-9411-a2d95d09822a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "AI is an atom bomb. One can be useful, but the other can destroy us."
## **Break 'em up**
When it comes to agriculture, Tucker blames monopolies for the woes of Texas farmers and ranchers.
Farmland and ranchland is being lost in Texas at an alarming rate. According to a 2025 Texas A&M Natural Resources Institute [report](https://substack.com/redirect/42c13b16-f5de-4145-a4bc-cbb40c31f3e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), between 2020 and 2025, Texas lost 17,000 agricultural operations, while 3.7 million acres of agricultural "working lands" were transferred to "non-agricultural uses."
A combination of agricultural consolidation and real estate demand from Texas's growing population have put the squeeze on small operations. Big Ag in Texas has used so-called "[right-to-farm](https://substack.com/redirect/dff26ecf-8981-4a45-b317-f66eed8b0718?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" laws to squash local regulation of industrial farms and undercut competition from small operations. For example, in the Panhandle, small cattle ranchers are literally being choked out by "[fecal dust](https://substack.com/redirect/5242cb47-1a9a-429d-b4ae-49d0f82a4b5a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" from the feedlots that have overtaken the area in recent decades. Texas's "right-to-farm" laws protect these big feedlot operations from nuisance claims filed by their neighbors. In recent years, Texas has passed additional laws strengthening Big Ag operators from environmental and nuisance complaints.
According to Tucker, not only has monopolization led to the decline of small and family-owned ranching and farming operations, but free trade policies such as the North American Free Trade Agreement ([NAFTA](https://substack.com/redirect/d861a599-1de6-4d06-a518-0e0a5750593d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) have damaged local supply chains to make Texas dependent on importing its own food.
"Texas used to be a breadbasket... now we're a net importer of food," Tucker told me in a [podcast](https://substack.com/redirect/f285dc48-444c-4ae8-ada9-1c477257c141?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) interview earlier this year. And in South Texas, the consequences of this lopsided system are glaring.
In "the RGV [Rio Grande Valley] mega breadbasket, fantastic soil, fantastic area for growing food, and you have food deserts literally next to farms," he said. This means it is harder for small farming and ranching operations to survive and the cost of food goes up.
## **What the Texas agriculture commissioner does**
The Texas agriculture commissioner has a wide mandate. It is responsible for the promotion, protection, and regulation of Texas' $32 billion [agricultural](https://substack.com/redirect/f5a8eb32-4241-4ba6-9598-cd87738d231b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) industry. On Hightower's watch it also took over management of Texas' organic certification. It is also responsible for rural economic development, managing U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) programs in Texas, and is supposed to protect consumers and workers in the industry. Since former Gov. Rick Perry kicked off the GOP sweep of Texas in 1990, protecting workers and consumers has been [less](https://substack.com/redirect/eba0b3a8-e544-44c2-99f5-c7638f29debb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of a priority.
Beyond these official roles, the Texas agriculture commissioner has traditionally enjoyed a large bully pulpit, something the current agriculture commissioner, Republican Sid Miller, regularly employs, often for his own benefit. While feuding with the Texas legislature over the state budget, Miller spent $91,000 on stickers with his name prominently [placed](https://substack.com/redirect/fbbcc217-3ef1-4895-8201-8750c39052d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on gas pumps across Texas putting the blame on gas prices on Congress and the legislature, and reminding Texans the agriculture commissioner is not responsible for gas prices.
Though a stalwart Republican, Miller has been willing to buck the party line. On June 11, Tucker and Miller [addressed](https://substack.com/redirect/bf418d14-b840-4704-a45f-9b0d4d3850e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a packed room in Matagorda County, where concerned Texans rallied against data centers. The data center issue has people fired up, but the question remains whether it will translate to votes.
Tucker ran unopposed in the Democratic Primary. In his 2020 run for the state senate, he [lost](https://substack.com/redirect/ac1266ec-1b74-45ae-9760-537ba30a281f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by nearly 40 points to a Republican. He is now up against a well-funded Republican opponent, Nate Sheets, who beat out Miller in the Republican primary by an estimated 100,000 votes.
Sheets, owner of the successful national brand Nate's Honey, received the endorsement of Gov. Abbott. His honey business is a major importer of honey from South America.
"Rural Texas won't come back until family farms and ranches make money again," Sheets told Barn Raiser. "That means changing the economics of agriculture so more of every food dollar stays with Texas producers instead of multinational food companies and middlemen."
Sheets also said the concentration of beef processing operations has hurt small ranchers.
"Today a handful of multinational corporations control much of the market, and that's bad for ranchers," he said, adding that as agriculture commissioner, he would "fight to expand Texas-owned meat processing capacity so ranchers have more competitive markets." Like Tucker, he also supports Country of Origin Labeling (COOL).
Sheets is a major [recipient](https://substack.com/redirect/239bc026-9d7e-48fc-8a18-c4f15a406c7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of funding from the Texas Farm Bureau, a major lobbying force behind Big Ag that supports [positions](https://substack.com/redirect/4099cd4c-851d-41c6-8e68-2a17c93e87f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) like "right-to-farm" that have hurt small producers.
Sheets has deep roots in establishment Republican politics. He claims Rick Santorum, the former Senator from Pennsylvania, was who [encouraged](https://substack.com/redirect/7b141a54-8951-4f02-8e6e-65d4a2f4cb46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) him to run for office in 2025. Those connections helped his campaign [amass](https://substack.com/redirect/127c447a-6568-4c84-ba3f-30905b053337?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than $2.4 million compared to [Tucker's](https://substack.com/redirect/f95ba17c-ef2e-4ccf-aad3-c23131ad774e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $225,000.
During the Republican primary, Sheets ran up the numbers in Texas' big cities, while Miller won in rural Texas. The Texas GOP establishment relies on rural voters, but its power players are based in the biggest cities. The limited effect of Trump's endorsement of Miller signals clearly that the Texas GOP establishment wanted Miller out.
Sheets's victory wasn't just his own. It was part of a longstanding feud between Miller and Abbott. Notably, even though Miller won Trump's endorsement, a [host](https://substack.com/redirect/1a2189a1-b5a2-489c-9673-73f8b0c2ee67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Texas industry groups and Texas GOP leaders backed Sheets. Miller had strongly considered a bid to challenge Abbott, and over the years had clashed with the governor, particularly over the governor's 2022 closing of the border with Mexico and his 2020 decision to extend early voting. Sheets's victory was Abbott's final act in a years-long attempt to unseat Miller. And Sheets intends to erase Miller's legacy.
"We're going to fire every one of the cancerous people that were pro-Sid and clean house," Sheets said in a March [interview](https://substack.com/redirect/cd29c57a-d763-41b4-ba4f-08ab19d06e1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with The Texas Tribune.
## **The New World screwworm**
While Sheets has powerful allies and plenty of money, Tucker has an advantage of some blame based on GOP incompetence: the return of the New World screwworm (NWS), a small fly whose larvae burrow like a screw into the open wounds of an animal and consume its living flesh.
On June 3, the USDA confirmed the first U.S. case of NWS since it was [eradicated](https://substack.com/redirect/67aa641a-0599-4482-a139-27a5a49a8b26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the country in the 1970s. USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins has [blamed](https://substack.com/redirect/b167c93f-f208-4b20-bb17-e71476ffb3ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), without evidence, immigrants for bringing in the pest, while Democrats blame DOGE-induced austerity for the outbreak. Elon Musk's DOGE cuts [included](https://substack.com/redirect/73c41a0b-a92d-447f-a70e-eaea71369586?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) program designed to monitor and fight NWS. While the NWS was approaching the state, Secretary Rollins and the USDA downplayed the threat. After Republican state Rep. McLaughlin claimed on June 2 that the NWS was only a mile from the border, Rollins rebuked him.
"When that false information gets out, it causes significant panic," she [said](https://substack.com/redirect/0a65a3c8-7ef0-450d-857e-e34fb0d636df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), claiming the NWS was 25 miles from Texas. In an embarrassing turn, the next day, the USDA [confirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/1c631da1-8860-481e-9b96-9f4199128164?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the first case of screwworm in Texas, in La Pryor, Texas, roughly 50 miles inside the border.
Sheets and Tucker see the solution for the New World screwworm very differently. For the most part, Sheets has backed Brooke Rollins's plan to use sterile flies to decimate the population. This technology was first used to push the screwworm out of Texas. But Tucker argues that this is too slow, with the USDA planning to open its facility in 2027. Tucker has [argued](https://substack.com/redirect/354dc893-051f-4ec5-baf2-461216dfac55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for a multi-pronged approach, specifically using SWASS (Screwworm Adult Suppression System) to eradicate fertile screwworm flies using sterile flies to keep the NWS out once the population has diminished.
"Sterile Insect Technique has a decades-long track record of successfully eradicating New World screwworm," Sheets told Barn Raiser. "SWASS could have a role if conditions change, but deploying it broadly today could also kill the sterile flies we're relying on, along with bees, butterflies, and every other pollinator in the area."
Sheets denied funding cuts have played a role.
"The USDA's sterile fly eradication program, the tool that actually stops screwworm, was never cut. What DOGE cut was a UN [United Nations] monitoring contract that had already failed."
Interestingly enough, Miller [agrees](https://substack.com/redirect/b00a4c05-526d-4324-b9fd-f09194b3bbaa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Tucker and has been pleading with the USDA to use every tool at their disposal. It is very likely that the NWS crisis will only accelerate as the state heads into the midterms, giving Tucker a fresh example of the consequences of GOP mismanagement.
NWS aside, with Republicans beginning to address data center outrage, Tucker will have to connect to other issues of democracy and monopoly power if he wants to win. While regulation of data centers largely lies outside of the purview of the agriculture commissioner, Tucker has an advantage. His political upbringing under Hightower has taught him that the Texas agriculture commissioner can serve as a voice for the forgotten farmers and ranchers. Populist Hightower served them in the 1980s, a century after rural Texans [found](https://substack.com/redirect/3aa3a233-d2a8-46b4-9ff4-38f63248499d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their voice in the Farmers' Alliance in Lampasas, Texas.
But it's a tall task. A Democrat hasn't won statewide office in Texas since 1994, and Tucker's fate will largely be defined by James Talarico at the top of the ticket. Tucker and Talarico can take a page from Ann Richards and Jim Hightower's book. As the pair rose in the 1980s, they campaigned together as part of a progressive slate. Clawing Texas back from GOP rule today will take similar unity.

Under the banner of "government efficiency," he methodically eliminated and undercut investigators who were in the process of probing his various companies and took a chainsaw to government regulators he deemed to be slowing down business. After eliminating surveillance of New World screwworm, the small fly, whose larvae burrow like a screw into the open wounds of animals, came surging back after decades of eradication. After Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy backed off of monitoring Cyclospora cayetanensis , the putrid parasite burst across the country, contaminating produce that produces explosive diarrhea with dire health implications. Along with parasites and larvae, the Trump administration has also encouraged the explosive growth of data centers across the country. All of it has combined to make the public just mad enough that a populist Democrat running for agriculture commissioner in Texas has a surprisingly serious chance of winning. The article below, on the campaign of Clayton Tucker, is part of Drop Site's ongoing collaboration with Barn Raiser Media t with a newsletter running through November. -- Ryan Grim | | ---|---|--- Clayton Tucker campaigns against data centers in Bay City, Texas on June 11, 2026. Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle via Getty Images. Story by David Griscom Texas agriculture commissioner candidate Clayton Tucker is well-versed in populist language. The former Our Revolution organizer has no problem against corporate monopolies like Tyson, Cargill, and John Deere that are rigging the system against the little people. That shouldn't be surprising; the 28-year-old is a longtime admirer and protege of Jim Hightower, the Texas agriculture commissioner from 1983-1991 and the last Democrat to be elected to the position. Tucker is from Lampasas, Texas, the of the Farmers' Alliance and American populism. But is that connection enough to get Tucker, a Democrat, elected Texas's Agricultural Commissioner? Betting big against data centers Tucker has bet big on the backlash to data centers that has engulfed the country. Whether on the trail or on social media, he is quick to raise the concerns of farmers, rural communities, and common Texans who are paying the price for the rollout of these massive warehouses--such as the planned Stargate data center in Abilene, Texas--which serve as the physical infrastructure of the artificial intelligence boom. Many progressives hope this issue will do something that hasn't been done in a generation: attract rural voters to the Democratic ticket. Data centers are wildly unpopular. A recent found that 56% of Texans oppose data centers being built in their community. To Tucker, the data center issue is one of local control. Major corporations like Oracle, Amazon and Meta have been sucking up Texas's scarce water and energy resources at the public expense, receiving than $1 billion in tax breaks each year. When local communities try to slow their development, they are often met with fierce industry resistance and even lawsuits. In early May, Hill County, north of Waco, became the first county in the state to pass a moratorium on data center construction. A month later, the county its moratorium after a data center developer filed a federal lawsuit, claiming the county "exceeded its lawful powers" in passing the one-year moratorium, which threatened the company's existing contracts to buy more than 800 acres of land for a data center project. Tucker was early in calling out data centers, but Republicans are now reacting to the data center unpopularity. Republican Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick has made AI regulation a priority for the upcoming legislative cycle. And, after earlier hailing Texas "the epicenter of AI development," Gov. Greg Abbott has reversed course. He recently ordered the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC) and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) to enforce a set of restrictions on data centers, including them to "fully fund the costs of electric infrastructure." "We must prohibit them [data center companies] from building AI data centers in rural Texas neighborhoods," Abbott at a recent campaign stop in East Texas. Nate Sheets, the Republican nominee for agriculture commissioner, has echoed the recent concerns made by Texas Republicans. "We have a responsibility to make sure that growth works for Texans, not against them," he told Barn Raiser. "Texans shouldn't be forced to subsidize private infrastructure projects, and companies need real plans to address electricity demand, water use, and impacts on local communities." Noting that the office does not regulate zoning, he argued that the best way to help Texas farmers was by improving the rural economy. "Texas is losing roughly 68 farms every week because the economics of agriculture no longer work for too many families," Sheets said. "When farmers and ranchers can't make a living on the land, they're increasingly forced to sell it for other uses, including data centers." Come November, the issue will remain contested ground for both parties. There are currently 248 proposed data center projects in Texas and much confusion about their oversight. Recently, when the Public Utility Commission of Texas that data centers report on their water usage to the state, only one-third responded. Texas counties rank among the nation's electric bills, and the state is poised to overtake Virginia as the nation's by 2030. "If the Internet were TNT," Tucker wrote in a recent , "AI is an atom bomb. One can be useful, but the other can destroy us." Break 'em up When it comes to agriculture, Tucker blames monopolies for the woes of Texas farmers and ranchers. Farmland and ranchland is being lost in Texas at an alarming rate. According to a 2025 Texas A&M Natural Resources Institute , between 2020 and 2025, Texas lost 17,000 agricultural operations, while 3.7 million acres of agricultural "working lands" were transferred to "non-agricultural uses." A combination of agricultural consolidation and real estate demand from Texas's growing population have put the squeeze on small operations. Big Ag in Texas has used so-called "" laws to squash local regulation of industrial farms and undercut competition from small operations. For example, in the Panhandle, small cattle ranchers are literally being choked out by "" from the feedlots that have overtaken the area in recent decades. Texas's "right-to-farm" laws protect these big feedlot operations from nuisance claims filed by their neighbors. In recent years, Texas has passed additional laws strengthening Big Ag operators from environmental and nuisance complaints. According to Tucker, not only has monopolization led to the decline of small and family-owned ranching and farming operations, but free trade policies such as the North American Free Trade Agreement () have damaged local supply chains to make Texas dependent on importing its own food. "Texas used to be a breadbasket... now we're a net importer of food," Tucker told me in a interview earlier this year. And in South Texas, the consequences of this lopsided system are glaring. In "the RGV [Rio Grande Valley] mega breadbasket, fantastic soil, fantastic area for growing food, and you have food deserts literally next to farms," he said. This means it is harder for small farming and ranching operations to survive and the cost of food goes up. What the Texas agriculture commissioner does The Texas agriculture commissioner has a wide mandate. It is responsible for the promotion, protection, and regulation of Texas' $32 billion industry. On Hightower's watch it also took over management of Texas' organic certification. It is also responsible for rural economic development, managing U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) programs in Texas, and is supposed to protect consumers and workers in the industry. Since former Gov. Rick Perry kicked off the GOP sweep of Texas in 1990, protecting workers and consumers has been of a priority. "Rural Texas won't come back until family farms and ranches make money again," Sheets told Barn Raiser. "That means changing the economics of agriculture so more of every food dollar stays with Texas producers instead of multinational food companies and middlemen." Sheets also said the concentration of beef processing operations has hurt small ranchers. "Today a handful of multinational corporations control much of the market, and that's bad for ranchers," he said, adding that as agriculture commissioner, he would "fight to expand Texas-owned meat processing capacity so ranchers have more competitive markets." Friend,
In 250 years of American history, we have never faced a moment quite like this one.
**The Democratic Party is being swallowed whole by an openly socialist, anti-American wing.**
This is not name-calling. Their own platform calls for gutting our military, nationalizing private companies, abolishing cash bail, throwing open the border, and handing voting rights to noncitizens.
Their radicals are beating establishment Democrats in primary after primary. Zohran Mamdani was just the beginning.
_But here is what most Americans still do not understand, and it worries me deeply._
**The Democrats have already rigged the system. And they did it through illegal immigration.**
It works like this. Our Census counts every single resident, citizens and illegal aliens alike, when it hands out House seats and Electoral College votes.
So every illegal alien sitting in a blue state quietly pads that state's power in Washington, D.C.
Elon Musk has been sounding the alarm on this, and he is exactly right. Record illegal immigration has already shifted an estimated 15 to 20 House seats toward the Left.
Now you understand why they fight secure borders and deportations so ferociously.
**That is the entire scheme. Flood the country. Inflate the count. Redraw the maps. Lock in permanent one-party power. **
President Trump fought to base representation on American citizens where it belongs. The courts blocked him at every turn. But the plot is now out in the open for all of us to see.
Which brings me to the SAVE Act, and to my single greatest fear in this fight...
Not enough Americans even know what it is. **One poll found that only 23% could accurately describe it.** That is a catastrophe, because you cannot rally the people to save something they have never had explained to them.
**So let me tell you plainly what this bill does: The SAVE Act bars noncitizens from voting, so that only American citizens ever cast a ballot in an American election. And it requires photo ID to vote.** _**Period.** _
That is the whole fight, in two sentences.
And the American people are with us by margins you almost never see in politics. Nearly 80% want proof of citizenship to register. More than 8 in 10 support voter ID, including most Democrats, most independents, every background and every region. It is 5 to 1.
**Yet every single Democrat is fighting to block it.** _**Every one.** _
I have spent a lifetime in these battles, and I will tell you the hard truth. You never win reform inside Washington, D.C. The lobbyists and the entrenched forces always control the inside game.
Reagan understood this. His job, he said, was to shine a light on the American people so they would turn up the heat on Congress. Tip O'Neill once admitted to me that Reagan's speeches cost him 46 Democrats in a single fight.
**That is exactly how we win this one. Not with insiders. With a grassroots army of patriots like you, moving all at once.**

I am furious. And I refuse to pretend this is normal. | | | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquO38L98SklfBdoDq94y0bmNpGkqxcvbwAwPTl2twJS_DaQ6rO1kJyrioj4TkVwp7fTl3uKhCnUQn_OapHw69ZRFn23sbxSjCvt5i5OF3KtXUVWCA2Wq0aTRUOPl0FGxx_-x-ksV_0xi7okmdx3lk082p9x23p_zOXJqmuo1m2JBuVthn0sr7gdpWILPqUgQe_zzCUALly8tBcax9yix_b2RCs6x5ccQM3SAzL7bxF8EeDzt6kbGYeM9DIZKcHOUzJhrHA958DL1sHW3dgFgBk-sASeijlbzbnKJaAgR4jndOpLe_Z0v0h88LGcomUB5_Ao8gjraJNZPYivQCIW1tbEQnkRSKYrAJcLMM1cXHPOTQ/4sb/YNnMzR4JRpWfxYAQkyVZJA/h0/h001.Z0KEpAJ2W2dilHk2DbWAM36n2lIwg4wP2tPv5nUTkXs)
---
Team,

In the span of one week, ICE agents shot and killed two people.

In Houston, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo -- a 52-year-old man -- was killed by an ICE officer while he was driving his construction crew to a job site. He wasn't even the target of their operation.

In Biddeford, Maine, a 26-year-old father from Colombia -- a man authorized to work in this country -- was shot and killed by an ICE officer. His wife watched from the street. His daughter will grow up without him. He wasn't the target either.

These incidents were not accidents. It is the result of an agency operating without accountability, without oversight, and without consequence. **An agency whose budget tripled over the two decades Doris Matsui has been in Congress, funded again and again directly by her and the establishment in both parties.**

I am furious. And I refuse to pretend this is normal.

Here's a question worth sitting with: in one of the bluest congressional districts in California, why don't we have a representative who will fight for immigrant families and say plainly that ICE must be abolished?

You don't have to guess where I stand. I've put it in writing. I've published a detailed plan to abolish ICE, close for-profit detention centers, end qualified immunity for agents who violate people's rights, and build a real pathway to citizenship. My family are Hmong refugees and Mexican immigrants. This isn't politics to me -- it's my life.

**Now look at my opponent's website. Doris Matsui lists eight issues she cares about. Immigration isn't one of them. After 21 years representing this region -- while ICE terrorizes the very communities she serves -- she won't even put a position in writing.**

That's the difference in this race. So before you do anything else, I'm asking you to read where I stand and see it for yourself:

[**READ MY PLAN TO ABOLISH ICE**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMR1VzI9aiAN61zAaV8H7z9Mfbe7volQ5yWjOiUeaZITzclJqIcXX-7AhYEvv_1j4_jovfnse630M_X70k7-s2RF4X5XXr8-mOVRNF7_-Y-AxkbJiPJiXj9AuqvfQQXZEHBNagNZGKD4MQBPuPnl9WNuEcExybK-FLFkdyc4LsZgJxX0bQUG40gsmol1FGKwf8Qge6hIsuooXlnYQ4GfFt5quaLIKj1nL4Jdc4_6_7yClH0Filgn4vS3tE99clAVrutBMj8BrdcKOLlvzsI7u5XQ/4sb/YNnMzR4JRpWfxYAQkyVZJA/h1/h001.QcClD7fC1prBAqGibxyOhnpMb2hlz8eqzbzvwDV_YjM)
Our neighbors deserve a representative who will say clearly, and without apology, that this has to end. I always will.

With heart and hustle,

Mai | |
---
Mai is the daughter of Hmong refugees, born and raised in Sacramento. Mai’s parents fled war in Laos and arrived in California to find a new life.

As the oldest of 16 children, she helped raise her siblings while working hard to build a career dedicated to helping her community thrive. Mai is a proud product of public schools and was the first in her family to attend college. As a young organizer, Mai returned home to serve the community that raised and supported her.

| | **_Meet Rob:_** Born and raised in Kingston, PA, Rob Bresnahan is currently serving his first term as PA-08’s homegrown Congressman. He’s a fifth-generation Northeastern Pennsylvanian, and the only representative in Congress who is part of the National Electrical Contractors Association. A product of the American Dream, Rob learned the true meaning of hard work by getting his hands dirty early and often. He wired junction boxes, ran heavy equipment, drove trucks, and learned the value of an honest day’s work in the process. His family instilled the values of hard work, discipline, and perseverance in him at a young age – and Rob has stayed true to these foundational values all his life. At just 19 years old, Rob joined his family’s business as the CFO for Kuharchik Construction. He became the CEO of the company in 2013. Rob spent over a decade working and connecting with blue-collar Americans across the country before running for Congress in 2024. He was outspent 2:1 in his race against a 12-year Democrat that year, but the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania demanded change when they sent Rob to be their fighter in Washington. Through his experience as an electrical contractor, Rob saw the real world struggles facing America’s blue-collar workers first hand. Wages are not keeping up with the skyrocketing cost of living, and Americans who wake up every day and pay their dues are being left out to dry by their elected officials. But Rob’s voting record in Congress tells a different story. He’s stood up for hardworking Americans at every opportunity, regardless of partisan politics. Simply put, Rob Bresnahan brings both insight and candid concern for blue-collar America to Congress that your run-of-the-mill representatives don’t. Every day that he steps foot on Capitol Hill, Rob is 100% devoted to restoring America’s energy independence, deregulating the economy, and bringing well-paying jobs back to the great commonwealth of Pennsylvania. While he’s still serving his freshman term in Congress, Rob has already introduced key legislation to re-invest in American trades and pave avenues to success for young people who forgo a traditional college education. Now running for re-election in one of the most pivotal battleground races in the country, Rob is stepping up to the plate once again to deliver for the people of PA-08 and preserve our Republican House majority for the remainder of President Trump’s second term.

body:
We need to respond.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41508%2E3422442%2Eua4ZUI)
There have been six polls in the six months since I launched this campaign for Alaska’s U.S. Senate seat. We were leading in the first five.
Then, after my opponent and the billionaires and super PACs that back him started spending millions on attack ads against me, **the New York Times/Siena University poll released this month shows us down two points.**
[](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260714_1_ak.X9fenv&refcode=em20260714-41508&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41508%2E3422442%2Eua4ZUI)
We need your help to respond.
Election forecasters like Cook Political Report, Sabato’s Crystal Ball, Split Ticket, and VoteHub have all called Alaska’s U.S. Senate race a toss-up.
They shifted the race in our favor because they know we can win, and that all eyes are on Alaska this year in what’s shaping up to be the most competitive and consequential race on the Senate map.
They know we can win because my opponent, Dan Sullivan, is the least popular senator up for reelection, and Alaskans want someone who will fight for their healthcare, jobs, disaster relief, and public media – not gut them.
**They know we can win this toss-up Senate race if we can raise the resources needed to overcome the attack ads and get our message out.**
We’re criss-crossing as much of Alaska’s 586,000 square miles as we can to bring every village and every voter into our campaign, and we’re doing all we can to fight back with ads online and on the airwaves.
But this is without a doubt the most expensive state on the map to run a Senate campaign. To win in Alaska means building a strong ground game and winning the screen war.
No one ever said flipping Alaska’s Senate seat was going to be easy. But we do know that this is our best chance to do it.
**I know we can pull this off, and here’s why:** If everyone getting this email split a donation between Truth to Power PAC and my campaign, we’d have enough to match the tens of millions in outside spending from the billionaire-backed super PACs propping up my unpopular opponent.
[Split a donation today](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260714_1_ak.X9fenv&refcode=em20260714-41508&t=3&akid=41508%2E3422442%2Eua4ZUI)
That’s the power of a grassroots movement. We can win this when we all chip in together.
Let’s go win.
\- Mary

# BREAKING: DHS changes tactics for ICE after two fatal shootings
_**Julio Rosas**_

---|---|---
It has been reported that the Department of Homeland Security has ordered U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to pause operations on vehicles driven by illegal immigrants following two fatal shootings in less than a week.
The first fatal shooting was in Houston, Texas, where DHS says an illegal immigrant who had been in the U.S. for 35 years, but was not the main target, refused to pull over and attempted to run over an agent. No agent was wearing a body camera and there is no clear video showing the moment the shooting occurred. The witnesses in the work van say an ICE agent fired through a side window, not from the front.
The second fatal shooting took place in Biddeford, Maine, where again DHS says an illegal immigrant, who had a permit to work and a Social Security number, did not stop his vehicle after agents tried to pull him over.
"The vehicle attempted to flee the scene and, fearing for public safety, an officer discharged his weapon," DHS said. Like in Houston, no agent at the scene in Biddeford had a body camera.
The outrage and backlash from Democrats has been severe. Calls for ICE to be straight up abolished, not simply defunded, have increased from the Left.
DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin had previously stated his goal is to keep the agency out of national headlines, hoping to increase arrests without causing too much noise and fodder for far-leftists. The recent shootings, along with the riots outside Delaney Hall in May, have obliterated that goal.
The new policy on not carrying out vehicle stops is temporary and does not apply to illegal aliens who have serious criminal records.

body:
Help us raise $100,000 in order to keep supporting the next generation of progressive leaders.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260714-2&t=1&akid=3722%2E587540%2Eka6Cjc)
Peter,
I'm reaching out because we have an important fundraising deadline coming up.
**[By midnight on July 15, we need to raise $100,000 to keep building the movement that's electing the next generation of progressive leaders.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260714_2_mm.sPn0tS&refcode=em20260714-3722&amount=5&t=2&akid=3722%2E587540%2Eka6Cjc)**
Here's why this matters.
Leaders We Deserve is endorsing **more candidates than ever before.**
That means we're investing in more young leaders, reaching more voters, and helping more campaigns compete in races that will shape the future of our country.
**But our work is far from over.**
There are still young, progressive candidates across the country who need the resources to knock on doors, reach voters, and build the kind of grassroots campaigns that can win.
That's only possible because of _people like you_.
Unlike the political establishment, we're not relying on billionaire donors or corporate PACs to fuel this work. We're building something different -- a movement powered by people who believe our generation deserves a seat at the table.
If we're going to continue expanding our impact, we need to hit our **$100,000 fundraising goal before midnight on July 15.**
**[Will you chip in $5 today to help us elect the next generation of leaders?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260714_2_mm.sPn0tS&refcode=em20260714-3722&amount=5&t=3&akid=3722%2E587540%2Eka6Cjc)**

The future won't build itself -- but together, we can help elect the leaders who will.
Thank you,
David Hogg

### The Executive Order is the largest shrinkage of protected public lands in US History and opened up some of Utah's most beloved lands to mining.

Yesterday, surrounded by every member of Utah's federal delegation (Rep. Blake Moore, Rep. Celeste Maloy, Rep. Mike Kennedy, Sen. John Curtis, Sen. Mike Lee, Rep Burgess Owens,), Governor Cox, Speaker of the House Mike Schultz and Secretary of the Interior, the president signed two proclamations cutting Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante national monuments by almost three million acres. Bears Ears goes from 1.36 million acres to about 121,000. Grand Staircase goes from 1.87 million to about 181,500. Less than 300,000 acres of protection is left between them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5708e951-f158-494e-8547-0420fd5d7032?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That is the largest shrinkage of protected public land in American history. It is bigger than what he did in 2017, and that was the record.
Trump stood in front of the cameras and said this: you can't do anything, you can't go hunting, fishing, you can't walk on it, we're remedying that today. That is a lie. And it is not a gray area or a difference of opinion. It is a lie you can check yourself in about five minutes.
Here is Clinton's 1996 proclamation creating Grand Staircase-Escalante:
> _Nothing in this proclamation shall be deemed to diminish the responsibility and authority of the State of Utah for management of fish and wildlife, including regulation of hunting and fishing, on Federal lands within the monument._
Hunting and fishing stayed under Utah's control the entire time. Grazing permits kept running. The document says so.
Here is Obama's 2016 proclamation creating Bears Ears, describing what the land offers:
> _world class outdoor recreation opportunities, including rock climbing, hunting, hiking, backpacking, canyoneering, whitewater rafting, mountain biking, and horseback riding_
Hunting is listed by name. So is climbing. So is mountain biking. These are the documents they tore up today, and the activities they claim to be restoring are written into them.
I have adventured on this land for twenty years. Nobody ever stopped me. Nobody ever stopped anyone.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6cd794a9-b861-458a-b27b-071cdac68d58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Caroline Gleich ⛰️ is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..ytVNVErSxlLjZWB1GTAc_Y6Yt6N32gvqHTwINulfMc4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=207085510)
So what did monument status actually block?
New mining claims. New oil and gas leases. New coal and geothermal leases. That is the list. The legal language in every one of these proclamations withdraws the land from "entry, location, selection, sale, or other disposition under the public land laws," from "location, entry, and patent under the mining laws," and from "disposition under all laws relating to mineral and geothermal leasing."
This order does not give the land to Utah. The land stays federal, under the BLM. The only thing that changed is that a mining company can stake a claim on it again, and the federal government can lease it out.
So this was never about your hiking boots. It is about uranium under Bears Ears and coal under the Kaiparowits Plateau in Grand Staircase. It is about who gets to own what is underneath. After Trump cut these monuments in 2017, new mining claims went up on ground removed from Grand Staircase, and the BLM's preferred plan would have opened more than 550,000 acres to mineral leasing. In 60 days, the land will open up for mining.
Inside the original boundaries of the monuments are nearly 100,000 archaeological and cultural sites at Bears Ears. Cliff dwellings, petroglyphs, burial grounds, and ceremonial sites still in use today.
Bears Ears was the first national monument in American history created at the request of a coalition of tribal nations. The Hopi Tribe, the Navajo Nation, the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe, the Zuni Tribe, and the Ute Indian Tribe of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation spent years building the case. In 2021 they signed a first of its kind agreement to co-manage the land with the federal government, and they spent nearly three years writing the management plan.
Today all of that was thrown out, and not one of those nations was consulted before it happened. They found out the same way you did.
In Trump's proclamation shrinking the monuments, they claim petroglyphs and pictographs are common across the West and did not warrant a monument. Then they carve out 693 acres to protect a vertical oil well drilled in 1926. A cowboy line cabin made the cut too. So a wildcat oil well from 1926 is a treasure worth saving, and thousand year old rock art is not. That is in their document.
Grand Staircase is one of the great paleontology labs on the planet. Nearly two dozen new dinosaur species have been named there since the monument was created, along with at least 660 species of native bees. Over 150 scientists signed a letter this year asking that it be left alone. Paleontologists will tell you we have barely started digging.
You cannot un-mine a mesa. You cannot un-loot a grave. There is no version of this where we get it back.
They say this what Utahns want, which is another lie. Seventy-one percent of Utah voters want to keep Bears Ears. Seventy-four percent want to keep Grand Staircase. Eighty-nine percent say tribal nations should have a strong role managing their ancestral lands. Sixty-five percent of Utah Republicans support keeping monuments at their current size and number.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/946fffa5-e5ee-4962-a727-14277ee975b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
John Curtis said today that Utahns manage this land better than people two thousand miles away. I want to believe that. But I live in a state with the largest open pit mine on earth and a drying Great Salt Lake that now blows arsenic dust into the lungs of two and a half million people. That is our management record. Saying otherwise does not make it true.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/30e28f9f-dda7-458d-9e50-aa8d94b687c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This spring, Mike Lee tried to gut Grand Staircase's management plan through Congress. About 600,000 calls and emails came in against it and he lost. So he went to the president instead, with no tribal consultation and no public comment period.
They did it this way because they knew they could not win the honest way. It also tells you that pressure works, because it already did once. The land opens to new mining claims and mineral leasing 60 days from signing, which is around September 11. That is the clock we are working against. You can't hike, run, camp, drive or explore on an active mining claim. Every lie they say is a projection.
The Antiquities Act lets a president create a monument. It says nothing about letting him take one apart. Congress kept that power. Tribes sued over this in 2017 and they will sue again.
Where do we go from here:
Support the groups doing the work (among others).
* [Native American Rights Fund](https://substack.com/redirect/2f6f88f7-25aa-4b3c-840d-fa7632d436d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* [Bears Ears Inter-Tribal Coalition](https://substack.com/redirect/bcf462c9-ba70-4e32-b04d-6d84551b8f55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* [Grand Canyon Trust](https://substack.com/redirect/868924be-121a-42cb-80d7-85366024aff6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Call your representative. [Link to other actions here.](https://substack.com/redirect/faa4a3cb-0a65-49e1-a290-f868ab3b78fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Share this with someone who loves our public lands.
In 2017, nearly three million Americans rose up when this happened. We won that fight in the end. We can win this one.

Blake Moore, Rep. Celeste Maloy, Rep. Mike Kennedy, Sen. John Curtis, Sen. Mike Lee, Rep Burgess Owens,), Governor Cox, Speaker of the House Mike Schultz and Secretary of the Interior, the president signed two proclamations cutting Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante national monuments by almost three million acres. Bears Ears goes from 1.36 million acres to about 121,000. Grand Staircase goes from 1.87 million to about 181,500. Less than 300,000 acres of protection is left between them. | | ---|---|--- That is the largest shrinkage of protected public land in American history. It is bigger than what he did in 2017, and that was the record. Trump stood in front of the cameras and said this: you can't do anything, you can't go hunting, fishing, you can't walk on it, we're remedying that today. That is a lie. And it is not a gray area or a difference of opinion. It is a lie you can check yourself in about five minutes. Here is Clinton's 1996 proclamation creating Grand Staircase-Escalante: Nothing in this proclamation shall be deemed to diminish the responsibility and authority of the State of Utah for management of fish and wildlife, including regulation of hunting and fishing, on Federal lands within the monument. Hunting and fishing stayed under Utah's control the entire time. Grazing permits kept running. The document says so. Here is Obama's 2016 proclamation creating Bears Ears, describing what the land offers: world class outdoor recreation opportunities, including rock climbing, hunting, hiking, backpacking, canyoneering, whitewater rafting, mountain biking, and horseback riding Hunting is listed by name. So is climbing. So is mountain biking. These are the documents they tore up today, and the activities they claim to be restoring are written into them. I have adventured on this land for twenty years. Nobody ever stopped me. Nobody ever stopped anyone. | | ---|---|--- Caroline Gleich ⛰️ is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. So what did monument status actually block? New mining claims. New oil and gas leases. New coal and geothermal leases. That is the list. The legal language in every one of these proclamations withdraws the land from "entry, location, selection, sale, or other disposition under the public land laws," from "location, entry, and patent under the mining laws," and from "disposition under all laws relating to mineral and geothermal leasing." This order does not give the land to Utah. The land stays federal, under the BLM. The only thing that changed is that a mining company can stake a claim on it again, and the federal government can lease it out. So this was never about your hiking boots. It is about uranium under Bears Ears and coal under the Kaiparowits Plateau in Grand Staircase. It is about who gets to own what is underneath. After Trump cut these monuments in 2017, new mining claims went up on ground removed from Grand Staircase, and the BLM's preferred plan would have opened more than 550,000 acres to mineral leasing. In 60 days, the land will open up for mining. Inside the original boundaries of the monuments are nearly 100,000 archaeological and cultural sites at Bears Ears. Cliff dwellings, petroglyphs, burial grounds, and ceremonial sites still in use today. Bears Ears was the first national monument in American history created at the request of a coalition of tribal nations. The Hopi Tribe, the Navajo Nation, the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe, the Zuni Tribe, and the Ute Indian Tribe of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation spent years building the case. In 2021 they signed a first of its kind agreement to co-manage the land with the federal government, and they spent nearly three years writing the management plan. Then they carve out 693 acres to protect a vertical oil well drilled in 1926. A cowboy line cabin made the cut too. So a wildcat oil well from 1926 is a treasure worth saving, and thousand year old rock art is not. That is in their document. Grand Staircase is one of the great paleontology labs on the planet. Nearly two dozen new dinosaur species have been named there since the monument was created, along with at least 660 species of native bees. Over 150 scientists signed a letter this year asking that it be left alone. Paleontologists will tell you we have barely started digging. You cannot un-mine a mesa. You cannot un-loot a grave. There is no version of this where we get it back. They say this what Utahns want, which is another lie. Seventy-one percent of Utah voters want to keep Bears Ears. Patriot,

It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners.

But even with the pardons, you may not realize what life is like for many J6ers...

**Some are homeless to this day. Some can 't get a job because of the time they've spent in jail. Many are struggling to return to some semblance of a normal life.**

They have been separated from their families for years. They have had their rights stripped from them. They can't vote. They can't own a firearm.

Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions.

_And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. _

So what comes next for J6ers?

There are nearly 1,600 Americans who need to rebuild their lives. That's exactly what Stand in the Gap Foundation is helping them do.

[Patriot, as a personal favor to me, can you please send an urgent donation of $10 or more? Stand in the Gap Foundation originally started to help reunite families with a loved one incarcerated due to J6. Now, our focus is on helping those J6ers navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated.

We are committed to providing comprehensive, practical support to ensure that each individual can rebuild their life with dignity, hope, and purpose.

Our mission is deeply rooted in the conviction that legal forgiveness is only the beginning. We want to give J6ers the support to fully reintegrate into their communities with the strength to start anew.

clean_body: It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners. Patriot, It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners. But even with the pardons, you may not realize what life is like for many J6ers... Some are homeless to this day. Some can 't get a job because of the time they've spent in jail. Many are struggling to return to some semblance of a normal life. They have been separated from their families for years. They have had their rights stripped from them. They can't vote. They can't own a firearm. Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions. And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. So what comes next for J6ers? There are nearly 1,600 Americans who need to rebuild their lives. That's exactly what Stand in the Gap Foundation is helping them do. Stand in the Gap Foundation originally started to help reunite families with a loved one incarcerated due to J6. Now, our focus is on helping those J6ers navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated. We are committed to providing comprehensive, practical support to ensure that each individual can rebuild their life with dignity, hope, and purpose. Our mission is deeply rooted in the conviction that legal forgiveness is only the beginning. We want to give J6ers the support to fully reintegrate into their communities with the strength to start anew. Surprisingly, there are very few resources for people who are released from prison, particularly if they are conservative or America First activists. While some J6ers come from families with means, most do not. We were founded to "stand in the gap" for those in prison and those navigating life after incarceration. null, it’s Haley Stevens. Did you catch Gary Peters and me on _Morning Joe_ this morning?

[](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/24365?t=3&akid=3526%2E49239%2E4W6opx) If so, you already know the big news: **Michigan Senator Gary Peters just endorsed me as his replacement in the Senate.**_[
](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/24365?t=4&akid=3526%2E49239%2E4W6opx)_
I am incredibly honored to have Gary's trust and confidence. If you missed us on _Morning Joe_ this morning, here’s the summary:
1️⃣ Gary Peters stepped off the sidelines to endorse me for U.S. Senate because Democrats cannot afford to lose this seat. And he knows that I am the strongest Democrat to defeat Mike Rogers in November. Poll after poll after poll shows it. And he knows that I’m one heck of a fighter.

2️⃣ Here’s what Sen. Peters had to say: “I worked with [Haley] back when I first got elected to Congress, during the auto rescue, when she worked closely with President Obama to make sure that we could save jobs and save the auto industry in Michigan. She is a workhorse. She gets things done."

3️⃣ He knows exactly why I’m in this race: to fight for working Michiganders. That means reducing the cost of living – from the grocery store to the gas pump. That means standing up to Trump’s dangerous abuses of power that have been hurting Michigan families for too long. That means investing in Michigan jobs so that our workers can support their families.
**
**I’m grateful that my friend and my senator, Gary Peters, endorsed me, and I am ready to step up and build on his legacy. **Right now, we’re quickly approaching our final pre-primary FEC deadline. We must reach our $250,000 goal if we want to stay competitive in this race.** With Senate control on the line, we can’t take any chances. We need to win the Democratic nomination, and we need to win in November.
I’m asking for the strength of this grassroots team to step up and help build on this momentum: **_[Will you pitch in $5 or $10 to help me hit my $250,000 pre-primary FEC goal before midnight tomorrow, fight back against Rogers’ MAGA megadonors, and flip the Senate?](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/24365?t=5&akid=3526%2E49239%2E4W6opx)_**
Together,
Haley
|
* * *

Now, I’m running for Michigan’s open Senate seat to continue fighting for the people and communities I love. The path to the Senate majority runs right through Michigan, which means this race is shaping up to be the most competitive and expensive in the entire country. The GOP is already coming after me as a top target for defeat, so I’m counting on your grassroots support to fight back and win. _“Hi folks, Andy Beshear here. I believe we can flip the governor’s office in Iowa – but only with your help. Please read my friend Rob’s message and get involved in his race if you can:_ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135281772/633702668/1380622239?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_FR_Sand_260714_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZGQyNjBlYmUtZDc3Zi1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=fYn-v8K9GO4i65Oen3pK3I8PeZxujkvkyxtLuf6NIWM=) Politicians famously lie a lot, Peter.

Now I love a good practical joke here and there, but I don’t lie. That’s one of the many reasons I consider myself a public servant, NOT a politician.

Folks, you know I like to call it like I see it. So I want to let you know the truth of how I’m feeling about chances in the toss-up race for Governor of Iowa.

**Hang on before I start yapping:** I just got my official opponent, and get this: he’s a Kansan culture warrior backed by _Steve King._

**Game on.**

Now that we’re up against Zach Lahn and the partisan machine behind him, [_**will you rush a donation between my campaign and Andy Beshear's In This Together PAC to help us maximize the post-primary energy here in Iowa? Every bit counts in a race THIS competitive.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135281773/633702669/1380622239?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_FR_Sand_260714_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZGQyNjBlYmUtZDc3Zi1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=fYn-v8K9GO4i65Oen3pK3I8PeZxujkvkyxtLuf6NIWM=) [SPLIT A DONATION](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135281774/633702670/1380622239?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_FR_Sand_260714_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZGQyNjBlYmUtZDc3Zi1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=fYn-v8K9GO4i65Oen3pK3I8PeZxujkvkyxtLuf6NIWM=)
Honestly, the primary results didn’t change my feelings much at all. **My gut and recent polling tell me we have a slight lead, but this governor’s race will probably come down to no more than 10,000 votes.**

I don’t want you to think I’m not confident in our chances. I’m extremely confident, in fact: experts have this race pinned as a toss-up, we have a big tent filled with Iowans from literally every walk of life, we have a provably persuasive message, we’re running several TV ads with great feedback from voters, the list goes on and on.

Even with all that going right for us, **this race is _still_ a dead heat.**

My team and I are aware of the potential pitfalls ahead of us. This is a wide-open race in a midterm (i.e. lower-turnout) year. Lahn has the full resources of the Republican party machine at his disposal. I don’t take corporate PAC cash; he does.

**I won re-election in 2022 by just a shade under 3,000 votes. I know we’ll have to work HARDER, raise MORE, and spend SMARTER than Zach Lahn just to pull off a narrow win.**

_That’s the honest truth._

With that said, we have a lot of work to do to win the race that’ll shape the next several years (and likely decades) of Iowa’s future. # [The worst thing to say at a BBQ in Michigan](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=207043925&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA3MDQzOTI1LCJpYXQiOjE3ODQwNzAxNjksImV4cCI6MTc4NjY2MjE2OSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.RRMPduXEHWqsB8torSHckgcqq0tMbHioo2Y-NuovF6k)
### FEC deadlines are boring conversation, but they really matter
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Jul 14
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/the-worst-thing-to-say-at-a-bbq-in?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA3MDQzOTI1LCJpYXQiOjE3ODQwNzAxNjksImV4cCI6MTc4NjY2MjE2OSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.RRMPduXEHWqsB8torSHckgcqq0tMbHioo2Y-NuovF6k&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/the-worst-thing-to-say-at-a-bbq-in?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Friends,
Here's a life tip! This is a foolproof way to bring conversation at a backyard BBQ to a screeching halt: stand up, shush the crowd, and say, "Hey everybody, can we please stop grilling and playing cornhole for a second so I can talk about the upcoming pre-primary Federal Election Commission deadline?"
You'll get stunned looks every time. Someone may spontaneously fall asleep.
Look, I know FEC deadlines aren't the most exciting thing in the world. But they REALLY matter for grassroots campaigns like ours - and midnight on July 15 is the biggest deadline of this entire campaign. It's also why I'm going to ask you to **[chip in $20 in a second.](https://substack.com/redirect/16d2103f-92a4-40d0-9823-ab642937ac07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
OK, so here's the FEC rule in plain English: Before every election, campaigns have to file one last public report, and it has to capture everything up to 20 days before Election Day. For us, that report covers July 1 through July 15.
So in that window (right NOW), we need to show the world exactly how strong this campaign is.
And everyone will be looking. Tons of media outlets. National Republicans. The MAGA megadonors deciding how many millions more to dump into Michigan. **They 'll all open that report and see whether this people-powered campaign has the fuel to finish the primary strong and win the general.**
Friends, there's no next primary FEC deadline after this one. The numbers EVERYBODY sees before the primary get locked in on July 15 - while ballots are already filled out at kitchen tables across Michigan and going back in the mail right now.
This is the last public test of strength before the August 4 primary. It's now or never.
I won't sugarcoat it: I'm not rich. I'm the only non-millionaire in this race, so I can't self-fund. I don't have a wealthy father-in-law. Mike Rogers has billionaires backing him. The Koch network is spending big. National Republicans are even meddling in our primary to prop up my opponent because they'd rather face him in November than face me.
But here's what we've got: thousands of hardworking folks - teachers, retirees, union workers, small-business owners - who chip in what they can because they believe Michigan deserves a senator who actually understands them and will fight for them.
That's what wins races in Michigan. Not flashy internet stars. Not likes on social media. It's working people who look at me and this movement and say, "Yeah, that lady seems like she actually cares about me. She gives a damn about Michiganders."
And I do! This whole campaign is a love letter to Michigan. Now I need your help to write the next paragraph.
So here's my direct ask, with the FEC deadline coming up: **[will you chip in $20 before midnight on July 15 to make sure this last report shows exactly what we 're made of? Let's show the strength of this campaign and keep Michigan blue. Together.](https://substack.com/redirect/8d9f6131-d201-46cc-9303-5ac1c728565e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CHIP IN](https://substack.com/redirect/8d9f6131-d201-46cc-9303-5ac1c728565e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And I promise, next time I'll have better conversation starters for your backyard BBQ than the financial nuances of the Federal Election Commission deadlines. Until then, here's the real tip: bring loads of Koegel's brats. You can never have enough. Everybody will want a couple.
With gratitude,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/16d2103f-92a4-40d0-9823-ab642937ac07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

body:
We have three weeks until the Missouri primary — and the choice couldn't be clearer.
#
Peter,

Friends,
This past week, I had the opportunity to get out across the district, attend local events, and visit organizations that are doing extraordinary work, often picking up where government has failed to deliver. I had the opportunity to tour Jawonio this week and see firsthand the incredible work they are doing caring for thousands of people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, behavioral health challenges, and chronic medical needs across Rockland and Westchester.
But I also learned how much harder this administration is making their work. Medicaid cuts, SNAP reductions, staffing shortages, and now 7% of their workforce under TPS and at risk of deportation. These are contributing members of our community, here legally, caring for our most vulnerable neighbors. We owe it to them to do right by them — protecting Medicaid and SNAP, ending TPS revocations, and fixing our broken immigration system so people here legally are not waiting a decade for citizenship. That is what this country is supposed to stand for. I also had the privilege of attending the Women's Distance Festival in support of Center for Safety & Change. It was one of the most inspiring mornings I've had on this campaign. Seeing so many people come together to support women in our community during their hardest moments was a powerful reminder of the strength and compassion that define the Hudson Valley.
The most meaningful part of this campaign is getting out across this district and hearing directly from you. Every conversation I have shapes how I think about this fight and what I will fight for in Congress. At the end of the day, I'm in this race because of you, and I mean that.
With gratitude and fire, **Cait Conley**

clean_body: | | | | Friends, This past week, I had the opportunity to get out across the district, attend local events, and visit organizations that are doing extraordinary work, often picking up where government has failed to deliver. I had the opportunity to tour Jawonio this week and see firsthand the incredible work they are doing caring for thousands of people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, behavioral health challenges, and chronic medical needs across Rockland and Westchester. But I also learned how much harder this administration is making their work. Medicaid cuts, SNAP reductions, staffing shortages, and now 7% of their workforce under TPS and at risk of deportation. These are contributing members of our community, here legally, caring for our most vulnerable neighbors. We owe it to them to do right by them — protecting Medicaid and SNAP, ending TPS revocations, and fixing our broken immigration system so people here legally are not waiting a decade for citizenship. That is what this country is supposed to stand for. I also had the privilege of attending the Women's Distance Festival in support of Center for Safety & Change. It was one of the most inspiring mornings I've had on this campaign. Seeing so many people come together to support women in our community during their hardest moments was a powerful reminder of the strength and compassion that define the Hudson Valley. The most meaningful part of this campaign is getting out across this district and hearing directly from you. Every conversation I have shapes how I think about this fight and what I will fight for in Congress. At the end of the day, I'm in this race because of you, and I mean that. name: Alex Vindman
subject: The Iran War
body:
# [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1317?t=1&akid=886%2E3892029%2EHwsISc)

Yesterday, Donald Trump formally notified Congress that the United States is at war with Iran — propelling our country back into another Forever War.
The Senate has the responsibility to be a check on this administration.
Donald Trump started this conflict months ago. And instead of conducting oversight, the Senate abdicated their responsibility and failed to pass a War Powers Resolution.
The Republicans and my opponent, Ashley Moody, voted to give Trump unchecked power. They own this failure.
Now that America is once again drawn into a war of choice, Congress must debate and vote on whether to continue Trump’s war. They must choose to put our families first.
Will they? I would not hold my breath.
I won’t hold my breath for Ashley Moody to do the right thing. She is a Florida Last Senator who is prioritizing pleasing the president ahead of the people of our state.
I’m a hell no on forever wars — I’m a 21-year combat veteran who was wounded in Iraq. I’ll fight to end the chaos, cruelty, and corruption, and battle to lower costs crushing Floridians. I'm in this race to fight for you.
The people of Florida deserve better.
No one wants unchecked power, and no one wants forever wars. There are huge numbers of Independents and Republicans in Florida who agree. That is why we are going to win this race.
Alex Vindman

**Alex Vindman is running in one of the most competitive and expensive Senate elections of the cycle.**
This is the Patriot vs. the Politician, and Alex’s history of putting Country First gives him a real chance to win this race. But he can’t do it alone. There is only one way to win this Senate race in Florida, and that is if we all do our part to help whenever we can.
Alex’s final FEC fundraising deadline before the primary is coming up fast. When it ends, we’re legally required to report what we’ve raised. Everyone will be looking. So we are asking for your help — today.

body:
https://elfrethformaryland.com/ [https://elfrethformaryland.com/]
Friend,

A reporter asked President Trump how much the financial strain on everyday Americans impacts his international negotiations. [https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/watch-i-dont-think-about-americans-financial-situation-when-negotiating-with-iran-trump-says] His response was incredibly blunt. He said, "Not even a little bit. I don't think about Americans' financial situation."

Honestly, that admission is a stark reminder of how disconnected national leaders can become from the people they are supposed to represent. Right now, families across Maryland are feeling the very real squeeze of grocery bills, high energy costs, and high prices at the gas pump – I feel it too. Economic pressure isn't some issue you can just brush off. It’s about putting food on the table and not staying up at night worrying.

While the President remains out of touch from the reality on the ground, that’s not how I was raised. Growing up in a working-class, union household, I look at public service through an entirely different lens. My focus is always on your bottom line. It is why I will always fight for practical pocketbook issues like lowering health care costs, expanding access to quality education, and supporting our small businesses.

This focus even extends to our work in the district to make sure the government is working on your behalf. We have successfully helped over 2,300 of our neighbors in the Third District with issues they are facing with a federal agency. We help cut through bureaucratic red tape and, to date, have returned $3.2 million directly back to the pockets of constituents. If you think we can be of assistance, you can always call our office at (410) 832-8890.

You deserve leaders who wake up every morning thinking about your financial security. We are building a campaign that puts the economic well-being of Maryland families first. If you are ready for leadership that actually fights for your family to get ahead, I hope you will join us today.

Can you chip in $15 today to invest in a campaign that takes affordability seriously? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-July2026-FR-TrumpAfford?&refcode=E30813-20260714-TrumpAfford-SL-Trump&amount=15]

Best,

Sarah Elfreth

Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises.
